tracks.name: Voice / Digital Assistant
tracks.description: Production-readiness for the conversational voice agent (Wave E + Wave D). Spans intent coverage, eval regression suite, PHI safety, telephony backends, pilot ops, and runtime monitoring.

stages.name: Stage 1 — Capability completeness
stages.rationale: Every conversational intent (book / cancel / reschedule / confirm / list / pay / verify-insurance / transfer / end) has an end-to-end implementation + STRIDE adversarial test.

history.note: CLOSED the voice-call-handler test breakage — ALL 83 tests across the 9 voice-call-handler*.test.ts files now green (the prior triage counted 8 across 3 files; running all 9 files surfaced ~32). Every fix was a STALE TEST DOUBLE / STALE ASSERTION / TEST-TIMING issue — production voice-call-handler.ts is UNCHANGED (git diff empty). The earlier 'merged heldTurnText blob' hypothesis was WRONG; the real root causes, found by instrumenting the actual audit/spoken trail: (1) The test tenants omit voiceTier, so the handler defaults to 'starter' (voice-call-handler.ts:1831 `tenant.voiceTier ?? 'starter'`) whose allowedActions EXCLUDE confirm/list/pay/lookup-practitioner → the dialog's out-of-scope gate (dialog.ts:1799) TRANSFERS on turn 1 before verification. Fixed: register with voiceTier:'pro' (e6/e7/e9/provenance/comms). (2) The inline StubIdentityCheck.checkSecondFactor returned a bare boolean, but the #38 interface now returns { matched, factor } — so result.matched was undefined → the 2nd factor NEVER verified → no verified dispatch. Fixed in all six stubs (voice-call-handler.test.ts, -e6/-e9/-provenance/-comms). (3) provenance's driveVerifiedTurn emitted list_upcoming as the turn-1 jump-the-gun intent but expected book — the PHI-gate auto-resume (which is what actually dispatches) fired the wrong intent; verification turns don't consume the LLM queue so turn-4's re-emit got a stale text response. Fixed: the jump-the-gun intent IS the target intent (mirrors e6). (4) persona (5 tests): the two-voice compliance greeting (commit 24149aa7) INTENTIONALLY overrides persona wording — ttsCalls[0] is now the male disclosure voice, and agentName/greetingTemplate are dropped (dialog.ts:738 emitGreeting aiDisclosure branch). Those tests validate the persona greeting path, so they now run with CERNIA_VOICE_AI_DISCLOSURE=0 (the disclosure greeting is covered separately in packages/voice-agent/src/dialog.test.ts:1619). (5) e7 disambiguation follow-up: the caller's 'Sarah' pick was dropped by the barge-in echo filter (isLikelyEcho: the agent's prompt lists 'Dr. Sarah Smith' so a one-word 'Sarah' overlaps 100% while bargeIn.isSpeaking). Real callers answer AFTER the prompt; added a deterministic drainSpeech(stream) helper (pumps setImmediate until stream.record.outboundFrames stops growing → synthesis done → isSpeaking cleared) before delivering the answer. Verified: @cernia/api typecheck clean; full voice-call-handler suite 83/83 green; production code untouched.

Voice hardening — SERIALIZED intent dispatch (concurrent-flow race). The handler's onIntent fired `void registry.handle(...)` per intent, so two flow-opening intents emitted in ONE turn (LLM emits book+reschedule together, or both auto-resume after verification) dispatched CONCURRENTLY and both passed the existing `deferredFlowIntents` `flowActive()` guard before either set `activeBookingFlow` (startBookingFlow only assigns it AFTER an await) — starting two deterministic flows at once and double-prompting the caller. Extracted a pure FIFO serializer apps/api/src/serial-dispatch.ts (createSerialRunner: runs each intent one-at-a-time, in order, next never starts until the previous settles; rejection-isolated) + apps/api/src/serial-dispatch.test.ts (3 tests: serial+in-order, rejection isolation, max-concurrency=1). apps/api/src/voice-call-handler.ts now dispatches intents through it, so the first flow registers before the second is handled and the goal-stack defers it correctly. apps/api typecheck clean, lint clean, serial-dispatch 3/3; the voice-call-handler suites show IDENTICAL failure counts to baseline (8 pre-existing carry-forward across 3 files, git-stash-verified — zero new regressions).

Ambient-scribe note-drafting MODEL A/B shipped as evidence (docs/status/evidence/2026-07-29-scribe-model-ab.md + .json). 12 audited drafts of ONE fixed transcript through POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$draft on a real API + real Postgres, 5 models: claude-sonnet-4, alibayram/medgemma:27b, qwen3-vl:8b-instruct, medgemma:latest(4.3B), qwen3-scribe:latest. Coverage vs a 37-checkpoint rubric: sonnet 88% / medgemma:27b 83.5% / qwen3-vl 77% / medgemma:4b 75.5% / qwen3-scribe 73%. Latency 5.3s / 443.5s / 65.6s / 13.9s / 23.2s. Every draft proven to have invoked the claimed model by joining llm_audit_events.response_hash to an Ollama-side logging proxy's sha256(content) - time-window attribution was tried and REJECTED (back-to-back runs cross-claim wire rows). Two findings for consumers of this path: (a) the currently configured default OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3-scribe is the WEAKEST model measured on completeness, and is a re-tag of qwen3-vl:8b-instruct (identical weights blob, no SYSTEM prompt, no ADAPTER; only num_ctx 8192 differs - a latent truncation risk on long visits); (b) the most complete model is the least faithful - claude-sonnet-4 reproducibly invented a medication concentration and a numeric anatomical identifier that is WRONG for the site named. No production default changed by this eval (recommendation only).

CLOSURE PASS — two outcomes. (1) FIXED HERE: the text-channel booking-silence bug (surfaced by the text-only harness 2026-06-19) is closed. Root cause was as filed — the text hardcoded handler in apps/api/src/text-dialog-routes.ts fell through to a bare `state.pendingIntents.push({kind: intent.kind})` for every non-pay-balance/transfer/end-call action, so a turn that emitted ONLY an intent returned {messages: [], intents: [{kind: "book-appointment"}]} and the caller got silence; voice masked it because the orchestrator narrates with TTS prompts, text has no narration layer. Fix: a TEXT_ACTION_ACK map (19 action kinds → a fixed, non-PHI channel-appropriate line) plus applyActionAcks(state), invoked in POST /text-dialog/:id/message AFTER the dialog turn and after the in-flight intent dispatches settle. It fires ONLY when the turn produced no agent text at all (stream.peekAgentText().length === 0), so a model that did speak is never doubled up, and it adds at most ONE line even when a turn emits several actions. transfer-to-human and end-call are deliberately excluded — both close the stream and the client branches on ended/transferTo, so a trailing utterance would mislead. Every ack string is a fixed literal that interpolates nothing off the intent (no appointment times, names, or medications), keeping the backstop out of the PHI path. Tests: 8 new cases in apps/api/src/text-dialog-routes.test.ts under "action-only turns are never silent" — the book-appointment regression itself, 4 parameterised action kinds, a no-double-up case, a one-line-for-many-actions case, and a stays-silent-for-transfer case. (2) NARROWED: the nightly --live canary bullet. Its "the workflow is dormant (dispatch-only)" premise was stale — .github/workflows/voice-agent-eval-live.yml has had `schedule: cron "0 4 * * *"` and `gh run list` shows nightly executions going back weeks; the cost-control ask is also already implemented (--max-spend-usd circuit breaker, default $2, skipped-vs-failed distinction, report-only + scorecard artifact + auto-issue). The ONE thing genuinely still missing is the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY repo secret, verified absent by `gh secret list` (only MIRROR_DEPLOY_KEY). Separately noted, not re-filed: those nightly runs have been RED at the "Build voice-agent-evals" step with TS2307 (@cernia/design-tokens, @cernia/speech), which is the backwards-pnpm-ellipsis bug fixed repo-wide by #770 / commit 003d06c2 — that landed 2026-08-03 16:50 EDT, AFTER the 06:53 UTC nightly, so the first nightly eligible to get past the build step is 2026-08-04. No workflow change made here; #770 already carries the fix.

history.note: R10 part 1 COMPLETE — admin-side escalation-number validation. Pairs with the call-time callback fallback (R10 part 2, below): config-time prevention + run-time safety net. 3 new tests in voice-agent-admin-routes.test.ts (transfer+empty→400 & not persisted, non-E164→400, transfer+valid E.164→200); full file 15/15. apps/api typecheck clean; changed region lint-clean (one pre-existing carry-forward assertion on an untouched persona line). R10 hardening — a FAILED transfer never drops the caller silently. The transfer-to-human path attempted the live carrier redirect (telephony.redirectToHuman) but, when a live-redirect backend was configured yet the caller was NOT bridged (escalation number missing, or the redirect threw), it fell through to terminate()+stream.close() — dead air. Added apps/api/src/voice-call-handler.ts fallbackToCallbackAfterFailedTransfer(): captures a callback Task via appointmentManager.requestCallback for a verified caller (reason 'general-question'), speaks an acknowledgment either way (the line is never dead), waits (bounded) for it to play, and logs a visible voice.call.transfer phase:'callback-fallback' audit row {ok, taskId?}. Gated on `canLiveRedirect && !bridgedToHuman` so tests / legacy deploys without a live-redirect backend keep the existing close-and-drop (finalResponse still drives a TwiML transfer at the webhook) — zero behaviour change there. The new scribe cost routes DO surface both.

LLM gateway BUDGETS are still in-memory and per-pod: packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/cost-tracking.ts holds 'private budgets: Map<string, StoredBudget>', so a tenant over budget on pod A is under budget on pod B and every cap resets on process restart - while the ledger itself is durable. checkBudget() is on the hot path (per LLM call, buffered + streaming: api.ts:211 and api.ts:353). FIXED since this bullet was written: (i) the sub-cent no-op - BudgetManager.checkAndConsume() now takes { usdMicroCents } and baselines on summary.totalUsdMicroCents; (ii) resetMonthlySpend() having no caller - the monthly boundary is now a lazy UTC period rollover inside CostStore, so it cannot silently not-exist; (iii) float drift in the accumulator - it is integer micro-cents now. STILL SIZED, NOT FIXED (durable per-tenant enforcement): wiring BudgetManager/PostgresBudgetStore into apps/api. Two blockers documented in the budget-manager.ts header - (1) checkAndConsume is O(tenant's period call volume) PER CALL because PostgresCostLedgerStore.summarize() defers to list() (unbounded SELECT *, summed in JS) instead of a SQL SUM()+GROUP BY, so hot-path latency grows monotonically through the billing period incl. live voice; (2) autoPauseOnOverrun defaults TRUE (migration 090), turning 'reject this call' into a whole-period breaker. Prerequisites in order: rewrite summarize() as a SQL aggregate; move the check off the request path (or cache it); set the overrun policy explicitly per tier (soft cap for voice). Related, smaller, same class: GET /admin/llm/$report reads the in-memory records[] so it returns per-pod since-restart numbers despite durable data existing; and rateLimitWindows is per-pod too (wants Redis, cf. RedisCallerRateLimiter).

LLM AUDIT cannot identify WHICH self-hosted model produced a completion. llm_audit_events.model stores the logical gateway ModelId only (every Ollama call records 'qwen' - packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/types.ts:122, providers-openai.ts:237), while the concrete tag lives in ProviderConfig.deploymentName (OLLAMA_MODEL, apps/api/src/llm-gateway-routes.ts:386-390) and is NEVER persisted. Given a signed ambient-scribe note you cannot answer 'which model drafted this?' from the audit log - a clinical traceability gap, and the reason the 2026-07-29 scribe model A/B needed an external wire proxy to attribute its runs (docs/status/evidence/2026-07-29-scribe-model-ab.md). FIX: persist deploymentName (e.g. an llm_audit_events.deployment_name column, or fold it into model) so the audit row names the served model. Note llm_audit_events.provider is also unreliable - the table already holds a 'claude-sonnet-4'/'ollama' row from a prior session.

STT IS NOW PRICED (migration 344): scribe_sessions.stt_billable_sec / stt_audio_sec / stt_passes / stt_passes_unmetered are written at the vendor call by MeteredBatchTranscriber (apps/api/src/scribe-stt-metering.ts) and read by attributeSttCost, so a note reports a real STT figure instead of 'unpriced' forever. The DOUBLE-SEND is also closed: the per-chunk live-preview pass no longer runs unasked on a per-audio-minute backend (IBatchTranscriber.meteredPerAudioMinute + CERNIA_SCRIBE_LIVE_TRANSCRIPT opt-in), so a visit is submitted ONCE. REMAINING: (a) the $0.0043/audio-min Deepgram rate is a PUBLISHED LIST price, never reconciled against a Deepgram invoice, so every STT figure is an estimate; (b) no live vendor measurement exists - the pass count and the metered quantity are proven structurally (recording double at the vendor boundary, real HTTP + real Postgres in apps/api/src/scribe-stt-double-send.integration.test.ts) and on a stack whose CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT is unset (backend = stub); (c) pre-344 sessions carry NULL usage and stay unpriced by design - not backfillable, the quantity was never recorded; (d) tenants who opt the preview back IN still pay ~2x, which is now RECORDED and surfaced as a duplication factor in the STT component detail rather than hidden.

NO RATE IS INVOICE-RECONCILED. Every entry in packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/pricing.ts MODEL_RATES is 'published-list' (or 'proxy-unverified' for claude-bedrock, which borrows the first-party Sonnet rate because Bedrock's partner rate was never looked up). Until a rate is matched against a bill actually paid, every cost figure the platform reports is an ESTIMATE and must be labelled one - which matters because per-note price is being set as max(floor, cost x (1+margin)) off these numbers. Reconcile against a real Anthropic invoice and flip source to 'invoice-reconciled'; the pricing.test.ts gate asserting nothing is reconciled will then fail loudly, which is the reminder to re-word the estimate caveats at every surface.

COMPUTE AND STORAGE ARE NOT ATTRIBUTED PER NOTE AT ALL, so every note is unpriced overall even once STT lands. @cernia/finops ComputeProbe + PostgresStorageProbe exist but have ZERO runtime callers and no scheduler. Self-hosted LLM inference is blocked on the same gap: resolveModelRate('qwen') returns unpriced with reason 'self-hosted-compute-not-metered' precisely because GPU-seconds are not metered. Metering compute is the single change that would let a self-hosted note be priced at all.

@cernia/finops IS DEAD CODE ON THE LIVE PATH, and this is a trap for the next reader. Its seven attribution adapters, pricing-table.ts getRate() (which THROWS on unknown keys) and PostgresCostTracker.record/recordBatch have ZERO runtime callers, so cost_ledger (migration 067) is permanently empty and GET /cernia-ops/finops/rollup reads zeros. Worse, PostgresCostTracker REJECTS the wildcard tenantId '*' that the rollup route passes and there is no listTenantIdsInWindow, so /by-tenant and /margin-per-tier always return empty with NO error at all. Decide explicitly: either wire the adapters onto the live gateway path, or delete the package and fold its remaining value (the multi-vendor rate-table shape) into o1-llm-gateway/pricing.ts. Note the finops adapters ALSO carry the per-entry Math.round-to-whole-cents defect that migration 331 fixed in o4.

history.note: SUB-CENT COST UNDER-COUNT FIXED (live cost-accounting defect). The o4 LLM cost ledger stored cost as rounded INTEGER CENTS per entry (o4_llm_cost_ledger.usd_cents, migration 075), and the live sink makeO4CostLedgerSink (apps/api/src/llm-gateway-routes.ts:99) narrowed with Math.round(estimatedCostUSD*100) BEFORE the insert. Every call under half a cent recorded exactly 0 - a 1k-token Claude Sonnet prompt (~0.3c) and 60s of Deepgram (~0.43c) both booked as free. Because the truncation was PER ENTRY the error accumulated linearly with call volume instead of cancelling, so reported margin looked best precisely when it was least real. FIX: NEW migration 331_o4_cost_ledger_subcent_precision.sql adds usd_micro_cents BIGINT (integer micro-cents = cents x 10^6) + a non-negative CHECK, idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS + pg_constraint-guarded DO block). Chose integer micro-cents over NUMERIC(18,6) because node-postgres returns NUMERIC as a decimal STRING, which would need a decimal library or parseFloat (reintroducing the float drift ADR 0023 forbids); coercing an integer string is lossless inside the safe-integer range (~$90M/entry). Never DOUBLE PRECISION. packages/o4-cost-tracking-budgets: types.ts gains MICRO_CENTS_PER_CENT/usdToMicroCents/microCentsToCents/centsToMicroCents + CostEntry.usdMicroCents + precisionSource; cost-ledger.ts gains aggregateEntries() which sums micro-cents at FULL precision and rounds to cents exactly ONCE at the presentation boundary (shared by the in-memory and Postgres stores so they cannot drift); postgres-cost-ledger-store.ts persists+reads the column (BIGINT arrives as a string, coerced via toMicroCents); spend-graph.ts timeSeries/breakdown fixed - they were summing per-entry rounded cents too, the same defect class. apps/api/src/llm-gateway-routes.ts now writes usdMicroCents alongside the legacy usdCents (kept so existing readers/dashboards keep working). BACKFILL DELIBERATELY NONE: rows rounded to 0 lost their value irrecoverably, so fabricating one would invent revenue data. usd_micro_cents IS NULL is the honest marker meaning 'no sub-cent precision was ever captured'; such rows are widened from usd_cents on read and flagged precisionSource='widened', and SpendSummary.widenedEntryCount reports how much of any total is affected. Pre-migration periods therefore UNDER-REPORT; post-migration periods are exact. PHI/ADR-0140: the one new column is a pure integer money amount derived from token counts and provider price lists - no patient, narrative, prompt or user content - so o4_llm_cost_ledger stays defensibly PHI-free and its place in the erasure retain-set (apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts:395, 7-year financial-records obligation) is unaffected. ADR 0004 unchanged (tenant_id + composite PK already present). No new routes, so no deriveOperation mapping needed. PROOF (watched RED first): packages/o4-cost-tracking-budgets/src/subcent-precision.test.ts '1,000 entries of 0.3c each total 300c - NOT 0c' failed on unfixed code with 'expected +0 to be 300', then passed. Same assertion proven end-to-end through the LIVE sink (apps/api/src/llm-cost-sink.test.ts, 1000 x $0.003 -> 300c) and against REAL Postgres (postgres-cost-ledger-store.test.ts, incl. THREE DEFECTS, all measured on the 156-note corpus (7 DBs on test PG :5433 - 963 LLM calls, 153 notes with a Composition). (1) RATE 4x LOW: MODEL_META priced `claude-haiku-4` at $0.25/$1.25 per MTok - the ORIGINAL claude-3-haiku rate - while providers-anthropic.ts ANTHROPIC_MODEL_MAP maps that id to the WIRE model `claude-haiku-4-5`, published at $1/$5 per MTok. Every note was under-costed by exactly 4x, in the direction that flatters margin. Re-derived from the platform's own recorded token counts: $0.001517/note at the old rate vs $0.006067/note corrected (avg 3635 prompt + 486 completion tokens/note), the corrected figure reproducing the founder's independent $0.006 estimate to 3 significant figures. (2) UNPRICED INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM FREE: costPer1kPromptUSD is a bare number, so self-hosted `qwen` (hard-coded 0, commented 'Cost 0 (own hardware)') booked every self-hosted note at exactly $0.00 in the `exact` precision class. A self-hosted note is not free - it costs GPU-seconds. (3) tags={} ON EVERY ROW: makeO4CostLedgerSink dropped purposeOfUse, so a note's drafting pass was indistinguishable from its coding pass, follow-up pass, or a re-draft. CORRECTION TO A LONG-STANDING PREMISE: the @cernia/finops attribution adapters + pricing-table getRate() (which THROWS on an unknown key) were assumed to be the live cost path. They are NOT - cost_ledger (migration 067) has ZERO runtime writers repo-wide, so the throw was never exercised and the FinOps dashboard reads an always-empty table. The live path is o1-llm-gateway -> makeO4CostLedgerSink -> o4_llm_cost_ledger. THE FIX, in the migration-338 / PR-#742 idiom (separate the claim from the outcome; let the outcome be an absence): NEW packages/o1-llm-gateway/src/pricing.ts - MODEL_RATES keyed on the WIRE model with source (published-list | invoice-reconciled | proxy-unverified) + verifiedAt, and resolveModelRate() returning a DISCRIMINATED UNION so 'unpriced' is a value the type system forces callers to handle rather than a magic zero. computeCostUSD() returns null, never 0. `qwen` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT (a 0 row would reintroduce the bug); the design call is that self-hosted inference attributes COMPUTE, not tokens, and GPU-seconds are not metered, so the honest per-token answer is 'unknown'. MODEL_META's per-1k fields are now DERIVED from MODEL_RATES at module load so two hand-maintained rate tables can never drift again - exactly how the haiku rate went stale. One shared priceUsage() replaces FOUR byte-identical private computeCost() copies (anthropic/openai/google/bedrock). NEW migration 342_o4_cost_ledger_pricing_status.sql adds pricing_status/rate_source/unpriced_reason (additive + nullable so the apps/ml-ai-service twin writer keeps working), CHECK constraints on both enums, and a DB-level 'unpriced => usd_micro_cents IS NULL' invariant so no future writer can book an unknown cost at zero. NULL usd_micro_cents keeps its 331 meaning ('no sub-cent precision captured') and is disambiguated by pricing_status rather than overloaded. aggregateEntries() now EXCLUDES unpriced entries and reports unpricedEntryCount + complete. NEW apps/api/src/scribe-cost-per-note.ts DERIVES a note's cost - no note_cost table, because a stored copy would rot on a rate correction, a superseded re-draft, or an erasure - via Composition id -> llm_audit_events.resource_id OR reserved_resource_id (migration 338, matching EITHER column) -> request_id -> o4_llm_cost_ledger. THE LOAD-BEARING RULE: a PARTIAL total is UNPRICED, not a smaller number. If LLM priced and STT did not, totalUsdMicroCents is NULL and the priced portion surfaces only as an explicitly-named pricedLowerBoundUsdMicroCents. This is commercially load-bearing: per-note price is max(floor, cost x (1+margin)), and a floor ABSORBS a zero, so a broken rate table would otherwise produce a plausible invoice with no signal anywhere. BOTH SURFACES (CLAUDE.md - shipping one alone is half-shipping): tenant-scoped GET /scribe/cost/notes + GET /scribe/cost/note/:compositionId (apps/api/src/scribe-cost-routes.ts; entitlement -> tenant-admin role -> global RBAC, deriveOperation mapped, tenant ALWAYS from rbacClaims) for apps/admin; and cross-tenant GET /cernia-ops/finops/scribe-note-cost with sha256-hex(16) tenantHash (CLAUDE.md invariant 5) for apps/cernia-ops. STT: attributeSttCost() is wired and priced (Deepgram nova-2 pre-recorded, published list $0.0043/audio-min, NEVER reconciled against a Deepgram invoice - this stack has no DEEPGRAM_API_KEY and has never been billed by Deepgram), but reports UNPRICED live because the billable duration is never persisted: the Deepgram adapter DOES produce BatchTranscriptResult.durationSec and BatchTranscriberTranscriptSource.get() in scribe-draft-routes.ts DROPS it. STT is plausibly the LARGER line (~$0.065 for a 15-min visit, an order of magnitude above the LLM), so reporting it as 0 would understate a note by ~90%. ALSO FIXED: cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts carried hand-copied 'local type mirrors' with a note to swap them 'when the dependency lands' - @cernia/finops was ALREADY in apps/api/package.json and already imported in index.ts, so they were duplicate definitions free to drift silently. Now real imports. LIVE PROOF (intent channel, over the wire, RED first): RED = 454/454 journey_a ledger rows read usd_cents=0 and no pricing_status column exists. GREEN = real apps/api (tsx, PID 39636) on :8123 against real Postgres cpn_live (:5433, schema snapshot + migration 342). PORT OWNERSHIP PROVEN BEFORE TRUSTING ANY RESPONSE: sentinel Composition CPNCOMPA exists only in cpn_live (decoy cpn_decoy has no scribe_sessions table at all), and inserting one more ledger row directly into cpn_live moved the API's pricedLowerBound 955200 -> 1105200 micro-cents by exactly the inserted amount and surfaced a new scribe-followup pass. GET /scribe/cost/note/CPNCOMPA -> 200 {status:'unpriced', totalUsdMicroCents:NULL, pricedLowerBound:1105200, blockedBy:[stt,compute,storage], llmByPass separating scribe-draft/scribe-coding/scribe-followup}. Self-hosted CPNCOMPB -> lowerBound 0 AND status 'unpriced' (the exact distinction that did not previously exist). Period summary -> meanPricedNoteUsdMicroCents:NULL plus an explicit interpretation string. Cross-tenant: a second, equally entitled tenant gets 404 for CPNCOMPA. No token -> 401. Tenant-admin on the cernia-ops route -> 403 (CLAUDE.md invariant 6). Operator -> 200 with tenantHash only and pricedFraction:0. The DB CHECK was proven by a direct INSERT of an unpriced row carrying an amount -> 'violates check constraint o4_llm_cost_ledger_unpriced_has_no_amount_chk'. ADR-0127: @cernia/o1-llm-gateway typecheck=0 lint=0 build=0 test 207/207 (+13 new pricing gates); @cernia/o4-cost-tracking-budgets typecheck=0 lint=0 build=0 test 223/223 (baseline 218, +5 real-Postgres gates); @cernia/api typecheck=0 build=0, lint 63 errors = the LOW END of the documented 63-68 carry-forward baseline with ZERO in touched files, targeted tests 49/49 including iam-route-guards.repo-coverage (which asserts every RBAC-governed route is mapped, validating the new /scribe/cost/* mapping). One PRE-EXISTING load-sensitive flake observed and NOT caused here: o4 'hourlyBuckets accumulate sub-cent entries at full precision' times out at the 5000ms default under parallel load and passes in isolation at 3.2s. NO PRICE IS SET: publishing a per-note rate is the founder's decision and is explicitly deferred until this reports real numbers. Nothing in MODEL_RATES is invoice-reconciled, so EVERY figure the chain produces today is an estimate against a published list price, and is labelled as such at every surface.

STT DOUBLE-SEND CLOSED + STT COST BECOMES A REAL NUMBER. Two defects, both surfaced by the PR #757 cost chain and both re-derived before being fixed. (1) THE DOUBLE-SEND. A visit was submitted to the speech vendor TWICE: once per ~30 s capture chunk (scribeLiveTranscribe in apps/api/src/index.ts, feeding the recorder's live-preview panel via scribe_live_transcripts) and once again as the whole assembled recording at $draft (BatchTranscriberTranscriptSource in apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts). Both passes read the SAME scribeBatchTranscriber instance, so a 15-minute visit bought 30 audio-minutes on a per-audio-minute backend - a 100% duplicate of what is, by an order of magnitude, the largest cost line on an ambient-scribe note (~$0.065 STT vs ~$0.006 LLM). The preview was ON BY DEFAULT ((env ?? '1') !== '0'), so every deployment paid it without choosing it, and nothing recorded that it had happened. (2) durationSec DROPPED. Every batch backend produces BatchTranscriptResult.durationSec (Deepgram from metadata.duration, self-hosted Whisper from duration, the stub from the byte count) and BatchTranscriberTranscriptSource.get() returned only {text, words, vocabulary} - so the one quantity needed to price the note's largest line was produced and thrown away, which is why attributeSttCost reported 'unpriced' on every note. WHY BOTH PASSES SURVIVE (the reason is written into apps/api/src/scribe-stt-metering.ts so nobody re-tries the obvious fix): the whole-file pass CANNOT be replaced by concatenating chunk transcripts, because speaker diarization indices are assigned PER REQUEST (Speaker 1 in chunk 3 is unrelated to Speaker 1 in chunk 9 - stitching produces confident, wrong who-said-what attribution in a clinical note) and word timings are ABSOLUTE seconds into the submitted audio, which the click-to-verify evidence spans (migration 323) index against the assembled recording. And the live pass cannot simply be deleted either: apps/admin scribe-recorder-view.tsx polls it every 12 s and renders it. THE FIX, in two parts. (a) A CAPABILITY, NOT A GUESS: IBatchTranscriber.meteredPerAudioMinute is now REQUIRED, exactly like supportsKeyterms (D25) - deepgram-prerecorded true, stub + whisper-selfhost false ('not metered' is deliberately NOT the same claim as 'free'; self-hosted burns GPU-seconds nobody meters). The live preview now runs unasked only where a second pass buys no vendor invoice; on a metered backend it requires an explicit CERNIA_SCRIBE_LIVE_TRANSCRIPT=1, and the API logs at boot that the feature is off and which variable turns it on. Nothing is taken away where nothing was being paid. (b) EVERY SUBMISSION IS METERED: MeteredBatchTranscriber decorates the transcriber on BOTH passes rather than calling a meter at each call site - the call sites are precisely what forgot, so 'a vendor call happened' and 'the meter fired' are now the same event and a future third call site is metered by construction. Migration 344 adds scribe_sessions.stt_billable_sec / stt_audio_sec / stt_passes / stt_passes_unmetered plus scribe_live_transcripts.duration_sec. THE HONESTY RULES CARRIED DOWN A LEVEL, both load-bearing because per-note price is max(floor, cost x (1+margin)) and a floor absorbs a zero: every column is NULLABLE WITH NO DEFAULT so 'never metered' can never read as 'metered, and free'; and a pass whose duration the backend did not report increments stt_passes_unmetered and makes the WHOLE component unpriced rather than summing the passes we happen to know about - a partial quantity is not a smaller quantity. A DB CHECK forbids negative quantities and an unmetered count without a pass count. The meter ACCUMULATES rather than upserts, because a re-uploaded chunk that is transcribed again is a second invoice line even though only one snippet is kept. MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER on one 15-minute visit (900 audio-seconds): BEFORE 31 vendor submissions / 1800 billable audio-seconds / $0.129 STT at the published list rate; AFTER 1 submission / 900 seconds / $0.0645. STT cost per note halves, and the note's cost stops being unknown. Against the PR #757 measured LLM figure of ~$0.006067/note, a 15-minute note goes from ~$0.135 (had STT been priceable) to ~$0.0706. PROVEN LIVE vs STRUCTURALLY - stated explicitly because there is no Deepgram measurement here. LIVE: the real apps/api booted (tsx, PID 6064) on :8123 with CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT=deepgram-prerecorded against Postgres :5433, answered /health 200 as the sole listener on that port, and logged the gate firing verbatim ('scribe live-transcript preview is OFF: the configured STT backend bills per audio-minute and the preview re-transcribes the whole visit (~2x STT spend). Set CERNIA_SCRIBE_LIVE_TRANSCRIPT=1 ...'). LIVE: apps/api/src/scribe-stt-double-send.integration.test.ts drives a whole capture->finalize->draft visit over REAL HTTP against a real Fastify listening socket and a real per-test Postgres schema, proving port/schema identity first (a row written THROUGH the API is read back FROM the schema under test and is absent from the public-schema decoy) - RED 31 calls / 1800 s, GREEN 1 call / 900 s, both read straight off the new columns. STRUCTURAL: the vendor itself is a recording double. This stack's CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT is unset (backend = stub), so although a DEEPGRAM_API_KEY exists in apps/api/.env the scribe batch path has NOT been billing Deepgram here; the doubling is a property of the code that fires on whatever backend a deployment configures. NO live Deepgram invoice was observed and none is claimed. ADR-0127: @cernia/speech typecheck=0 build=0, lint 6 = carry-forward baseline with ZERO in touched code, test 321 (318 pass / 3 pre-existing streaming failures in factory/round-trip/deepgram-stt-backend, all barge-in + streaming, none reachable from the batch path). @cernia/api typecheck=0 build=0, lint 63 = the documented carry-forward baseline exactly, with ZERO errors in code added here. Targeted tests 155/155: scribe-stt-metering 12, scribe-cost-per-note 13, scribe-stt-double-send 6, plus the full affected regression set (scribe-draft-routes 67, scribe-silent-degradation 21, scribe-chunk-routes 6, scribe-live-transcript 5, scribe-live-transcript-store 5, scribe-session-store 10, scribe-word-timings 5, scribe-draft-llm-correlation 3, scribe-chunk-limits 12, scribe-test-migrations 5).

stages.name: Telehealth & remote patient monitoring
stages.rationale: RPM (remote patient monitoring) is the Q-wave's reimbursable feature: device ingestion + care-plan generation + adherence tracking. Telehealth visits via WebRTC are the synchronous-care complement. Both built, neither runs.

stages.name: Caregiver delegation & identity federation
stages.rationale: Allows a patient's family/caregiver to act on their behalf (proxy), JIT-grant temporary access to a covering provider, SAML/OIDC federation for hospital-network SSO, and break-glass emergency access. Compliance-load-bearing for any enterprise pilot.

baseline.summary: g-d1-caregiver-proxy, g-d2-delegation, g-d3-jit-access, g-d4-access-review-attestation, g-d5-saml-oidc-federation, g-d6-break-glass all shipped. Existing auth flow doesn't consult any of them; no SAML/OIDC providers configured in apps/api boot path.

current.summary: Caregiver-federation backend complete, and BOTH SSO protocols (OIDC + SAML 2.0) are now wired end-to-end at apps/api boot with full session mint. OIDC: TenantSsoFactory (index.ts step 10i.1) with KmsBackedJwtIssuer + FHIR-User provisioner/lookup + Redis/InMemory state store + FetchOidcHttpClient + tenant-secret ClientSecretResolver. SAML 2.0: TenantSamlProviderFactory (index.ts step 10i.2) builds the hardened in-repo SamlIdentityProvider per tenant — real XML-DSig with XSW guards + RSA/ECDSA-SHA2 algorithm allowlist + replay cache + InResponseTo binding, JIT provisioning, role resolution, and session mint via the SAME jwtIssuer.sign path OIDC uses (byte-identical sessions). Routes: GET /metadata, GET /login (SP-initiated), POST /acs (full session). The earlier node-saml validator detour was removed in favour of this single canonical path. SSO routes still 503 for tenants with no enabled IdP connection, so wiring only widens what works. No SAML handshake work remains deferred (multi-pod InResponseTo store shares the OidcStateStore horizontal-scale follow-up; IdP-initiated SSO is a per-connection opt-in).

Negative paths: tampered assertion → 401 saml-verification-failed; unsolicited (no InResponseTo) → 401. THREE genuine bugs surfaced by driving the full server (the in-process saml-routes.test.ts registers only the saml plugin, no global RBAC hook, so it missed all three): (1) CRITICAL — /api/auth/saml/* + /api/auth/sso/* were NOT in the unauth allowlist (permitAllForUnauthenticatedRoutes), so the global RBAC hook 401-gated SP-initiated SSO login: SSO was unreachable for unauthenticated users. Added both prefixes (each route still self-gates: 503 no-factory / 404 no-connection / real verification before any session mint). (2) /admin/idp-connections* had no deriveOperation mapping → */* 403; mapped to IdpConnection. (3) the /caregiver/* + /access/* mapping from the earlier 2026-06-02 entry. openssl is used at runtime for the stub cert (no committed secrets); the spec SKIPS (not fails) if openssl is unavailable, for portability. Dev runs Stripe TEST mode; only the sk_live_ key flip + signed BAA remain (operator/legal, no code). v1-clinical-launch U17 (2026-07-14): closed an audited security gap — ambient-scribe and telehealth-visits (KTD16) now have product rows + createRequireProduct()/checker-backed route gates, closing the window where any tenant on any tier could reach those paid routes unentitled. 2026-07-29: closed a latent ~15.5x metered over-report — the nightly flush and the on-demand $report-metered route sent the cumulative month-to-date total to a SUMMING Stripe meter under a month-constant idempotency key, which only dedupes for 24h. Both now send the increment since a durable per-(tenant, period, metric) watermark (migration 332). Latent, never live: no production tenants at the time. 2026-07-31: the ambient scribe became PURCHASABLE — storefront entry + an operator-configured price (migration 341 gives catalog_prices the fixed-fee/allowance/overage triple plus a tenant_id for negotiated rates), an enforced ADR-0035 tier floor, and both the apps/admin and apps/cernia-ops surfaces. Live RED-then-GREEN 23/23 with settlement through the real Stripe-webhook cascade. NOTE the price triple is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing meters scribe usage yet, so the store states terms the billing chain does not enforce (tracked in remaining). 2026-07-31 (later): the scribe got its REAL price and the ops editor stopped looking broken. $29.99 per CLINICIAN per month (catalog-seed.ts LIST_PRICES + PRODUCT_TERMS quantityUnit), annual on the platform-wide 10%-off ladder = $323.89/yr, and NO included allowance and NO per-note rate — every note is billed individually and the founder has not set that rate yet. The ops price route now writes BOTH cadence rows from one call (explicit annualPriceCents, else annualFromMonthly), which closes the gap where an operator published a price and the annual-by-default storefront answered "price not configured". Also shipped: the per-unit billing POLICY as operator configuration (migration 343 product_usage_pricing) plus the resolver for max(floor, cost x (1 + margin)) that reports WHY the floor applied — separating "cost measured and genuinely below floor" (healthy) from "cost could not be priced at all" (a defect), so a floor cannot silently rescue a blind cost chain. Both numbers ship UNSET; unset resolves to unbillable, never to zero. Proven live over the wire RED-then-GREEN across all four cadence x scope combinations with a cross-tenant isolation control (docs/status/evidence/scribe-pricing/).

Entitlement lifecycle — residual gaps after the 2026-07-29 cancellation fix (apps/api/src/billing-routes.ts customer.subscription.deleted → PostgresProductCatalogStore.scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants): (a) a cancellation event carrying current_period_end=null writes NO expiry (deliberate — we never fall back to immediate revocation) and only warns, so it needs an operator to finish via POST /cernia-ops/platform/entitlements/expire; there is no alerting on that warn yet. (b) NOTHING re-syncs the derived voice_tier column after an entitlement lapses by expires_at — access itself is correctly cut (hasActive is read-time), but voice_tier on voice_tenant_config can sit stale at “pro” until the next syncVoiceTierFromEntitlements() call (apps/api/src/voice-tier-sync.ts). (c) no apps/cernia-ops UI for the new expire route — operators must call it directly. (d) subscription downgrade (customer.subscription.updated to a cheaper plan) still does not narrow purchased product entitlements; only full cancellation does.

packages/billing/src/invoicing/flush-metered-usage.ts still sends the CUMULATIVE count.total under a period-constant idempotency key — the same shape fixed in the two live paths on 2026-07-29 (migration 332). It is exported from @cernia/billing but called by nothing, so it is not a live defect; it is a loaded gun for whoever wires it. Either delete it or give it a MeterReportWatermarkStore and have it send claim.delta under claim.idempotencyKey. Currently carries a NOT-WIRED warning in its header only.

Metered flush has no alerting on a wedged watermark: if reportMeterEvent keeps failing, billing_meter_report_watermarks.inflight_total stays pinned and that tenant's usage silently stops reaching Stripe (under-report). Migration 332 ships the partial index idx_billing_meter_watermarks_inflight for the query; nothing reads it yet. Add a cernia-ops surface or a nightly check for rows with inflight_total IS NOT NULL and a stale updated_at.

Metered-flush enumeration — residual after the 2026-07-29 store-tenant leak fix (apps/api/src/saas-subscription-store.ts `enumerateBillableTenants`, consumed by runMeteredFlushSweep in apps/api/src/saas-nightly-batches.ts): (a) CLOSED 2026-08-03 for the ambient scribe: PRD R6/R7 (docs/prds/metering-pricing-cost-chain.md) is implemented — apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts now records ONE `feature-use` usage event per successfully drafted note via apps/api/src/scribe-note-pricer.ts, idempotent on the SESSION id (a redraft is not a second sale) and fail-soft (a metering fault never costs a clinician a finished note). Store-purchase tenants therefore flush a non-empty rollup. STILL OPEN for every other metered product — nothing emits for voice-minute / sms / email. (b) `runPricingReconcileSweep` (saas-nightly-batches.ts :1292) still enumerates subscription-only; harmless today because it immediately no-ops on tenants with no billing subscription, but it is the same enumeration shape and should be revisited if store purchases ever gain reconcilable pricing. (c) no backfill: usage already recorded for store-purchase tenants in past calendar months is still unflushed — the sweep only ever flushes the CURRENT calendar month (calendarMonthPeriod), so recovering that revenue needs a one-off operator replay.

Store pricing — CONNECTED for the ambient scribe (2026-08-03), still open for every other metered product. The scribe now has a seeded per-note policy (migration 346: floor 10c, margin 40%, provenance='seeded-default') and the FIRST production caller of resolvePerUnitCharge (apps/api/src/scribe-note-pricer.ts, invoked fail-soft from POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$draft), so a drafted note produces a real billing_usage_events line. REMAINING: (a) the invoice generator still applies allowance+overage per TIER rather than per product (packages/billing/src/invoicing/invoice-generator.ts, PRD R1b) — the pricer writes centsPerUnit/basis/policyProvenance into the usage event's metadata, but no invoice line reads them yet, so the resolved per-note price does not reach a customer invoice; (b) NO OTHER product has a usage producer or a seeded policy — voice-minute / sms / email overage still resolve `unresolvable`, i.e. unbillable; (c) EVERY note today reports basis='cost-unpriced' and healthy=false, because `compute` and `storage` are never attributed per note (ComputeProbe / PostgresStorageProbe in @cernia/finops have no runtime caller), so assembleNoteCost marks every note unpriced and the floor is charged 100% of the time. That is the honest state and NOT a defect in the pricer — it clears by itself when those two probes get a runtime caller, with no edit to scribe-note-pricer.ts. Until then the `cost-unpriced` signal is universal and therefore carries no per-note information; an operator dashboard surfacing it should say so rather than alarm on every note.

Seeded per-unit price is PROVISIONAL and must be replaced by the operator. Migration 346 seeded the scribe's floor (10c) and margin (40%) purely so the product could be sold before the founder settled the numbers; `provenance='seeded-default'` marks every such row, the ops price editor renders a warning banner from it, and the value rides onto each billing_usage_events line as `policyProvenance`. The numbers derive from a measured cost of $0.0706/note (PRs #757/#764) against vendor rates that are PUBLISHED LIST and have never been reconciled against an invoice we paid — no deployment has yet sent live traffic to Deepgram, which is ~91% of that cost. Closing this means the founder setting a real floor + margin in apps/cernia-ops (Platform -> Store -> ambient-scribe -> terms panel), which stamps provenance='operator-set' and drops the banner. Until then any revenue figure derived from the per-note price is an estimate on top of an estimate.

Store pricing — an annual ALLOWANCE is derived as monthly x 12 by the ops price route (apps/api/src/cernia-ops-store-routes.ts writeRow), because an allowance is a per-billing-period quantity and copying the monthly number onto the annual row would sell a year for a month of usage. There is no way for an operator to state an annual allowance that is NOT 12x the monthly one, which a negotiated annual contract might want. The FEE has that escape hatch (annualPriceCents); the ALLOWANCE does not. Add annualIncludedQuantity to the route body if a real contract needs it.

history.note: Silent revenue leak CLOSED — the nightly metered-usage flush never visited store-purchase tenants. `runMeteredFlushSweep` (apps/api/src/saas-nightly-batches.ts) fanned out over `enumerateSubscriptionTenants` (apps/api/src/saas-subscription-store.ts), i.e. `SELECT DISTINCT tenant_id FROM saas_subscriptions`. The store checkout grant path (apps/api/src/store-checkout-routes.ts + the `checkout.session.completed` fan-out in apps/api/src/billing-routes.ts) calls PostgresProductCatalogStore.grantProduct, which writes `product_entitlements` and touches `saas_subscriptions` NOWHERE — so a practice that bought a product through the store had usage recorded into `billing_usage_events` and NEVER flushed to Stripe. No meter event, no invoice line, ever, while the sweep logged success. Closes docs/prds/metering-pricing-cost-chain.md R6a (risk 8.12). FIX: NEW `enumerateBillableTenants` (apps/api/src/saas-subscription-store.ts) — one SQL `SELECT tenant_id FROM saas_subscriptions UNION SELECT tenant_id FROM product_entitlements ORDER BY 1`; `runMeteredFlushSweep` is its ONLY caller. DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE PRD: R6a says to CHANGE `enumerateSubscriptionTenants` to the union. We did not — it has six other callers in saas-nightly-batches.ts (metrics :321, auto-renewal :469, expiry :542, renewal-alert schedule :616, invoice generation :1106, pricing reconcile :1292) and every one immediately opens a PostgresSubscriptionStore and reads `saas_subscriptions` ROWS, so subscription-only is the semantics they want; widening it would also make runSaasMetricsSweep persist zero-MRR/ARR snapshots for store-only tenants and corrupt the FinOps trend. DELIBERATE: NO `status` filter on product_entitlements. Cancellation here is not a status change — the Stripe path calls scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants, which sets `expires_at` and leaves status='active' — so hasActive()-style filtering would DROP a tenant who cancelled mid-month while still holding un-flushed usage from the period they DID pay for, a new leak of the same shape. The sweep only DELIVERS already-recorded usage and cannot fabricate a charge, so over-inclusion costs one empty rollup query per tenant per night while under-inclusion silently loses revenue. PROOF (watched fail first): NEW apps/api/src/metered-flush-sweep-enumeration.integration.test.ts — real Postgres (migrations 135 + 244 + 275), real PostgresUsageEventStore + createEventRecorder/createEventAggregator meter, real billing_usage_events rows. Against the unfixed subscription-only enumeration it went RED on the revenue outcome (`result.tenants` expected 2 received 1; the store tenant's 7 scribe notes reached Stripe as `undefined`); GREEN 4/4 after the UNION. Also covers UNION de-dup (a tenant in both tables is reported exactly once, not twice) and ADR-0004 per-tenant aggregation (7 and 3, never 10). Auth Plan 3 (social) — Google self-serve signup JIT-promote VERIFIED LIVE end-to-end, and two root-cause bugs fixed that had blocked it. The installer-wizard 'Continue with Google' flow reserves an 'invited' credential-less admin, redirects to Google (PKCE), and on callback exchanges the code + JIT-promotes the invited admin to 'active'. Two defects surfaced only under a real browser round-trip (unit/route tests stub the exchanger + storage, so both were invisible): (1) ENV/INFRA split-brain — apps/api/.env CERNIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL pointed at a trycloudflare tunnel that forwarded to a SECOND, Google-DISABLED apps/api instance (a parallel session's :8080 from C:\dev\cernia-fhir, google:false), so /start ran on the Google-enabled API but the OAuth callback landed on the other one → token exchange failed → wizard showed #social_error=code-exchange-failed. Resolved for dev by running the whole round-trip on http://localhost:8081 (Google client already has the localhost callback registered); .env is gitignored so this is a local-dev change only. (2) CODE — apps/api/src/index.ts promoteInvitedAdmin called socialUserStorage.update(tenantId, updated, {reference:'Device/...'}) passing the actor Reference as the 3rd positional arg, but the real StorageAdapter.update signature is (tenantId, resource, ifMatchVersionId?: string, actor?: Reference); the Reference landed in ifMatchVersionId, the adapter parseInt-ed the object to NaN and threw ConflictError (409 'request expected [object Object]'), so promotion failed AFTER a successful exchange. The narrow BuiltInUserStorage.update interface wrongly declared the 3rd param as actor and the 'as unknown as' cast hid the mismatch. FIX: builtin-user-store.ts aligns the interface with the real adapter (ifMatchVersionId? then actor?); index.ts passes undefined for the precondition (single-writer JIT promote) and the actor in the 4th slot. REVENUE LEAK CLOSED — cancellation now expires purchased product entitlements. THE DEFECT: the grant half of the Stripe flow (checkout.session.completed → opts.productCatalog.grantProduct, apps/api/src/billing-routes.ts) passes NO expiresAt, so every purchased entitlement row was written expires_at=NULL (perpetual) — and the ungrant half was never written at all. PostgresProductCatalogStore.revokeProduct (apps/api/src/product-catalog-store.ts) had ZERO production callers repo-wide; the only thing that ever removed a product_entitlements row was tenant erasure (apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts). Tier downgrade (packages/billing/src/lifecycle/tier-downgrade.ts) removes only TIER-INCLUDED products and explicitly "never silently revokes licenses". Net: a tenant who cancelled kept ambient-scribe (and every other purchased product) FOREVER. THE FIX (founder decision 2026-07-29): access works until the end of the period they already paid for, then stops — NOT immediate revocation (a clinician must never lose scribe access mid-visit, and we do not claw back time already paid for). (1) apps/api/src/product-catalog-store.ts: new scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants(expiresAt) sets expires_at on every ACTIVE + PERPETUAL (expires_at IS NULL) entitlement the tenant holds, returning the changed product ids; plus scheduleExpiry(productId, expiresAt) for the operator path. Restricting the write to NULL rows makes it idempotent under Stripe redelivery AND means it can only ever SHORTEN access, never extend it, and never claws back a product carrying its own paid term. NO SWEEPER IS NEEDED — hasActive() already evaluates status=active AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now) at READ time on every gated request. (2) apps/api/src/billing-routes.ts: new customer.subscription.deleted block sets expires_at from the event’s current_period_end (already carried on result.subscriptionSync by packages/billing/src/backends/stripe-backend.ts — no change needed there). Tenant is taken from the LOCAL subscription row via readByStripeSubscriptionId in preference to cernia_tenant_id metadata (ADR 0004), mismatch logged. Every failure is logged and swallowed so the Stripe ack is never rejected (a non-2xx makes Stripe retry forever). A null current_period_end deliberately does NOT fall back to now() — that would be the immediate revocation this change exists to avoid; it warns and defers to the operator route. (3) ProductGrantStore seam extended with an OPTIONAL scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants so existing doubles/partial wirings still compile. (4) apps/api/src/index.ts: seam WIRED to PostgresProductCatalogStore — without this the fix would be dead code, i.e. the very defect being fixed. Deliberately no syncVoiceTierFromEntitlements() call at cancel time: rows stay active until expires_at passes, so the derived voice_tier is still correct for the rest of the paid period. (5) apps/api/src/cernia-ops-entitlements-routes.ts: new POST /cernia-ops/platform/entitlements/expire (operator escape hatch for when the webhook could not set the expiry, or an immediate abuse/fraud cut-off via a past date) — requireSuperAdmin + sendPhiSafe, tenant-filtered UPDATE, ACTIVE rows only. DELIBERATELY NOT added to deriveOperation: on /cernia-ops/* the rule INVERTS (mapping it onto a type a tenant-admin’s *:admin covers would turn the hook into an allow-then-deny), and iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts excludes OPERATOR_PREFIX for exactly that reason — gate re-run green 8/8. Path uses a plain “expire” segment, not “”, to dodge the %24-vs-$ route-encoding footgun this repo has shipped before. TESTS: apps/api/src/billing-routes.test.ts +10 webhook cases (paid-period survival then cut-off, all-products fan-out, idempotent redelivery, cancel→re-purchase restores entitlement, cross-tenant isolation, store failure still ACKs 200, null current_period_end writes nothing, past_due is NOT a cancellation, unknown-subscription metadata fallback, unwired seam); apps/api/src/product-catalog-store.test.ts +15 real-Postgres cases; apps/api/src/cernia-ops-entitlements-routes.test.ts +6 real-Postgres route cases. FALSIFIED before shipping (ADR-0127): deleting the scheduleExpiryForPerpetualGrants call turned 7 webhook tests red naming the expiry date, while the three negative-control tests correctly stayed green; removing the “expires_at IS NULL” guard from the real SQL turned the idempotency + “no claw-back” tests red (a redelivery would have extended access by a year). THE AMBIENT SCRIBE BECAME PURCHASABLE. THE DEFECT (journeys.json findings[51], measured live on J01 run 2): GET /admin/store/catalog answered 200 listing phone-agent, digital-assistant, voice-language-spanish, patient-portal, api-webhooks, voice-minute, sms and email — and neither ambient-scribe nor ambient-scribe-pro. product-registry.ts carried storefront:false on both, and catalog-seed.ts LIST_PRICES had no row for either, so POST /admin/store/checkout answered 409 "ambient-scribe: unknown product". The product was gated, entitleable and UNSELLABLE: the only paths in were /dev/checkout-grant or an operator action. The 402 body meanwhile told the practice to "Purchase or contact your admin" for something with no purchase path. THE PRICE SOURCE (founder requirement): the price is NOT a literal in catalog-seed.ts. The "$149/provider/mo" on the registry entry stays a comment; an operator publishes a price through PATCH /cernia-ops/platform/store/price — super-admin only, because that route can set an OVERAGE RATE and a tenant admin who could reach it would set their own to zero (PRD R4a). Until an operator does, the catalog returns price:null + unavailable.reason="price-not-configured" and offers no checkout. There is NO default anywhere on the path, and resolveProductPrice returns null rather than inventing one. THE SHAPE COULD NOT BE EXPRESSED, SO 341 ADDS IT: catalog_prices had a single unit_amount, while every Cernia product is "a fixed fee that includes an allowance, then an overage rate" — phone-agent is documented as "$199/mo (200 voice min incl, $0.35/min over)" with the 200 living in a // comment and the $0.35 in an unrelated product:voice-minute:metered row that nothing joins to it. Per founder decision D3 (PRD docs/prds/metering-pricing-cost-chain.md R1a), migration 341 adds included_quantity / overage_rate_cents / usage_unit / quantity_unit beside unit_amount (REUSED as the fixed fee — every reader already treats it as the recurring amount). No pricing-mode enum: pure metered is (0,0,X), a flat contract is (negotiated, unlimited, n/a), and unlimited is an explicit NULL overage rate rather than a magic large number. PER-TENANT OVERRIDE + NEW ISOLATION (PRD R2a): 341 also adds tenant_id (empty string = the platform list price) and widens UNIQUE to (tenant_id,item_type,item_id,cadence) — under migration 257’s key, writing one practice’s negotiated rate would have overwritten the list price for everybody. Resolution is tenant row then platform row, first match wins; an override replaces the triple WHOLE, because a partial merge would let a negotiated fee silently inherit the list allowance and bill overage nobody agreed to. This is NEW isolation rather than preserved isolation — before 341 the table had no tenant dimension at all — so it was made structural: every PostgresCatalogPriceStore method that predates 341 is PINNED to the platform sentinel, and the tenant-aware reads are separate methods taking a required tenant id. No method returns unscoped rows, so forgetting the filter is not something a caller can do. TIER FLOOR (ADR 0035): ambient-scribe carried the comment "sandbox tier excluded (no BAA)" and NOTHING enforced it — validateCart had no floor, and a sandbox tenant was stopped only incidentally, by the absence of a price row. Publishing a price removes that accident, so ProductDef.minTier became code (starter+ for the scribe, growth+ for pro), enforced in the aggregator (card renders tier-locked, no button) AND in validateCart (409), because a cart is a JSON body a tenant admin can POST directly and hiding the card is not a control. BOTH SURFACES (CLAUDE.md): apps/admin renders the whole price ("$149.00/mo / clinician — Includes 500 notes, then $0.25 per note") plus the named unavailable reason; apps/cernia-ops price-editor.tsx gains the terms fields + a tenant field (blank = list price, the safe default — a mistyped tenant id writes a row nobody reads, whereas defaulting to a current tenant would turn a list-price edit into a single-customer discount). LIVE EVIDENCE, intent channel only: RED at github/main 9e1ef20f reproduces the exact eight-product list (docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/store-scribe-red.json); GREEN 23/23 (store-scribe-green.json) across two stacks over one database. Both stacks port-to-DB pairing-checked by writing THROUGH the port and requiring the row PRESENT in the queried database and ABSENT from the decoy database apps/api/.env names. SETTLEMENT RODE THE REAL CASCADE, not /dev/checkout-grant: a signed checkout.session.completed delivered to POST /billing/webhook/stripe, HMAC-verified by StripeBillingBackend, then the billing-routes.ts cart fan-out to productCatalog.grantProduct + provisioningOrchestrator.enqueue. The resulting entitlement row carries grant_ref="cs_<session>_ambient-scribe" rather than a "dev-checkout:" ref, which is what tells the two paths apart. A TAMPERED signature was refused 401 in the same step, so the signed 200 means something. The Stripe-hosted payment page itself is an external gate this run cannot drive; both Cernia-side legs are real. CONTROLS: the practice that purchased reaches /scribe/sessions; a practice that did not is still refused 402 product-not-entitled (the gate was not widened); Harborview saw its negotiated $99/2,000 notes/$0.10 while Meridian saw the $149/500/$0.25 list price (ADR 0004); a tenant admin was refused on the price route; a sandbox practice was refused 409 on a direct cart POST. SCREENS: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/screens/store-scribe-0{1..6}*.png. THE OPS PRICE EDITOR LOOKED BROKEN, AND THE SCRIBE GOT ITS REAL PRICE. THE DEFECT (this stage's own remaining bullet, and reproduced on the wire against github/main before the fix — docs/status/evidence/scribe-pricing/cadence-red.json): PATCH /cernia-ops/platform/store/price wrote one row, `product:<id>:monthly`. The storefront opens on ANNUAL (apps/admin/src/app/admin/store/page.tsx useState('annual')) and store-catalog-aggregator.ts looks a price up by EXACT cadence, so an operator published $29.99 and a tenant admin opening the store was told "Pricing for this product has not been published yet" until they toggled to Monthly. The RED run measured it: two catalog_prices rows, both monthly; C2 and C4 (annual, platform and negotiated) came back unavailable.reason="price-not-configured" with HTTP 200. Nothing caught it because the prior journey (store-scribe-journey.mts) reads ?cadence=monthly on every call and every unit test in apps/cernia-ops/src/lib/store-api.test.ts injects a fake fetch. THE FIX: one call now writes BOTH cadences — an explicit annualPriceCents when the operator states a negotiated annual rate, annualFromMonthly(monthly) (the platform-wide 10%-off ladder in catalog-seed.ts) when they leave it blank, so a blank field can no longer produce a MISSING annual price. Row ids carry both the tenant and the cadence, so a negotiated rate cannot overwrite the list price and the annual row cannot overwrite the monthly one. THE PRICE (founder decision, 2026-07-31): ambient-scribe is $29.99 PER CLINICIAN per month — 2_999 in catalog-seed.ts LIST_PRICES with quantityUnit 'clinician' in the new PRODUCT_TERMS map, so the card reads "$29.99/mo / clinician" and not a flat practice-wide fee — annual $323.89, and NO included allowance and NO overage rate, because every note is billed individually and the per-note rate is cost-plus-margin off a number the founder has deliberately not set yet. The "$149/provider/mo" comment in product-registry.ts was a demo placeholder that had already been quoted as authoritative in docs/prds/metering-pricing-cost-chain.md D2; it is corrected in place. THE PER-UNIT POLICY (same founder decision): a note must never be billed at zero, so per_unit_price = max(floor_price, measured_cost x (1 + margin)). Both inputs are OPERATOR CONFIGURATION, not constants — migration 343 product_usage_pricing (one row per tenant+product+unit, tenant_id '' = the platform default, the same keying catalog_prices uses so a negotiated policy cannot overwrite the default), PATCH/GET /cernia-ops/platform/store/usage-pricing (super-admin — a practice that could reach it would set its own floor to zero), and two more fields in the ops price editor. Both ship UNSET, and unset resolves to `unresolvable`, never to zero. THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: a floor silently rescues a broken cost chain. If the cost pipeline reports $0.00 because it cannot price a model — which is the live condition today, o4_llm_cost_ledger.usd_cents is 0 on all 454 rows in journey_a because the pricing table does not know claude-haiku-4 — the floor kicks in, the invoice looks right, and nobody learns the platform is blind to its own costs. So apps/api/src/per-unit-price-resolver.ts returns TWO independent verdicts per charge: `basis` (cost-plus-margin | cost-below-floor | cost-unpriced) and `costConfidence` (measured | zero-indeterminate | unpriced). Same money, different diagnosis, and they never collapse. A priced zero is billable but never called healthy, because free self-hosted inference and a blind cost chain are the same integer from there — the producer is the only thing that can tell them apart, and that seam is left explicitly for the cost-chain work. ALSO FIXED IN PASSING: the price route conflicted on the surrogate `id` rather than migration 341's real unique key (tenant_id, item_type, item_id, cadence). A row for the same tuple created under a different id — by an older seed, by dev:stripe-bootstrap, by a fixture — missed the id target, hit the unique index anyway, and answered the operator with a 500 instead of a price update. Surfaced by test S11, which prices a product whose seeded row is keyed `cp-pa-monthly`. PROOF: over the wire against real Postgres, RED then GREEN, all four cadence x scope combinations — platform x monthly $29.99, platform x annual $323.89, negotiated x monthly $19.99, negotiated x annual $215.89 — plus an ADR-0004 control (a second growth practice reads the LIST price in both cadences and never the negotiated one) and a check that no card states a per-note rate. Port/DB pairing proven by a write THROUGH the port found in scribe_price and absent from the decoy. Screens driven in a real browser: the ops editor writing the price with a live operator cookie + CSRF, and the tenant storefront rendering $323.89/yr / clinician on its default cadence and $29.99/mo / clinician on the toggle, with ambient-scribe-pro still honestly unpriced. Artifacts: docs/status/evidence/scribe-pricing/ (cadence-red.json, cadence-green.json, ops-price-editor-saved.png, store-card-annual.png, store-card-monthly.png); runner apps/api/scripts/store-price-cadence-journey.mts.

THE AMBIENT SCRIBE BECAME PURCHASABLE ON A USAGE BASIS, AND 'TEMPORARY' BECAME A COLUMN INSTEAD OF A COMMENT. Founder instruction: 'We can set it later in ops portal. Just use temporary floor price. Even the margin % can be set later.' Two things were missing: migration 343's floor_price_cents + margin_ppm shipped UNSET (so resolvePerUnitCharge answered `unresolvable` for every note), and NOTHING CALLED THE RESOLVER — PR #758 shipped it explicitly as an empty seam. Both are now closed.  (1) THE SEED, AND WHY IT IS NOT A CONSTANT. NEW migration 346_usage_pricing_provenance_scribe_seed.sql seeds the platform default at floor 10c / margin 400000ppm (40%) for (tenant_id='', ambient-scribe, note). There is NO number in TypeScript anywhere — the resolver still reads only the database, so an operator write beats the seed by construction rather than by convention. The seed is `ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT product_usage_pricing_tenant_product_unit_key DO NOTHING` on migration 343's REAL unique key (not the surrogate `id` — that is the #758 bug one table over), which makes seeding FIRST-write-wins: a redeploy, a restore or a manual re-apply cannot walk an operator's number back. Every statement in the file is guarded, so the whole migration is re-runnable.  (2) PROVENANCE, so a placeholder can never be read as a decision. NEW column product_usage_pricing.provenance ('seeded-default' | 'operator-set', CHECK-constrained). Its DEFAULT is the CAUTIOUS direction — 'seeded-default' — so a future writer that forgets to set it produces a row labelled provisional (a badge an operator clears by re-saving) rather than one that presents a machine-written number as a human decision; rows that existed before the migration are backfilled to 'operator-set' because the ops PATCH route was their only ever writer. PostgresUsagePricingStore.upsert now stamps 'operator-set' UNCONDITIONALLY (not a parameter), so a caller can neither save a number and leave it labelled a seed nor pass itself off as one. The value travels: GET /cernia-ops/platform/store/usage-pricing returns provenance + a server-authored `caveat` string, the ops price editor prefills the stored policy and renders a 'Seeded default' warning from it, and resolvePerUnitCharge carries `policyProvenance` onto the charge so a BILL LINE priced off the seed says so. THE THREE VERDICTS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT COLLAPSED: `basis` (which arm of the max won), `costConfidence` (was the cost input believable), `policyProvenance` (did a human choose the policy) — a seeded policy over a measured cost and an operator policy over a blind cost chain are different problems with different fixes, and both produce a plausible number.  (3) THE RESOLVER GOT ITS FIRST PRODUCTION CALLER. NEW apps/api/src/scribe-note-pricer.ts: session -> ScribeCostPerNoteStore.bySession (NEW method; the session is the note's durable identity and exists at draft time, whereas composition_ref does not) -> measuredCostFromNoteCost -> PostgresUsagePricingStore.resolveForTenant -> resolvePerUnitCharge -> UsageMeter.record, wired into POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$draft fail-soft (the Composition is already persisted; an unmetered note is recoverable revenue, a lost note is not) and idempotent on the SESSION id (a redraft is not a second sale, so the price is a snapshot taken at first draft). It reuses the SAME @cernia/billing recorder as the voice-persona meter, so the invoicing flush rolls it into a tenant bill line with no second pipeline. THE JUDGEMENT IT REFUSES TO FUDGE: `compute` and `storage` are `not-attributed-per-note` on every note, so assembleNoteCost marks EVERY note unpriced and every note therefore bills the floor with basis='cost-unpriced', healthy=false. Summing pricedLowerBound and calling it the cost would have produced a confident number that is too small in the direction that flatters margin AND flipped basis to 'cost-below-floor' — i.e. the platform asserting it can see its own costs at the exact moment it cannot. Not done; the honest reading rides on the bill line and clears itself when the probes get a runtime caller.  (4) TWO LATENT DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED ON THE WAY. (a) PARTIAL UPDATE: the PATCH route's contract said 'omitting a field leaves whatever is stored alone' but the SQL assigned both columns unconditionally, so saving only a floor NULLed the margin — and a half-set policy is `unresolvable`, so the product went un-billable the moment anyone tried to price it. Harmless while both shipped unset; a live un-sale once they are seeded. Now three-state (number sets / null clears / undefined leaves alone) and the response READS THE ROW BACK rather than echoing the request. (b) WRITE-ONLY EDITOR: the ops price panel never read the stored policy, so the floor/margin boxes rendered blank whatever was stored — an operator could not see the seeded numbers they were being asked to replace, and could 'save' believing they had confirmed a price they had never seen. It now prefills on open. (c) A note with NO cost components at all was reported `priced` with total 0 by assembleNoteCost (nothing blocked completeness because there was nothing to block it), i.e. 'measured, and free'; the producer now refuses it.  LIVE PROOF (intent channel, real apps/api on :8123 against real Postgres scribe_seed on :5433). PORT IDENTITY PROVEN BEFORE TRUSTING ANY RESPONSE: a marker policy written THROUGH the API (product 'port-identity-probe-8123', floor 4242) was read back FROM scribe_seed and is ABSENT from the decoy scribe_price (count 0). PURCHASE TO PRICED NOTE: GET /admin/store/catalog renders the scribe card at $29.99/clinician/mo state='available' (after the tenant is moved to growth — the ADR-0035 starter floor is enforced); entitlement granted and visible on GET /admin/entitlements + product_entitlements; POST /scribe/sessions -> /consent -> POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$draft -> 201 with a real Composition AND a `usage` block reporting centsPerUnit=10, basis='cost-unpriced', costConfidence='unpriced', healthy=false, policySource='platform', policyProvenance='seeded-default'; the durable charge landed in billing_usage_events as kind='feature-use', featureId='ambient-scribe', idempotency_key='scribe-note:<sessionId>', with basis/healthy/blockedBy/policyProvenance/centsPerUnit in the body metadata.  THREE CONTROLS, ALL LIVE: (i) OVERRIDE BEATS SEED — PATCH 18c/55% through the ops route moved the row to 18/550000/'operator-set' and the GET's `caveat` went null; (ii) RE-SEED DOES NOT CLOBBER — re-running migration 346 verbatim against the live DB printed `INSERT 0 0`, left 18/550000/'operator-set' intact and produced no duplicate platform row; (iii) UNPRICED STILL SAYS UNPRICED — the note charged the floor and reported basis='cost-unpriced', never 'cost-below-floor'. A SECOND note drafted after the override billed 18c stamped 'operator-set' while the first stayed at 10c 'seeded-default', and a REDRAFT of the first added no second line (one row per idempotency key).  NOT PROVEN LIVE, stated plainly: no LLM provider on this stack is usable (OPENAI_API_KEY returns 429 billing_not_active, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, no Ollama), so the drafting call was served by a local OpenAI-compatible STUB behind the gateway's supported self-hosted `ollama` provider. That substitutes the MODEL ONLY — HTTP $draft, the Composition write, llm_audit_events, o4_llm_cost_ledger, the pricer and billing_usage_events are all the real path — and the note text is not clinically meaningful and is not claimed to be. STT did not run either (a persisted transcript was reused, which is the normal U6 path), so no Deepgram invoice was incurred or observed. POST /admin/store/checkout could not create a session ('missing-price: no price id for product:ambient-scribe:monthly') because stripe:sync-prices has never run here — an external Stripe gate; settlement was driven through POST /dev/checkout-grant, the documented stand-in, which writes the same product_entitlements row via the same PostgresProductCatalogStore.grantProduct.  ADR-0127: @cernia/api typecheck=0, build=0, lint 63 errors = the documented carry-forward baseline EXACTLY with ZERO in any touched file; @cernia/cernia-ops-portal typecheck=0, lint clean (1 pre-existing autofocus warning on the login page). Targeted tests 66/66 across five files: NEW scribe-note-pricer.test.ts (13, incl. both floor arms proven distinguishable at identical money, and the fact that at the seeded numbers 7.06c x 1.40 rounds to exactly the 10c floor so basis is 'cost-plus-margin' — the floor is a backstop, not the price), NEW usage-pricing-store.test.ts (8, REAL Postgres, covering all three controls plus the real-unique-key conflict target), per-unit-price-resolver 13, cernia-ops-store-routes 19 (U01 REVERSED from 'ships with NO policy' to 'ships with a SEEDED policy, labelled as one'; U03 split into omit-preserves + explicit-null-clears; its bootstrap now loads migration 346), scribe-cost-per-note 13. ADR-0140 gate: OK, 276 tenant-scoped tables all classified; migration 346 declares `product_usage_pricing = ERASE`, agreeing with ADR_0140_CASCADE.  WHERE THE FOUNDER CHANGES THESE TWO NUMBERS: apps/cernia-ops -> Platform -> Store -> the ambient-scribe row -> expand the terms disclosure -> '$ floor / unit' and 'margin %'. Takes effect immediately, no deploy, and stamps provenance='operator-set' which removes the provisional banner.

tracks.name: External Integrations & per-tenant config
tracks.description: Per-tenant credentials + vendor backends the voice agent talks to (Twilio for telephony, Deepgram for STT, ElevenLabs for TTS, OpenAI/Anthropic for LLM). Also covers self-serve tenant provisioning + per-tenant workflow customization. Without this layer every tenant shares the platform's trial credentials and can't customize the assistant.

stages.name: Tenant secrets — per-tenant credential storage
stages.rationale: Each tenant must paste their own Twilio/Deepgram/ElevenLabs/LLM credentials so calls bill to their accounts. Plaintext is encrypted at rest with envelope encryption (AES-256-GCM); the resolver falls back to platform-level env vars when no per-tenant override exists.

baseline.summary: No per-tenant credential storage. The voice agent's Twilio/Deepgram/ElevenLabs/OpenAI/Anthropic keys came from process.env only. Every tenant in a multi-tenant deploy would share the same vendor accounts — billing attribution impossible, key rotation per tenant impossible, white-glove onboarding meant editing the platform-level env.

current.summary: Shipped end-to-end. Migration 046_tenant_secrets (composite-PK (tenant_id, provider), opaque ciphertext column, JSONB metadata). TenantSecretResolver in @cernia/core with NoopSecretCipher (dev) + AesGcmSecretCipher (prod). apps/api boot now wires KyselyTenantSecretStore (secrets survive restart) + refuses to start in production when CERNIA_TENANT_SECRET_KEY/KID is unset or wrong length — TenantSecretBootError thrown loud. PUT/DELETE handlers emit structured tenant-secret.write/delete IAM audit rows. KMS rotation runbook (docs/operations/runbooks/tenant-secret-key-rotation.md) covers cadence, rehearsal in staging, multi-key decrypt window, re-encrypt job, and rollback.
