history.note: LIVE OUTBOUND PSTN CALLS surfaced + closed TWO real telephony bugs that only a genuine call could expose (the inbound trial call could not reach the /voice path; outbound + a keypress past the trial preamble does). Setup: same cloudflared tunnel + operator trial Twilio account; destination +13029834679 added as a Verified Caller ID (trial accounts can only dial verified numbers); outbound placed via POST /telephony/outbound (real JWT → RBAC deriveOperation /telephony/outbound→TelephonyCall → caller-id allowlist assertOwnedByTenant(+12402444312) → real Twilio Calls API → CallSid → call.outbound.placed audit → call_sessions row → 200 — all proven live). BUG 1 (apps/api/src/telephony-routes.ts, POST /telephony/twilio/voice): the handler resolved the tenant from the To number — correct for INBOUND (To = our number) but WRONG for OUTBOUND, where Twilio fetches the TwiML *after* we placed the call and the tenant-owned leg is From (To is the external party). So every outbound TwiML callback resolved tenantId=null → call.unknown-number → no dialog (observed live: CallSid CA0f96c6… fetched /voice after a keypress but bailed to unknown-number). FIX: branch on body.Direction; for outbound-* resolve tenant from From, mark the existing outbound session answered, emit call.outbound.answered, return Connect/Stream TwiML (skip the inbound _dispatchInbound path). LIVE-VERIFIED on a fresh call (CallSid CA41d57c…): call.outbound.answered now fires with tenantId=22222222-… resolved from From, and the call_sessions row flips ringing→in-progress with answered_at set. BUG 2 (packages/telephony/src/backends/twilio-backend.ts placeOutboundCall): StatusCallbackEvent was sent COMMA-separated ('initiated,ringing,answered,completed'); Twilio's Calls API requires the call-progress event list to be SPACE-separated and parses a comma-joined value as one invalid token → subscribes to NO events → the StatusCallback never fires → outbound sessions never reach 'completed' (confirmed live: 0 /status POSTs for any of 3 outbound calls, while inbound /status worked because that comes from the phone NUMBER's own StatusCallback config, not this param). FIX: 'initiated ringing answered completed' (space-separated) + doc-comment corrected. ADR-0127: @cernia/api typecheck=0 + telephony-routes.test.ts 18/18 (added an outbound-direction regression test asserting tenant-from-From + call.outbound.answered + session direction stays outbound); @cernia/telephony typecheck=0 + twilio-backend.test.ts 26/26 (2 assertions updated to the space-separated form). The /voice fix is LIVE (apps/api hot-reloaded by tsx watch); the StatusCallbackEvent fix is unit-verified and goes live on the next @cernia/telephony rebuild + api restart. Secrets used as launch-time env overrides only; trial account = no BAA → synthetic/non-PHI calls only. UPDATE (live re-verify, same day): the BUG 2 comma→space change was INSUFFICIENT — Twilio rejected the space-joined value too, emitting notification 21626 'invalid statusCallbackEvents' on CallSid CA1bac94… (a live call surfaced this; unit tests never could). TRUE ROOT CAUSE: Twilio's Calls REST API requires StatusCallbackEvent as a REPEATED form param (StatusCallbackEvent=initiated&StatusCallbackEvent=ringing&…), not any single joined string. FINAL FIX in packages/telephony/src/backends/twilio-backend.ts buildTwilioVoiceClient.calls.create: split the whitespace event string and params.append() each event. LIVE-CONFIRMED on CallSid CAf4ebe5…: /status POSTs 1→5 (initiated/ringing/answered/completed all delivered), Twilio notifications now [] (21626 gone), audit chain call.outbound.placed→answered→ended (tenant 22222222), call_sessions row reached status=completed duration_seconds=4 — the outbound voice lifecycle now closes end-to-end on a genuine PSTN call. twilio-backend.test.ts 26/26 (added a getAll('StatusCallbackEvent') repeated-param assertion); @cernia/telephony typecheck=0. Also added a wiring cross-reference comment at the outbound-backend construction in apps/api/src/index.ts.

LIVE INBOUND PSTN CALL verified end-to-end through a public tunnel — the genuine-call half of the Wave-E telephony path that unit/synthetic tests could not exercise. Setup: cloudflared quick tunnel (https://sailing-multimedia-maple-nearly.trycloudflare.com) → local apps/api :8080 booted with CERNIA_TELEPHONY_BACKEND=twilio + the operator's real account (AC2ca625…, trial) + CERNIA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=tunnel; the number +12402444312 (PN3eba5f6…) registered in tenant_phone_numbers (tenant 22222222-… purpose voice-agent) with its Twilio VoiceUrl + StatusCallback pointed at the tunnel via the Twilio REST API. RESULT: a real inbound call (CallSid CAed80803a93606fef5a64aac9edee9561, from +13029834679, status=completed, 13s) hit POST /telephony/twilio/status through the tunnel; our handler VALIDATED the Twilio HMAC-SHA1 signature against the reconstructed https URL (Host header preserved by cloudflared), emitted a call.ended audit (toNumberHash 067e8a95…d6ac93 — byte-identical to the hash of +12402444312, proving it was our number; status=completed, durationSeconds=13) and returned 204. Twilio's own Calls.json log corroborates the same CallSid/from/duration. This proves the live chain: real PSTN → Twilio → public tunnel → Fastify route → signature validation → audit → 204. The /voice (media) webhook did NOT fire on this inbound call — only /status did (log: 2 voice POSTs = both the synthetic signed test [valid→200+call_sessions row; bad-sig→403], 1 status POST = the real call) — because on a Twilio TRIAL account inbound calls play the mandatory ~13s trial greeting and the custom inbound VoiceUrl isn't proxied as on a paid account; NOT a handler defect (the /voice path is independently proven by the real-Twilio-signed synthetic webhook → 200 + persisted CAtuntest… session). REMAINING for live /voice media on a genuine inbound call: an UPGRADED (non-trial) Twilio account, and a signed Twilio BAA before any real patient audio is routed (trial = no BAA → synthetic/non-PHI only). Secrets used as launch-time env overrides only; never written to a committed file.

history.note: Deepgram STT VALIDATED live against the operator's real key — AND fixed a real bug that meant STT produced ZERO output in production. (1) BUG FIXED (apps/api/src/deepgram-ws-transport.ts): the ws 'message' handler gated on `typeof data === 'string'`, but the `ws` library delivers Deepgram's JSON TEXT frames as a Node Buffer (isBinary=false), so EVERY transcript/VAD/error message was silently dropped — STT never emitted a single transcript. The unit test gave false confidence because it called onJsonMessage() directly with a string, bypassing the ws delivery path. Fix: new handleSocketMessage(data, isBinary) decodes any non-binary frame to UTF-8 (Buffer | Buffer[] | ArrayBuffer | string); binary frames ignored. (2) Live proof: new apps/api/src/deepgram-stt.live.test.ts — a TTS→STT round trip in the Twilio telephony format (ElevenLabs Sarah → ulaw_8000 → DeepgramSttBackend encoding=mulaw/8000 over the real WS) — Deepgram transcribed 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' at 0.998 confidence. Diagnosed via direct WS probes that confirmed the full backend query (nova-2-medical + redact + no_retention, both finish modes) transcribes correctly, isolating the defect to the transport's frame-type guard. (3) Regression guard: 3 new unit tests exercise handleSocketMessage with a Buffer text frame / string / binary (the path the old test missed). Gated on ELEVENLABS_API_KEY + DEEPGRAM_API_KEY (skipIf). ADR-0127: @cernia/api typecheck=0, build=0, transport+live tests 18/18, changed-file lint clean (1 pre-existing close() require-await baseline). Inbound transcription now works end-to-end on the operator's free-tier Deepgram key.

ElevenLabs TTS FULLY VALIDATED live on the free tier — real μ-law-8000 phone audio confirmed end-to-end, AND a real telephony bug fixed. (1) Free-tier voice: researched + probed the operator's key — Library voices and OLD defaults (Rachel 21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM) return 402 paid_plan_required, but NEW default voices work free via API; verified HTTP 200 for Sarah (EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL, female), Laura, Lily, Jessica, Will (Aria is library-gated). Live test now defaults to Sarah. (2) BUG FIXED (packages/speech/src/backends/elevenlabs-tts-backend.ts): output_format was sent in the request BODY, which ElevenLabs's /v1/text-to-speech/:id/stream endpoint IGNORES — it silently returned its mp3_44100_128 default (observed: an 'ID3'-tagged MP3, head 49443304). For the telephony path that is catastrophic: Twilio Media Streams expect raw μ-law 8 kHz and would have received MP3 → broken call audio. Moved output_format to the query string; the live synth now returns real μ-law (head ff ff 7e … — 0xFF silence + speech samples, 16 KB, no ID3). Updated the 2 backend unit tests that asserted body.output_format → assert the query param + body absence (6/6 green). The live test's format guard now keys off the ID3 signature only (μ-law leading silence 0xFF would false-trip an MPEG frame-sync check). ADR-0127: @cernia/speech typecheck=0/lint=0/build=0/6 tests; @cernia/api typecheck=0, live test 2/2. This bug would have shipped silently — the gated live smoke test caught it. The agent now speaks real phone audio on the operator's free tier; production voice is selected per-tenant via voice_tenant_config.persona.

LIVE ElevenLabs TTS smoke test shipped + run against the operator's real API key (apps/api/src/elevenlabs-tts.live.test.ts). Gated like the Stripe live-sandbox test (describe.skipIf on ELEVENLABS_API_KEY); mirrors the telephony path exactly — constructs ElevenLabsTtsBackend (model eleven_flash_v2_5) over the production buildElevenLabsFetchTransportFactory() and synthesizes a short phrase at format 'mulaw-8k' (→ output_format ulaw_8000, what Twilio Media Streams require). Contract assertion: a correct key + request shape + endpoint yields EITHER real μ-law audio (usable voice + adequate plan) OR a clean HTTP 402 paid_plan_required; only 401/400/422/5xx fail (real drift). VERIFIED live (2/2 green): the operator's key AUTHENTICATES and has TTS access, and our request reaches the /v1/text-to-speech/:voiceId/stream endpoint correctly — proven by a clean 402, not a 401/400. FINDING: on a FREE ElevenLabs tier, the API rejects ALL stock/Library voices ('Free users cannot use library voices via the API') — confirmed for both the operator's chosen Library voice (g6xIsTj2HwM6VR4iXFCw) and the canonical default Rachel (21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM). So free-tier API TTS is unusable with stock voices; producing real μ-law audio needs a paid plan (any tier) or the tenant's own voice. The byte-level μ-law assertion (incl. an MP3-default guard against the /stream endpoint ignoring output_format) is dormant until then. CERNIA_ELEVENLABS_TEST_VOICE_ID env override lets CI point at a usable voice. The .env key + CERNIA_SPEECH_TTS=elevenlabs are set so the boot path builds the real backend. ra-tts-4 voiceId-routing followup closed — PerTenantTtsRouter now applies a per-tenant voice id override. On each synthesize() call, when the tenant secret resolved source='tenant', the router overrides TtsOpts.voiceId with the secret's metadata.defaultVoiceId (preferred) or vendorAccountId (fallback) before delegating to the per-tenant ElevenLabs backend; default fall-through preserves the caller's persona voiceId unchanged. ra-tts-4 closed — PerTenantTtsRouter shipped in apps/api/src/per-tenant-tts-router.ts. Wraps the default TextToSpeech backend (built at boot from ELEVENLABS_API_KEY env var) with a tenant-aware adapter that consults PerTenantSpeechCredentials.resolveElevenLabs(tenantId) on each synthesize() call. OnboardingFullProvisioner retry: the resolveExisting error-conflation half is FIXED (2026-08-03, this PR — a storage outage no longer masquerades as a permanent slug conflict; see history). RESIDUE, structural: the durable provisioning_runs row is written LAST. apps/api/src/onboarding-full-provisioner.ts runs fhir.provision (:449) → startTrial (:490) → grants (:529) → enqueueProvisioning (:735). A first attempt that dies anywhere in steps 1-3 therefore leaves ZERO provisioning_runs rows, so the U3 orchestrator retry surface cannot pick it up: POST /admin/entitlements/:productId/$retry-provisioning (apps/api/src/entitlements-routes.ts:117-134) only re-queues EXISTING rows, and it needs an authenticated tenant principal the stranded admin cannot produce (their User exists but the session never completed). Fix shape: enqueue a durable run row (or a `create-tenant` step) BEFORE step 1 so early failures are retryable by the standard worker rather than by hand. Not blocked externally — deferred here only because reordering the provisioning steps deserves its own change with its own migration + replay tests.

Deepgram no-heal — REMEDIATION FLOW still absent (re-verified 2026-08-03: repo-wide grep for "reprovision" returns exactly ONE hit, the aspirational JSDoc at apps/api/src/deepgram-project-provisioner.ts:102; "clearDeepgram" returns zero). A tenant whose deepgram_project_id is set but whose tenant_secrets.deepgram row is gone cannot recover: ensureProject() short-circuits on existingProjectId with no network call and never re-saves a key (:106-116), and the store CANNOT clear the id — tenant-external-resources-store.ts:153 upserts with COALESCE(EXCLUDED.deepgram_project_id, existing), i.e. merge-only, with no clear/delete method. Needs: (a) clearDeepgramProject(tenantId) on TenantExternalResourcesStore (a plain UPDATE … SET deepgram_project_id = NULL — the COALESCE upsert structurally cannot express it); (b) a PLATFORM-OPERATOR route (apps/cernia-ops surface per CLAUDE.md persona rules — cross-tenant remediation, not tenant self-serve), e.g. POST /cernia-ops/tenants/:id/$reprovision-deepgram, plus its iam-route-guards deriveOperation entry; (c) delete the stale tenant_secrets deepgram row so the next ensureProject writes cleanly. The (a)-(c) work is pure local code and is NOT externally blocked. What IS permanently external: Deepgram has no key-retrieval endpoint, so true self-heal is impossible, and the orphaned project must be revoked by a human in the Deepgram console. Do this before Card 5 fail-closed turns the condition into a hard failure for production tenants.

THE A2P 10DLC / REAL-TWILIO-CREDENTIALS GATE (merged 2026-08-03 from four separate bullets that were all waiting on this one external event — SMS-verified signup, A2P status reconciliation, the 10DLC send gate, and E911/A2P-on-every-number). All four code paths are BUILT, tested and flag-gated; none can be switched on until Twilio A2P 10DLC registration is approved and real per-tenant subaccount credentials exist. In dependency order: (1) A2P-status reconciliation must be able to mark rows approved FIRST — apps/api/src/a2p-status-reconciler.ts (reconcileA2pRegistrations + scheduleA2pReconciler, boot + every A2P_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS, default 15m; queries Twilio per-tenant with that tenant's subaccount creds via a2p-registrar.queryStatus — campaign→brand for 10DLC, /v1/Tollfree/Verifications for toll-free; APPROVED/VERIFIED→approved, FAILED/REJECTED/BLOCKED→rejected; refreshes smsComplianceGate on approve; 20+17 tests) returns nothing real without live creds. (2) THEN flip CERNIA_ENFORCE_10DLC=1 per-env to arm the send gate — apps/api/src/sms-compliance-gate-boot.ts feeds a TenDlcRegistry from approved tenant_messaging_registration rows and is consulted via the NotificationService smsPreSendHook (the chokepoint for appointment confirm/reminder SMS from the tenant number; OTP/Twilio-Verify bypasses NotificationService and is exempt); default OFF = advisory log, fail-OPEN on read errors; 15+4 tests. Flipping it BEFORE (1) works would block every tenant SMS. stages.name: Per-tenant workflow customization
stages.rationale: Different customers want different things: SNF wants 'medication-pickup-reminder' but not 'cancel-appointment'; pain clinic wants a custom intake script; pediatric clinic wants distinct red-flag thresholds. The voice agent must be configurable per tenant — not forked per tenant.

Remaining refinement: map the developer_portal product onto the saas-platform tier matrix (@cernia/saas-platform) so the entitlement is auto-granted by Growth+ tier rather than only via an explicit product grant; today entitlement is per-tenant product-grant driven. DECISION-GATED (2026-07-12 audit): this is NOT a mechanical mapping — it CONFLICTS with the current product-registry design. developer_portal is deliberately tierFeature:null in apps/api/src/product-registry.ts (a paid add-on, same as marketplace_access + api_access), and public-store-catalog-routes.ts:67 documents the rule explicitly: "tierFeature is null — add-ons are never bundled into a tier; they are bought." The tier-inclusion mechanism ALREADY works (store-catalog-aggregator.ts:62 grants any product whose non-null tierFeature is in the tier feature set), so auto-granting developer_portal at Growth+ would require giving it a tierFeature and adding that to Growth+ features — i.e. GIVING AWAY a monetizable add-on to a tier. That is a pricing/packaging (bundle-vs-a-la-carte) FOUNDER decision, not code work. Until that decision is made, product-grant-driven entitlement is correct-as-designed, not a gap.

(2) Cross-tenant lookup: NEW apps/api/src/api-key-lookup.ts PgApiKeyLookup.byPrefix() queries the live `resources` table on the STORED generated column apikey_secret_prefix with NO tenant filter (the token is the sole credential; tenant is derived AFTER the match) — safe because secretPrefix has 60 bits of entropy + a platform-wide uniqueness constraint and ApiKey is a credential resource, NOT PHI (CLAUDE.md invariant 5). recordUsage() writes lastUsedAt by id, best-effort/non-fatal. (3) principalResolver branch: apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts PrincipalResolverDeps gains an optional apiKeyVerifier; a Bearer/cookie token starting with cernia_pk_ is verified as an API key (cross-tenant prefix lookup + constant-time scrypt verifyPassword + status/expiry gates), the tenant is read from the key's urn:cernia:tenant meta.tag, and the principal is built via the SAME resolvePrincipalFromClaims so RBAC/RoleBindings apply identically (authVia='api-key'). A cernia_pk_ token NEVER falls through to the JWT verifier: null verify → 401, no verifier wired → 401. The JWT Bearer path is byte-unchanged (regression test A4). (4) $revoke + $rotate: apps/api/src/admin-api-key-routes.ts adds tenant-admin-gated POST /admin/api-keys/:id/$revoke (status=revoked + revokedBy/revokedAt, idempotent, cross-tenant id → 404) and POST /admin/api-keys/:id/$rotate (mints a new verifiable secret for the same principal/name, revokes the old with reason='rotated', returns the new secret once with no-store headers). Boot wiring: apps/api/src/index.ts constructs DefaultApiKeyVerifier(PgApiKeyLookup(db)) injected into registerRbacHook so EVERY authed route honors API keys, and passes the tenant-scoped storage to adminApiKeyRoutes for revoke/rotate. Tests: NEW api-key-lookup.test.ts (6, real Postgres :5433 via createMigratedDatabaseFixture — cross-tenant byPrefix, unknown/soft-deleted→null, recordUsage), NEW admin-api-key-routes.test.ts (8 — format-reconciliation round-trip, revoke idempotent + revoked-key-no-longer-verifies, rotate, non-admin 403 / cross-tenant 404), + 6 API-key-branch cases in iam-route-guards.test.ts (seeded-RoleBinding authenticates with right roles, revoked→401, expired→401, JWT regression, no-verifier→401, unknown-prefix→401). ADR-0127: @cernia/api typecheck=0; the 47 tests across the 3 files (33 iam + 8 admin + 6 lookup) all green; changed source files lint-clean (package-wide 314 pre-existing baseline lint errors in unrelated files are carry-forward, unchanged). FINDING: the dev `cernia` DB on :5433 holds 9 ApiKey rows all in the OLD cernia_pk_<8 hex> format (e.g. cernia_pk_9b42e3a9, no _ separator) — these dev artifacts stop authenticating under the reconciled verifier (their plaintext was never recoverable); no key migration needed on a pre-launch system. Files: apps/api/src/admin-api-key-routes.ts, apps/api/src/api-key-lookup.ts, apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts, apps/api/src/index.ts + the 3 colocated *.test.ts.

Release 3 / T2 follow-up — three live-path bugs the T2 unit suite missed (it mocked RBAC + seeded the tenant tag) FIXED so self-serve API keys actually work end-to-end against the running stack. Bug A (RBAC fail-closed 403): deriveOperation (apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts) had NO mapping for /admin/api-keys/* custom-verb routes, so the global RBAC hook fell through to the {*,*} catch-all and 403'd a tenant-admin BEFORE the route's own isAdmin check ran. Added 4 mappings → write:ApiKey: $generate-secret, $issue, :id/$revoke, :id/$rotate. Bug B (UI-created keys never authenticate, 401): the admin UI creates ApiKeys by POSTing the resource, but storage scopes tenancy by COLUMN and does NOT stamp meta.tag urn:cernia:tenant, so the verifier failed closed ('API key is not tenant-scoped'). NEW server-side POST /admin/api-keys/$issue (apps/api/src/admin-api-key-routes.ts) issues via DefaultApiKeyIssuer, which stamps the tag from the AUTHED principal's tenantId (SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE — never client body); defaults the key principal to the caller so it inherits the caller's RoleBindings; tolerates empty/{} bodies; returns {secret, apiKey} once with no-store headers. Bug C (FHIR auth layer rejects api keys): T2 wired apiKeyVerifier into registerRbacHook ONLY, but @cernia/server's FHIR routes (GET /ApiKey, /Patient, …) have a SEPARATE auth preHandler (createAuthMiddleware → identityProvider.authenticate) that only knew JWTs — so an api key got 'Token malformed' (401) on any FHIR route even after passing the RBAC hook. FIXED by composing the FHIR-router identityProvider in apps/api/src/index.ts (step 6b): a cernia_pk_ bearer is verified as an api key (tenant from meta.tag, fail-closed if absent), any other token delegates UNCHANGED to the JWT provider; one shared DefaultApiKeyVerifier backs BOTH the FHIR layer and the RBAC hook. NEW apps/api/src/api-key-live-flow.test.ts: real createServer + real registerRbacHook + real PgStorageAdapter on :5433, asserts dev-login → $issue (200, tag stamped) → authenticate a REAL FHIR route (GET /ApiKey, 200) → $revoke (200) → same secret rejected (401), plus non-admin $issue → 403. Each of the three bugs was reproduced (test fails) then fixed (test passes). ADR-0127: @cernia/api typecheck=0; api-key-live-flow + iam-route-guards + admin-api-key-routes = 43 tests green; zero NEW lint errors (64 pre-existing carry-forward in unrelated files). PROVEN LIVE on a fresh isolated boot (:8097, same :5433 DB the running stack uses): POST /dev/login → POST /admin/api-keys/$issue (200, meta.tag=urn:cernia:tenant) → GET /ApiKey with the issued secret → auth-with-issued-key=200; after $revoke → 401. Files: apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts (deriveOperation only), apps/api/src/admin-api-key-routes.ts, apps/api/src/index.ts, apps/api/src/api-key-live-flow.test.ts.

Release 3 / T3 — tenant self-serve WEBHOOKS shipped by EXTENDING the existing SubscriptionEngine rest-hook engine (no second delivery path). A tenant-admin registers an HMAC-SIGNED FhirSubscription rest-hook and receives POSTs when matching resources are written. (1) Signing (security): packages/subscription/src/{types.ts,dispatcher.ts} gained an OPTIONAL rest-hook channel field `signingSecret` (additive — existing Workflow/Connection callers unaffected); when set, dispatchRestHook adds `X-Cernia-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, rawBody)>` over the EXACT bytes POSTed (body serialized ONCE so the tenant can recompute). (2) Secret storage — approach (a), REUSE the encrypted tenant-secret store: apps/api/src/webhook-secret.ts stores each webhook's secret in tenant_secrets (migration 046) under synthetic provider key `webhook:<subscriptionId>` via TenantSecretResolver (AES-256-GCM in prod, Noop in test); encrypted at rest, tenant-isolated by the (tenant_id,provider) PK, generated server-side, returned ONCE at registration with Cache-Control:no-store, NEVER written to the FhirSubscription body (so it cannot leak via a FHIR read). get() accepts ONLY a tenant-sourced row (never the platform-env fallback — that would be a forgeable shared secret). Rejected (b) HMAC(masterKey,subId): one compromise forges every tenant + no per-hook rotation. (3) Bootstrap (apps/api/src/subscription-bootstrap.ts): startup scan now also materialises active rest-hook FhirSubscriptions (criteria derived from filterBy/topic — bare resourceType matches every write of that type, the SAME criteria format Workflow triggers use), AND the onWrite hook (re)materialises a FhirSubscription on create/update + tears its handle down on off/entered-in-error, keyed by tenant::subId so there is never a duplicate. LOOP-AVOIDANCE: a FhirSubscription write is treated as CONFIG (re-materialise) and is NEVER fanned out as a deliverable match. (4) Routes (apps/api/src/webhook-routes.ts, tenant-admin gated + deriveOperation→FhirSubscription in iam-route-guards.ts): POST /admin/webhooks (server-authoritative tenant; pre-assigns id, stores secret BEFORE create fires onWrite so the materialised handle is SIGNED; returns {subscription,secret} once, 201, no-store), GET /admin/webhooks (lists own; never a secret), POST /admin/webhooks/:id/$test (synthetic signed Parameters ping through the SAME dispatcher), POST /admin/webhooks/:id/$disable (status=off + unmaterialise + secret removed). Tenant isolation: register/list/test/disable all scoped to the authed principal's tenant; deliveries fire only for the subscription's tenant (engine is per-tenant via onResourceWrite(tenantId,…)). MANDATORY LIVE TEST (apps/api/src/webhook-live-flow.test.ts — the T2-lesson acceptance bar): real node http receiver + real createServer + real PgStorageAdapter on :5433 + real engine bootstrap → register a Patient webhook → write a Patient via a REAL FHIR route → receiver gets EXACTLY ONE POST whose body is the Patient and whose X-Cernia-Signature equals an INDEPENDENTLY-computed sha256 HMAC; the secret is NOT readable via GET /FhirSubscription/:id; a Patient in a DIFFERENT tenant does NOT reach the receiver. TWO ITEMS REMAIN, both re-scoped 2026-08-03. (a) NOT "multipart" — that premise is stale. The repo has DELIBERATELY refused @fastify/multipart: apps/api/src/brand-asset-routes.ts:19-28 and docs/security/threats/wave-h-h1-c-brand-assets.md:149 both reject it BY NAME to avoid its file-system temp-write surface, the package is in no manifest, and the ratified house pattern for binary upload is base64-in-JSON ({filename, contentType, bytesBase64}). The REAL gap is that nothing anywhere turns .cernia-plugin ARCHIVE BYTES into the RawPackageContents the route already accepts: packages/extension-runtime/src/plugins/package-loader.ts:30-32 states it is pure-data and leaves unpacking "to the route layer", and no unpacker exists — it needs a tar reader over the ADR 0043 §3 layout plus its own SHA-256 of the canonical bytes, which is also what would finally make the loader's currently-unreachable `hash-mismatch` verdict producible. (b) EXTERNALLY GATED, not code. A real cryptographic verifier needs the KMS custody grant already tracked as an external gate on the marketplace track ("per-service KMS grant for the Ed25519 package-signer"). @cernia/marketplace DOES already ship PackageSigner/PackageVerifier with a pluggable SignBackend seam, but its only implementation is StubSignBackend, self-documented as "clearly NOT secure for production"; an adapter is also needed, since SignBackend.verify(checksum, signature, keyId) does not line up with SignatureVerifier.verify({archiveHash, signature, signerFingerprint}), and PackageVerifier currently ignores the signer fingerprint entirely.

remaining: apps/desk still has no sign-in surface of its own — deliberately: the credential is the shared cernia.token minted by the web hub, and a second login form would be a second place for that to go wrong. The visitor was not missing a role, and the message was a dead end. useSurfaceState now distinguishes loading / unauthenticated (no token, or 401/403 from /api/me/surface) / error / ready, and the layout renders a 401 sign-in panel linking to the hub (same NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_URL resolution as apps/admin/src/lib/auth-session.ts) instead of a role denial. current.summary: REOPENED 2026-07-29 — the prior 'complete' summary was inaccurate. comprehensive-tests.yml runs the 3 audit scripts, two package smoke suites, Playwright and a scoped typecheck, but has never run any app's unit suite. That let the ADR-0140 erasure forcing function rot to RED on main with PHI-bearing tables unclassified. A `gates` job now enforces the forcing functions (`pnpm --filter @cernia/api test:gates`, self-defending via gate-registration.test.ts). 2026-08-03: the workflow's build steps were fixed — pnpm's `...` ellipsis was written backwards in ten steps across seven workflows, so NO job ever built a dependency closure, and 5 of the 10 gate files were dying on unresolved `@cernia/*` imports rather than running. Running the FULL apps/api suite in CI remains open — see remaining[]. 2026-08-03 (later): the Playwright job was root-caused, restructured and measured. It ran all FIVE playwright projects while installing only chromium (1812 of 3046 tests had no browser binary), and it never started apps/api even though 108 of 147 spec files POST to it — so the "dense F/T" was mostly ECONNREFUSED and "Executable doesn't exist", not product failures. Now --project=chromium-desktop, a booted apps/api with a /dev/login preflight, a 4-way shard behind an aggregate check still named "Playwright E2E", and 450 of 485 passing locally in 3.5 min (from 351 of 620 in 24 min). The rest is quarantined and counted in remaining[].

remaining: CI does not run the full `pnpm --filter @cernia/api test` suite (~570 files under apps/api/src). The `gates` job in .github/workflows/comprehensive-tests.yml covers only the eleven forcing-function files listed in apps/api/package.json `test:gates`; every other apps/api unit and integration test is still enforced by no CI check. Blocked on two prerequisites, both real: (1) a Postgres service reachable on the port the fixtures use (apps/api suites target :5433 locally while the workflow's service container publishes :5432, so the fixture port resolution has to be settled first, see apps/api/vitest.config.ts and packages/testing-real-services), and (2) a known-green baseline — the suite has never been run in CI, so its true red count is unmeasured and a job added blind would fail on day one and be disabled. Next step is to run it once in a workflow_dispatch job, record the baseline, then gate.

The same blind spot applies to every OTHER app: apps/*/src holds ~1026 test files in total and no CI job runs any of them. apps/api is the one addressed on 2026-07-29 (it holds the compliance gates); apps/admin, apps/patient, apps/cernia-ops and the extracted services (voice/audit/identity/interop/erx/telehealth/ml-ai/engagement/marketplace/billing) are unaudited for the same class of rotted forcing function. Audit each for gate-shaped tests before assuming apps/api was the only one.

comprehensive-tests.yml still has its push-to-main trigger disabled (commented out 2026-05-28 after the workflow failed on every push and spammed email). Gates therefore run on pull_request and workflow_dispatch only — a direct push to main bypasses them entirely. Re-enabling the push trigger depends on the workflow being reliably green, which the two bullets above gate.

NARROWED 2026-08-03 by PR #772 — the openapi-diff drift itself is CLOSED (see history), but the exporter's remaining blind spot is not. scripts/export-openapi-spec.mjs resolves routes by static regex, so routes registered through `app.route({ method, url })` with NON-LITERAL values are still absent from the exported spec and therefore unguarded by the drift gate. One such site exists today: the `for (const spec of specs)` loop at apps/api/src/grace-suspend-routes.ts:83, which registers the whole grace/suspend lifecycle family. Closing it needs either literal registrations at that site or a real boot-and-export (strategy (a) in the exporter header, which needs Postgres/Redis/NATS/MinIO in the job). Until then, treat 'the gate is green' as 'the gate is green for the 996 literal registrations it can read'.

SURFACED 2026-08-03 by PR #772 while auditing the newly-visible route surface — the seven service-to-service secret brokers (POST /{billing,engagement,erx,interop,marketplace,mlai,telehealth}-platform/secrets/$resolve) have two authorization defects. (1) The 'never broker a signing key as plaintext' rule is keyed on a CLIENT-SUPPLIED body field, not on the stored secret: apps/api/src/erx-platform-routes.ts:443-446 tests `req.body.kind === 'epcs-signing-key'` and, when the field is simply omitted, falls through to :485-496 which returns `plaintext` for the same provider — i.e. the DEA 21 CFR 1311 sole-control EPCS signing key in cleartext. Same shape at interop-platform-routes.ts:337-349 (mtls-client-cert) and via isSigningKeyKind() at telehealth-platform-routes.ts:363-366, mlai:419, marketplace:433, billing:391, engagement:456. packages/core/src/tenant-secret.ts:364-395 keys only on (tenantId, provider) and has no notion of `kind` at all, so the classification must move to the stored row's metadata. (2) No `provider` allowlist on any of the seven: `provider` is an arbitrary caller-supplied string (erx-platform-routes.ts:438-442,485; interop:350-358; telehealth:359,405), so a route-family grant does NOT segment secrets — a token scoped only to /interop-platform can resolve the tenant's Stripe, Twilio or LLM keys. SERVICE_ROUTE_FAMILY_REGISTRY (apps/api/src/service-identity-grants.ts:54-105) constrains paths, not secret namespaces. CI BLIND SPOT FOUND AND HALF-CLOSED — this stage's own summary was false. It claimed comprehensive-tests.yml "runs unit + integration + Playwright + 3 audit scripts"; it never ran the unit suite of any app. The workflow's only test steps were `pnpm --filter @cernia/testing-real-services test` and `pnpm --filter @cernia/external-fakes test`. NO job ran `pnpm test` (= `pnpm -r test`) or `pnpm --filter @cernia/api test`, so ~570 test files under apps/api/src — INCLUDING THREE SECURITY/COMPLIANCE FORCING FUNCTIONS — were enforced by nothing. PROVEN CONSEQUENCE, not a theoretical one: apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.completeness.test.ts (the ADR-0140 forcing function, whose whole purpose is to block a release when a tenant-scoped table is unclassified) was sitting RED ON MAIN at commit 442931e9 with FOURTEEN unclassified tables, among them scribe_transcripts — a table whose own DDL comment (migration 311) reads "The full visit transcript. PHI — server-side system of record only." PHI survived tenant erasure and the gate that existed to catch exactly that had never been executed by CI. The other two unenforced gates were iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts and iam-route-guards.scribe-coverage.test.ts. CORRECTION TO THE OBVIOUS DIAGNOSIS (recorded so the next agent does not 'fix' the wrong file): root vitest.config.ts:24 omits `apps/*/src/**` from its `include`, which LOOKS like the cause and is NOT. That config only governs a bare `vitest` run at the repo root, which no script and no workflow invokes — the root `test` script is `pnpm -r test`, which recurses and runs apps/api under ITS OWN vitest.config.ts, and that one does include `src/**/*.test.ts`. Widening the root include would have enforced nothing new while re-running 1000+ app tests under a config lacking apps/api's setupFiles (./vitest.setup.ts) and its 30s/60s timeouts — i.e. it would convert an unused command into a mass-failing one. The include is now commented in place explaining why it stays as it is. FIX SHIPPED (option c — make the gates real today rather than block on a green full suite): new `test:gates` script in apps/api/package.json + new `gates` job "Forcing-function gates (@cernia/api)" in .github/workflows/comprehensive-tests.yml running `pnpm --filter @cernia/api test:gates`. The gates are pure static analysis over migration DDL / route declarations / the cascade constants — NO Postgres, NO build, 4.9s for all five files — so they get a fast standalone job instead of waiting on service containers. THE GATE LIST DEFENDS ITSELF: an explicit file list in a package script has the same rot mode as what it replaced (write a new gate, forget to register it, it runs nowhere, we are back here). So apps/api/src/gate-registration.test.ts enumerates gate-shaped files on disk (`*.completeness.test.ts` / `*-coverage.test.ts`, plus a GATE_EXTRAS list for pre-convention names) and fails naming any file missing from `test:gates`; it also fails on a stale entry naming a file that no longer exists, and it is itself in the list so it runs in the same job. FALSIFIED: dropping an unregistered zz-probe.completeness.test.ts into apps/api/src turned it red with "expected [ 'zz-probe.completeness.test.ts' ] to deeply equal []", then green on removal. VERIFICATION: `pnpm --filter @cernia/api test:gates` → 5 files / 32 tests passed in 4.86s.

CI NEVER BUILT A DEPENDENCY CLOSURE — every step that claimed to was selecting the opposite set. GitHub Actions returned from a multi-day spending-limit pause and four jobs in .github/workflows/comprehensive-tests.yml went red on every PR with TS2307: Cannot find module '@cernia/audit-posture' (also '@cernia/mapping', '@cernia/design-tokens', '@cernia/branding'). ROOT CAUSE 1 — pnpm's `...` is DIRECTIONAL and was written backwards in ten steps across seven workflows. '...pkg' = pkg + its DEPENDENTS; 'pkg...' = pkg + its DEPENDENCIES; '...^pkg' = dependents excluding pkg; 'pkg^...' = dependencies excluding pkg. MEASURED, not assumed: `pnpm --filter '...^@cernia/storage' exec pwd` lists apps/admin, apps/api, apps/cernia-ops and 50+ others, all of which depend ON storage; `pnpm --filter '@cernia/storage^...' exec pwd` lists audit-posture, config, core. So `--filter '...@cernia/api' build` selected Scope: 2 of 331 projects and built NONE of the 116 packages apps/api needs, and `--filter '...^@cernia/testing-real-services' build` selected Scope: 72 of 331 dependents while omitting @cernia/audit-posture, which packages/storage/src/adapter.ts imports in PRODUCTION source. Fixed in comprehensive-tests.yml (4 steps), openapi-diff.yml, owasp-zap-dast.yml, perf-regression.yml, playwright-browser-matrix.yml (2), voice-agent-evals.yml, voice-agent-eval-live.yml. ROOT CAUSE 2, only visible once the filter was right — six packages' tsconfig `references` disagreed with their own package.json dependencies, so a dependent that referenced them compiled THEIR sources with nothing to resolve against: packages/storage was still missing ../audit-posture (so @cernia/connectors, which references ../storage, failed even under the corrected filter — audit-posture was unordered and built in parallel with it), packages/connectors missing ../mapping, packages/server missing ../audit-posture + ../connectors, packages/finops and packages/notifications missing ../storage, packages/voice-agent missing ../speech. apps/* still have reference gaps but are build leaves — nothing references them and pnpm's topological order supplies their deps' dist — so they are flagged, not changed. ROOT CAUSE 3 — the `gates` job added 2026-07-29 had NO build step, and every @cernia/* resolves through dist/, so on a fresh checkout 5 of its 10 gate files never ran at all: vitest died with "Failed to resolve entry for package" on @cernia/rbac, @cernia/server (x2), @cernia/core and @cernia/scribe, taking BOTH ADR-0140 iam-route-guards coverage gates with them, and the job reported that as a single red step rather than as gates that never executed. It now runs `pnpm --filter '@cernia/api^...' build` first; timeout-minutes 10 to 25. REGRESSION GUARD: apps/api/src/ci-build-closure.completeness.test.ts scans .github/workflows and fails naming file+line if the leading-ellipsis form returns; registered in apps/api/package.json `test:gates` so gate-registration.test.ts keeps it there. VERIFICATION from a genuinely clean checkout — RED `pnpm --filter '...^@cernia/testing-real-services' build` reproduced byte-identically to the CI log including "Scope: 72 of 331"; GREEN `pnpm --filter '@cernia/testing-real-services^...' build` = Scope 5 of 331, all Done, then both CIT typechecks clean; GREEN `pnpm --filter '@cernia/api...' build` = 117 projects, apps/api build: Done, exit 0. TRAP RECORDED: *.tsbuildinfo lives NEXT TO tsconfig.json, not under dist/, so `rm -rf dist` alone leaves tsc --build reporting "Done" while emitting nothing — a false green that cost one repro cycle here. PR #770.

THE DRIFT GATE WAS READING A QUARTER OF THE API, AND ITS ONE RED WAS A PHANTOM. With #770/#771 landed, openapi-diff reached its check and reported 25 unrecorded routes plus one UNWAIVED BREAKING removal, GET /scribe/templates. The removal was not real. That route has been served continuously since c6b8ff0a and is registered today at apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts:1850. ROOT CAUSE — the gate's producer, scripts/export-openapi-spec.mjs, walks apps/api/src with a regex requiring `(` to follow the method name directly, so it cannot read any route carrying an explicit TypeScript generic. Commit 59e77ffb (#637) retyped the route from `fastify.get('/scribe/templates', …)` to `fastify.get<{ Querystring: … }>( '/scribe/templates',`; the route did not move, the scanner simply went blind to it, it dropped out of the export, and the diff engine reads 'in baseline, not in candidate' as a deleted endpoint. MEASURED on this commit: the old regex saw 259 route registrations, the fixed one sees 996 — 737 registrations, 74% of the API surface, were invisible to the drift gate, and a breaking change to any of them would have passed silently. TWO REASONS IT STAYED HIDDEN: (a) scripts/export-openapi-spec.test.mjs already carried the U11 regression lock asserting the baseline covers the FULL surface, and NO workflow ran it — it was dead from the day it was written; (b) the gate was not reaching its check at all. FIXED — exporter regex tolerates inline, multi-line and nested generics (scan fn exported as scanRouteSource for direct testing); baseline re-seeded 223 to 871 paths per docs/api-contracts/README.md §3.3; six scanner regression locks + a `baseline.length > 600` floor added; the test is now wired into .github/workflows/openapi-diff.yml BEFORE the export step. PROOF THE GATE CAN FAIL (all three reverted): renaming /scribe/templates gave 'BREAKING — 2 unwaived endpoint change(s)' exit 1; adding a generic to the untyped POST /voice/$verify-ingress gave 'No changes detected' exit 0, i.e. the original bug is dead; adding a scratch GET /voice/$scratch-probe gave 'Added (additive — 1)' exit 0. HONEST COUNT — comparing the real surface at the last baseline refresh (79c5f9a5, 2026-07-12) against HEAD with a working scanner: 113 routes ADDED, 0 removed. The reported '25' was just the subset written without a generic. Recorded in docs/api-changelog/2026-08-03-surface-added-since-july-baseline.md (additive) + 2026-08-03-openapi-scanner-blind-to-typed-routes.md (patch). SIDE FINDING FIXED — /dev/login was published in docs/api/openapi.json, which apps/api/src/openapi-routes.ts serves verbatim and UNAUTHENTICATED at GET /api/openapi.json, so anonymous callers were told a token-minting seam exists; `/dev` added to NON_PUBLIC_PREFIXES and the entry removed from the artifact. Three authorization findings on the newly-visible service seams filed in remaining[]. PR #772.

TWO GATES THAT WERE RED FOR REASONS UNRELATED TO THE CODE UNDER TEST. (1) MIGRATION NUMBERING — not two duplicates but FOUR: 289 (289_erx_refill_fulfillment + 289_provisioning_runs), 290 (290_referrals + 290_scheduled_workflows), 335 (335_invitations_tenant_id_text + 335_scribe_coding_pass_outcome) and 338 (338_llm_audit_reserved_resource + 338_scribe_consent_decision). In each pair the file with NO later dependent moved to the tail — 289→347, 290→348, 335→349, 338→350 — and the survivor stayed put because a later migration ALTERs what it created (297_provisioning_run_context, 306_referral_listing_handle, 337_scribe_coding_pass_backfill) or, for 338, because 339_scribe_audio_destruction implements the path it introduces. In all four pairs the mover also sorted FIRST alphabetically, so the survivor's position in the total order is unchanged. Renaming a shipped migration is NOT free — schema_migrations is keyed by filename, so a rename makes an applied migration look pending (observed: catalog_price_terms recorded as 339_* in one database and 341_* in the repo). packages/storage/src/migrate.ts now carries MIGRATION_RENAMES, an append-only old→new ledger; runMigrations rewrites the schema_migrations row instead of re-running the file, and assertRenameLedgerIsSound fails closed on a malformed entry. PROVEN on real Postgres: a FRESH database migrates 306 files / 292 tables with zero duplicate numbers and all eight movers' and survivors' DDL present; and a database rewound to the OLD filenames re-runs NOTHING (306→306 rows, the one-time relocation in 350 leaves its probe row untouched). RECURRENCE: scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs — the existing zero-dependency pre-push hook, which already reads the whole migration corpus — gained checkMigrationNumbering (C0), so a duplicate cannot be pushed; migrate.test.ts now reports ALL collisions at once instead of aborting on the first, which is why three of these four were invisible. packages/storage 324/325 → 330/330. (2) OWASP ZAP DAST — the baseline job had NEVER run once since it landed 2026-05-26; every PR died at ~30s in `Initialize containers`. TWO stacked defects. The minio service cannot start under Actions (minio/minio needs `server /data` as its CMD and a services: entry has nowhere to put one); its own comment claimed the container would be "ignored if it fails", which is not a thing Actions does — a failed service container fails the job before checkout. Behind it, unreachable until now: softwaresecurityproject/zap-baseline and -full-scan are NOT published Docker repositories (404 — that namespace is gone); zap-baseline.py is a SCRIPT inside ghcr.io/zaproxy/zaproxy. Both fixed. NOTHING THAT WAS BEING CHECKED STOPPED BEING CHECKED: the minio service never came up in any run, S3_ENDPOINT/MINIO_ENDPOINT were never exported, so apps/api has always booted here on its in-memory object store and a passive HTTP scan is unaffected by the blob backend either way. The gate also stops lying by omission — a run that produces no report now says "SCAN DID NOT RUN — this is not a pass" in the PR comment and names what went unchecked, instead of failing with an empty comment as it had for 70 days. (3) Found in passing: apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.completeness.test.ts is RED on a pristine Windows checkout of main and GREEN in CI — core.autocrlf=true gives scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs CRLF endings, which vitest's module transform cannot parse, and it reports SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token at the import line rather than at the .mjs. Root-caused to a missing root .gitattributes; `*.mjs text eol=lf` added (same remedy as packages/design-tokens/.gitattributes). apps/api test:gates 66/80-with-a-dead-file → 80/80. Also repaired a coupling the renumber exposed: llm-audit-dangling-correlation.integration.test.ts selected the migration to withhold with startsWith('338_'), which silently stopped matching and made the test claim the one-time relocation was broken; it now selects by the shared LLM_AUDIT_RESERVED_RESOURCE_MIGRATION constant.

ZAP: A THIRD STACKED DEFECT, VISIBLE ONLY BECAUSE THE FIRST TWO WERE FIXED — then GREEN. With the minio service removed and the image corrected, the job reached the scan for the first time in 70 days and died there: `Failed to load config file /zap/wrk/rules.tsv — Level MEDIUM is not a supported level: ['PASS','IGNORE','INFO','WARN','FAIL']`, after which ZAP EXITS WITHOUT SCANNING — no JSON, no HTML — and the summariser correctly returned exit 2. .zap/rules.tsv is a four-column repo format whose second column is a SEVERITY; zap-baseline.py requires an ACTION. It has never been loadable by ZAP, and docs/security/zap-baseline-config.md §1 asserted the opposite ("ZAP itself reads the first two columns") — corrected in place, along with the file's own header. `-c` is no longer passed, and that is the right shape rather than a workaround: .zap/rules.tsv is the SUMMARISER's allowlist and the summariser is the gate, so it needs ZAP to REPORT an allowlisted finding in order to list it under "Allowlisted (suppressed)" with its reviewer-signed reason — a ZAP-side IGNORE would delete it from the JSON before the gate saw it. No row asks for OFF, so nothing that was suppressed stops being suppressed; all five reviewer-signed rows still parse (verified against parseRulesTsv). Also corrected: the "SCAN DID NOT RUN" fallback added earlier the same day did not fire, because zap-summarise.mjs writes "ERROR: cannot read input: ENOENT ..." to STDOUT — summary.md was non-empty, the emptiness test passed, and the PR comment was that one ENOENT line with no statement of consequence. Now keyed on the exit code. RESULT: `ZAP baseline (passive)` PASS in 9m29s (run 30864114881), 0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 5 INFO — the first security signal this gate has ever produced. The same run also proves the renumbered migrations apply to a FRESH CI Postgres end to end: `Apply migrations` succeeded and apps/api reached /healthz.

ZAP CORRECTION — the MEDIUM is already gone, and how it went is the evidence the gate works. The entry logged earlier today recorded `10098 Cross-Domain Misconfiguration` (3 instances) as the scan's first real finding and left it for triage. On the next run of the same branch — head 19db4880, which merges main including #775 `fix(audit-service,cors)` — the count is 0 MEDIUM. A finding that appears on one tree and not on a tree with a CORS fix merged in is a scan measuring the application, which is the property this gate had never once demonstrated. The remaining bullet is corrected so the portal does not carry a triage item that no longer exists; what is left is deciding on the record whether the five 90005 Sec-Fetch-* informationals are noise for an API.

PLAYWRIGHT E2E — THE RED WAS CONFIGURATION, NOT 3046 ROTTEN TESTS. Three defects, each of which alone made a green run impossible, none of which had ever been observed because the job was gated behind a failing `needs: [backend-integration]` and had literally never executed a spec until PR #770/#771. (1) FOUR FIFTHS OF THE RUN HAD NO BROWSER. tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts declares five projects (chromium-desktop, firefox-desktop, webkit-desktop, edge-desktop, chromium-mobile); the e2e job runs `playwright install --with-deps chromium` and then `playwright test` with no --project filter. MEASURED with --list on a clean worktree: 3046 total, 630 chromium-desktop, 604 firefox-desktop — i.e. ~1812 firefox/webkit/edge tests whose only possible outcome was "Executable doesn't exist". That is the arithmetic behind "Running 3046 tests". Cross-browser is the job of .github/workflows/playwright-browser-matrix.yml, which installs the right binary per matrix entry; .github/branch-protection-README.md already described this check as a "single-project smoke". It now pins --project=chromium-desktop. (2) THE BACKEND WAS NEVER STARTED. 108 of the 147 spec files read E2E_API_BASE (default http://localhost:8080), mint a tenant JWT with POST /dev/login and POST fixtures over HTTP before they touch a page — see tests/e2e/specs/wave-U-mips.spec.ts mintToken()/createReport() for the shape. The job built apps/api and ran its migrations and then never ran it, so every one of those specs died in its fixture helper on ECONNREFUSED. Only 8 specs carry a `test.skip(!process.env['E2E_API_BASE'])` guard; the other 100 fail loudly. Fixed with a "Boot apps/api on :8080" step modelled on perf-regression.yml + owasp-zap-dast.yml, CERNIA_DEV_LOGIN=1, and a PREFLIGHT step that POSTs /dev/login once and fails the shard with one legible line if no token comes back — a 200 from /health only proves something is listening. (3) VISUAL BASELINES ARE WINDOWS-ONLY. Every file under tests/e2e/screenshots/ ends -win32.png (e.g. status-full-chromium-win32.png, and 20 design-*-chromium-desktop-win32.png). Playwright appends the platform from process.platform at compare time, so on ubuntu-latest it looks for -linux.png, finds nothing, and fails all 28 toHaveScreenshot tests no matter what the UI looks like. All 10 call sites already sit inside tests tagged @visual, so the config now folds @visual into every project's grepInvert when CI runs off win32 — QUARANTINE, explicitly counted, with the docker recipe for generating Linux baselines in the config comment. Also quarantined: tests/e2e/specs/onboarding-installer.spec.ts (12 tests), which belongs to tests/e2e/installer.config.ts — it navigates to absolute http://localhost:3212 and only ever ran under the main config because `testDir: './specs'` matches every file in the folder; added to testIgnore. TOTAL DISABLED: 28 visual + 12 installer = 40 of 630 chromium-desktop tests, leaving 620 running as a real gate. STRUCTURE: the job is now a 4-way `--shard` matrix (fail-fast: false, so one shard's red does not hide the others) with a new `e2e-summary` job named exactly "Playwright E2E" so the required check in .github/branch-protection.yml keeps pointing at something. timeout-minutes 30 to 45 per shard — NOT a re-run of the raise-the-budget experiment that was already tried and reverted at 60 minutes (that experiment is what proved the suite was red rather than slow); ~14 of the old job's 30 minutes went to install + three builds before the first spec ran, and sharding duplicates that fixed cost into each shard instead of dividing it.

PLAYWRIGHT E2E, PART 2 — WHAT THE SUITE SAID ONCE IT COULD SPEAK. With the browser and the backend fixed (previous entry), the specs ran for the first time and the red set was 134 of 620. It was not 134 problems; it was six, and five of them were the product moving on without the test. (a) THE ADMIN SHELL BECAME AUTH-GATED AND ~51 TESTS NEVER NOTICED. apps/admin/src/lib/auth-session.ts redirects a visitor with no `cernia.token` to the public web hub, so an unauthenticated `/` renders no <aside> at all. FALSIFIED both ways on a live build: unauthenticated aside count 0, token present 1. navigation (18), branding (10), status (10), theme (6), schedule-import and smoke were all timing out on chrome that had never rendered, reading exactly like "the nav is broken". New tests/e2e/fixtures/admin-session.ts seeds the chrome-level session and says in its own header why a signature-less JWT is right for a rendering guard and wrong for anything that touches the API. (b) /dev/login GRANTS THE PRODUCTS THE PAYWALL TEST ASSERTS ARE ABSENT. entitlement-gating.spec.ts asserts PATCH /api/voice-agent/policy -> 402 for an unentitled tenant and its header claimed the tenant "never has a phone-agent grant"; measured 200, and product_entitlements showed five active rows created by the login itself. Worse, that hand-written five-slug grant list had drifted against a 33-product PRODUCT_REGISTRY — the exact rot product-registry.ts exists to end — so DOZENS of real-stack specs died on 402 (telehealth rooms, compliance evidence, imaging, erx...) because their tenant held 5 of 33 products. FIX: DEV_LOGIN_GRANTED_PRODUCTS is now DERIVED from PRODUCT_REGISTRY, and /dev/login accepts `grantProducts: false` for the two specs whose premise is a tenant that holds nothing (entitlement-gating, spine-admin-boundaries — the latter had been passing only because the five-slug list happened to omit `migration` and `erx`). Verified on a live api: default login now writes 33 rows, grantProducts:false writes 0. Dev-only, behind isDevLoginEnabled(). (c) TESTS ASSERTING A UI THAT WAS DELETED. login.spec.ts (7) and two accessibility.spec.ts tests target the v1 paste-a-bearer-token form — input#token, label[for=token] reading "Bearer token". /login is now the real credential form (label[for=tenantId|email|password]) covered by auth-login.spec.ts. The a11y pair was retargeted at the form that ships; login.spec.ts was quarantined rather than deleted so replacing it stays a decision by whoever owns login. Consequence worth stating: /login had no label-association coverage the whole time. (d) BRAND AND MARKUP DRIFT. status/theme asserted a "FHIR" badge (the brand badge now reads "Health"), the literal class `border-r` (@cernia/ui SidebarShell uses the LOGICAL `border-e` so RTL works — asserting the physical property would now be asserting an RTL bug), and title "Cernia Admin" while a metadata export shipped and made it "Platform Status | Cernia Health Admin". One of those tests contained the sentence "If a metadata export is added ... this test should be updated"; it was added and nobody came back. (e) A REQUIRED FIELD THE FIXTURES NEVER SENT. wizard-orchestrator.ts made primaryAdminPhone mandatory (E.164, the admin's own mobile for SMS-OTP, distinct from the facility number); onboarding-complete-flow, phone-number-selection and number-port-in 422'd on every run. Five tests, one field. (f) TWO PLAIN TEST BUGS, one of which the compiler had already reported: schedule-import called page.setInputFiles(LOCATOR, ...) where the API takes a selector string — it is one of the standing `tsc --noEmit` errors under tests/e2e, and neither the spec nor the typecheck was gated, so both signals sat there; and multi-tenant-isolation read page.content() while the auth guard was navigating away ("Unable to retrieve content because the page is navigating"), now a plain HTTP GET, which is the stricter check anyway since PHI would leak from the wire. Its sibling assertion was rewritten to test the INVARIANT (no admin shell for an unauthenticated visitor) instead of the mechanism (a redirect to /login that no longer happens). RESULT: 485 collected, 450 pass, 22 skip, 3.5 min at 4 workers, against a live apps/api + built admin on a fresh database. Everything still disabled is counted in remaining[] and annotated at its own call site. CI worker count also corrected: `workers: "50%"` resolves to ONE on a 2-core runner (that is the "using 1 worker" in the log, and why shard 2 was still mid-suite at its 45-minute deadline); pinned to 2, with the line reporter added so a CI failure is legible as text rather than as a wall of F and T.

PLAYWRIGHT E2E, PART 3 — THE E2E ADMIN PORT IS NOT IN apps/api's CORS ALLOWLIST, AND A LOCAL ENV VAR HID IT. With the API booted and the specs fixed, the first real CI run still reported 36 failures in shard 1 alone — every one a UI assertion, every one "element(s) not found", while the API-only assertions in the very same files passed. The failure's own DOM snapshot gave it away: "Failed to load framework / Failed to fetch". That is a browser network refusal, not a missing element. ROOT CAUSE: packages/config/src/defaults.ts corsOriginsDefault allows localhost and 127.0.0.1 on ports 3000-3006. tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts boots the admin app on :3210 (chosen precisely to avoid colliding with a dev server on :3000). So every BROWSER-side fetch from a spec's page to apps/api is refused at preflight, while the same spec's node-side `request` fixture — which performs no preflight — sails through. That splits the suite exactly in half along the line the CI log showed. FALSIFIED BOTH WAYS on one build: with the 3000-3006 default, `OPTIONS /compliance/frameworks` with `Origin: http://localhost:3210` returns NO access-control-allow-origin header and compliance-flow is 6/6 RED; with CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3210 the preflight answers `access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:3210` and it is 6/6 GREEN. Fixed by setting CORS_ORIGINS on the e2e job. NOT '*' — packages/server forces credentials:false on a wildcard origin, which changes auth behaviour under test. HOW IT WAS NEARLY MISSED, recorded because the next agent will hit it: every local run up to this point had CORS_ORIGINS='*' exported into the shell, so the whole UI half of the suite was GREEN locally and RED in CI for a reason invisible in the diff. A local green obtained under an env var CI does not set is not a green. The proof that mattered was re-running with the CI allowlist and watching it go red. FINAL MEASURED BASELINE under CI-equivalent CORS: 477 collected, 449 pass, 22 skip, 6 fail — and all six failures are @visual tests, which are excluded on non-win32 CI because their baselines are -win32.png. 3.0 minutes at 4 workers.

PLAYWRIGHT E2E — GREEN IN CI, FIRST TIME EVER, AND THE BUDGET RATCHETED TO THE MEASURED NUMBER. PR #773, run 30870058710: all four shards pass and the aggregate "Playwright E2E" check (the one .github/branch-protection.yml requires) is green. Per shard, 112 tests each: 102+10 skipped in 1.3 min, 108+4 in 1.0 min, 104+8 in 1.1 min, 112+0 in 1.5 min — 448 collected, 426 passed, 22 skipped, ZERO failed. Job wall clock 12m35s to 14m30s, of which roughly TWELVE MINUTES is install + three build steps and about ONE is testing. timeout-minutes accordingly 45 → 25, which is the ratchet the earlier comment promised; it is not the raise-and-hope move that was tried and reverted at 60 on the unsharded job. NOTE FOR THE NEXT CHANGE: at these numbers the four-way shard is buying almost nothing — it spends four runners' setup to divide five minutes of tests. Collapsing to one job (rename it "Playwright E2E", drop e2e-summary, keep --project=chromium-desktop) should run in ~18 minutes on a single runner. It was left sharded because the sharded shape is the one measured green, and changing the shape and the budget together makes it impossible to say which mattered. Also green on the same run and worth recording since both were red on main earlier today: openapi-diff and ZAP baseline (both fixed by PRs #774/#776, not by this one).

PHI SURVIVED TENANT ERASURE — FIXED. The ADR-0140 cascade (apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts) left FOURTEEN tenant-scoped tables classified neither for deletion nor for the retain-set, so a right-to-erasure run completed while leaving them intact. Seven of the fourteen carry clinical content: scribe_transcripts (migration 311 — "The full visit transcript. PHI — server-side system of record only"), scribe_transcript_words (per-word timings whose `text` reconstructs the transcript verbatim), scribe_live_transcripts (per-chunk in-visit snippets), scribe_after_visit_summaries, scribe_edit_diffs (before_text/after_text ARE the clinical note body), scribe_coding_suggestions (clinical rationale) and scribe_proposed_actions (payload + a verbatim transcript quote in source_span). CLASSIFICATION — 13 Scoped-IN (delete-all on tenant_id), 1 Scoped-OUT. Every one of the thirteen carries tenant_id DIRECTLY (it leads the PK on all of them), so none needs a join through scribe_sessions and all are plain delete-all; they are deliberately NOT flagged afterObjectPurge, because buildScribeAudioEraser (apps/api/src/scribe-retention-sweep.ts:121) enumerates ONLY scribe_sessions, so nothing new gates the object purge and the existing "exactly four deferred tables" assertion in erasure-cascade.test.ts still holds. The seven PHI tables above, plus: scribe_vocabulary, scribe_template_defaults and note_template_versions (tenant configuration, no retention obligation); scribe_coaching_events (non-PHI engagement telemetry); voice_cutover_state (migration 308 — routing flag, no PHI, same class as tenant_record_mode / tenant_isolation_mode which are already Scoped-IN); and event_outbox (migration 309 — a drain-and-discard DELIVERY QUEUE, not an audit anchor: it MIRRORS rbac_audit_events rows, and rbac_audit_events is itself retained, so the 6-year audit obligation is discharged by the original while the PHI-bearing copy goes). ON scribe_vocabulary specifically: migration 317 asserts "NOT PHI", but it is admin-typed free text and the migration's own description lists "clinician names" as expected content, so a tenant can put a person's name in it. Nothing turns on resolving that — it is tenant configuration with no retention obligation, so it is Scoped-IN whether or not any individual term is PHI, which is the only classification safe under both readings. THE ONE RETAIN-SET ADDITION, billing_meter_report_watermarks (migration 332, added the same day by PR #675), is deliberate and is NOT the retain-set being used as a dumping ground: it is PHI-free by construction (tenant id, period string, metric name, two integers) and it is retained as the INTEGRITY GUARD on records that are themselves retained. runMeteredFlushSweep still VISITS an erased tenant, because enumerateBillableTenants (apps/api/src/saas-subscription-store.ts:165) reads saas_subscriptions — in the retain-set — and the aggregate reads usage_rollups, also in the retain-set. Delete the watermark and the next nightly claim sees reported_total = 0 and re-reports the whole period's cumulative total to a formula=sum Stripe meter: precisely the ~15.5x double-report defect migration 332 was written to close, now aimed at a tenant who no longer exists to dispute the invoice. Its inputs outlive the tenant, so it must too. FALSIFIED: a scratch tenant-scoped table added to packages/storage/src/migrations turned it red naming zzz_scratch_falsify_probe, then green on removal — the gate genuinely detects a NEW omission. The cascade was then executed END TO END against real migrated Postgres (apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts 8/8, including the armed "erases in-scope, preserves Scoped-OUT + sibling tenant" case), proving all eleven new DELETEs are valid SQL against the real schema rather than only well-formed constants. (1) THE ADR. docs/architecture/adrs/0140-right-to-erasure-scope.md gained the thirteen Scoped-IN rows from the 2026-07-29 classification (the seven PHI-bearing scribe tables, scribe_vocabulary / scribe_template_defaults / scribe_coaching_events, note_template_versions, event_outbox, voice_cutover_state) plus billing_meter_report_watermarks in Scoped-OUT, each carrying the per-table justification that had been living only in the constant. Two table names in the retain table were WRONG — `audit_events` and `jit_grants` name nothing; the real tables are `audit_log` and `jit_access_requests`, reconciled in code on 2026-07-14 and recorded in prose but left standing in the table a reader would actually look them up in. One malformed markdown row (scribe_audio_destructions, missing its closing pipe) fixed. (2) THE AUTHORITY CONTRADICTION, which is what let the drift happen. The ADR’s Alternative 4 said "the AUTHORITY is this ADR; the constant is generated from this list in code review" and erasure-cascade.ts’s header repeated it, while the ADR’s own Completeness-audit section said "the code is the operative list". Measured cost of the ambiguity: 167 erase-classified and 75 retain-classified tables in the constant with no counterpart in the markdown. Settled in both files: the constant is OPERATIVE (it is what the worker executes and what both gates reconcile against); the ADR is the RATIONALE OF RECORD for the curated set — every table whose classification was argued rather than derived. A rule requiring 250+ tables to be transcribed into markdown is a rule nobody followed. (3) THE TEST. apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts seeded 13 tables, exactly one of them scribe (scribe_sessions), and the other 2026-07-29 tables were not in MINIMAL_DDL at all — so the worker’s PG-42P01 skip swallowed each DELETE and the cases asserted nothing. All 13 now exist in the DDL, are seeded for BOTH the erasing tenant and the sibling, and are asserted zero-then-one. Every PHI column carries a canary string, and a post-erasure sweep over information_schema searches EVERY text/varchar/json/jsonb column in the schema for it — asking the schema rather than asking the list, which is the shape of the defect J09-F1 found. 13/13 green against real Postgres on :5433.

current.summary: 4 of 5 bullets shipped; 2 remain, both awaiting something other than code. 2026-08-03: the self-serve PASSWORD path no longer strands its founding admin — $complete now upgrades the deferred (status:'invited', credential-less) admin in place on the conflict-recovery path it already ran, so the password typed on the request body reaches the canonical User.passwordHash instead of being discarded. The ADR-0140 classification gate is in a CI job for the first time, and the five-family cascade audit is complete — leaving a compliance sign-off on eRx/fax and a required-status-check that needs GitHub Actions billing restored.

remaining: ADR-0140's release-blocker rule is enforced at EXECUTION (the unbypassable auditCascadeClassification HOLD in apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.ts) and at AUTHORING by a ~0.5s pre-push hook plus the machine-read `-- ADR-0140:` migration directive. NARROWED 2026-08-03: `node scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs` is now wired into a workflow — it runs as the FIRST step of the `gates` job in .github/workflows/comprehensive-tests.yml, ahead of `pnpm install`, since it is dependency-free and takes ~0.5s, so an unclassified table fails in seconds rather than after a 25-minute dependency build. It was previously in NO workflow at all. WHAT REMAINS is not a wiring problem: (a) GitHub Actions cannot run — the spending limit has been exhausted since 2026-07-29 and every check reports fail in ~5s without starting, so a gate in a workflow is a gate that never executes; (b) once CI returns, `gates` must be made a REQUIRED status check on branch protection, otherwise a red job is advisory; (c) the workflow's `paths-ignore: docs/**` means an ADR-only PR skips the whole file — harmless today because this gate reads migrations and erasure-cascade.ts rather than the ADR, but it is the reason an ADR amendment cannot be gated the same way.

The cascade-completeness audit for the five flagged families is DONE (2026-08-03) and the outcome is narrower than the bullet assumed. Findings: (i) the provenance was misattributed — ADR 0143 flags none of these tables; it governs WHEN the cascade may run, not what it covers. (ii) There is no `auth_sessions` table; the real ones are `patient_auth_sessions` (migration 293) and `patient_credentials` (292). (iii) All seven tables across the five families — patient_credentials, patient_auth_sessions, fax_transmissions, erx_prescriptions, erx_refill_requests, pharmacy_status_events, scheduled_workflows — were ALREADY classified ERASE and none was unclassified, so both gates were green on them all along. What was actually missing was the deliberate rationale: six of the seven landed in the 2026-07-14 alphabetical bulk block with no justification comment, which is exactly the "by whichever list they happen to land in" condition. Each now carries one in apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts. WHAT REMAINS is a compliance sign-off, not code: two are genuine RETAIN candidates and the ERASE argument written at them is an engineering argument. eRx is a controlled-substance prescribing record (DEA §1311.305 EPCS audit trail; state boards commonly 2-7 years) and fax_transmissions is a disclosure record (HIPAA §164.528 accounting-of-disclosures, 6 years). The case for ERASE in both is that the obligation attaches to the AUDIT record — audit_log, Scoped-OUT, 6 years — and not to the operational row, and that retaining the row without the `resources` Composition it belongs to leaves an unusable fragment. Someone with a compliance opinion needs to agree before CERNIA_ERASURE_EXECUTE is armed; if they disagree, the change is to move the two entries to ADR_0140_SCOPED_OUT.

The canonical field is User.passwordHash and it is the ONLY one packages/auth-providers/src/providers/builtin-provider.ts reads; nothing in the repo ever read the nested path.
