J09-F1 — ADR-0140 ERASURE CASCADE LEFT A DEPARTED TENANT'S DATA ON DISK, FIXED. Run 3 of the J09 journey measured t-northside still holding 156 rows in product_entitlement_events after a confirmed, dual-controlled erasure that reported 190 tables cascaded and took `resources` to 0. Reproduced live on github/main before touching anything (docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/j09f1-red-verify.json): THREE tables survived, not one — product_entitlement_events (migration 340, 44 rows), product_usage_pricing (343, 3 rows) and catalog_prices (341, 3 rows) — and the erasure job's own tables_erased audit array shows all three attempted=false, i.e. the DELETE was never issued at all. Same fixture, same real operator routes, fixed cascade (j09f1-green-verify.json): 193 tables cascaded, all three at 0 with attempted=true / rowsDeleted 27+3+3, control tenant t-j09f1-control unchanged AND still non-empty, and the platform tenant_id='' price rows intact. Residue is commercial only, NO PHI — a broken guarantee, not a disclosure. CLASSIFICATION = ERASE for all three, argued per-entry in apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts and amended into docs/architecture/adrs/0140-right-to-erasure-scope.md: the parent product_entitlements has been Scoped-IN since the 2026-07-14 audit; ADR-0140 already classified the identical shape (scribe_recording_consent_events — an append-only history whose current-state sibling is Scoped-IN); logIsConsistent() in entitlement-history-store.ts returns raw.length===0 when the live row is absent, so RETAINING the history manufactures a state the reader itself calls incoherent and degrades every later read to 'cannot determine'; and none of the three is a financial record of record — invoices / stripe_invoices / charge_history / revenue_events / billing_usage_events / revenue_contracts / saas_contracts carry that 7-year obligation, are all Scoped-OUT, and are untouched by this change (grant_ref is only a pointer into Stripe, whose own horizon ADR-0140 already defers to). TWO CLASS-LEVEL DEFECTS behind the instance: (1) the completeness gate NAMED product_entitlement_events and product_usage_pricing — it was red on github/main with both — and both shipped anyway, because test:gates is not wired into any pre-merge check and CI cannot run (see the new `remaining` bullet); (2) the gate's scanner read only CREATE TABLE bodies, so catalog_prices — which acquired tenant_id by ALTER TABLE in migration 341 — was structurally invisible to it and the gate stayed GREEN for it. The scanner now also reads ALTER TABLE ... ADD [COLUMN] <tenant-key>, pinned by its own assertion so a refactor cannot silently drop the pass, plus an assertion that these three stay in the ERASE list (moving one to SCOPED_OUT would re-open the leak with the gate still green). NEW HAZARD FOUND AND CLOSED: catalog_prices and product_usage_pricing are the first cascade tables to reserve tenant_id='' as a PLATFORM sentinel row that every practice on the fleet resolves against. Every cascade predicate is `<key> = <tenantId>`, so a job row with a blank tenant id would delete the whole fleet's price list, irreversibly, while reporting a perfectly ordinary erasure. runTenantErasureWorker now REFUSES a blank tenant id before any gate or count, including for in-flight 'erasing' rows; regression test in tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts. J09'S OWN CHECK TIGHTENED (the finding's namesake): it asserted 'every SCRIBE table is zero' while ADR-0140 promises 'every TENANT-SCOPED table', and the defect lived exactly in that gap. New apps/api/scripts/erasure-residue-sweep.mts sweeps information_schema for every tenant-key-bearing table and reads the SAME constants the cascade executes from, so 'permitted to survive' cannot drift from 'actually retained'; run-journeys-c.mts J09-4 now asserts on it. Proven red-then-green independently of the journey via apps/api/scripts/j09f1-residue-sweep.mts (j09f1-sweep-red.json names all 3 leaks and permits the 6 retained; j09f1-sweep-green.json 0 leaks / 5 permitted), with a falsifying control — pointed at the never-erased tenant it lights up 9 tables, so it is not merely returning empty. Because it reads the LIVE schema it has no ALTER blind spot at all. PR #745's separate audio-destruction path is untouched and still does not go through the executor. VERIFICATION: test:gates 10 files / 69 tests green; tenant-erasure-worker.integration 9/9 against real Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5433; apps/api lint 63 problems = the stated baseline, 0 new; typecheck and build clean. Evidence: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/j09f1-{red,green}-{seed,verify}.json + j09f1-sweep-{red,green}.json.

ADR-0140 RELEASE-BLOCKER MADE ENFORCEABLE (follow-up to PR #762, which fixed the symptom and said it had not fixed the rule). The rule 'a table that lacks a classification is a release-blocker' was not one: test:gates runs in no pre-merge check and GitHub Actions cannot run at all (spending limit exhausted since 2026-07-29 - every check on every PR reports fail in ~5s without starting), so a gate that was RED on github/main naming two unclassified tables let those PRs merge and a real dual-controlled erasure left 156 rows behind. CI-based enforcement was therefore rejected as worthless today. THREE LAYERS SHIPPED. (1) AUTHORING - the migration declares its own classification, MACHINE-READ: migrations numbered above 345 must carry `-- ADR-0140: <table> = ERASE | RETAIN | NOT-APPLICABLE` and it must AGREE with apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts. This closes the actual defect: migration 340's header stated its classification CORRECTLY in prose and the array never learned it - a truth written in a comment and not in code. Forward-only ratchet (DIRECTIVE_RATCHET_FROM=345, pinned by an assertion so it cannot drift upward silently). (2) PUSH - NEW scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs: zero dependencies (node:fs + regex; no build, no node_modules, no DB), one parallel pass over the 305-file migration corpus, MEASURED 444-574 ms wall including node startup (sequential reads measured 1.8-4.3 s on this OneDrive working copy - parallelising the reads, not weakening the check, is what made it cheap). Installed on pre-push by NEW scripts/install-hooks.mjs (cross-platform; install-hooks.sh is now a wrapper) which the root postinstall runs, so `pnpm install` installs it; hooks are written to `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`/hooks so ONE install covers all ~100 worktrees, and a checkout that predates the script skips cleanly. Chosen over folding into test:gates because the ADR-0127 checklist is per-PACKAGE and packages/storage/src/migrations is not apps/api - the migration author had no reason to run an apps/api suite, and did not. (3) EXECUTION, UNBYPASSABLE - auditCascadeClassification in apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.ts asks the LIVE information_schema (scoped to current_schemas(false), because every cascade op is an unqualified DELETE and search_path is exactly the set of schemas such a DELETE can reach) and HOLDS every job on the new 'cascade-classification-incomplete' reason, naming the tables in report.unclassifiedTables. Applies to in-flight 'erasing' RESUMES too, unlike the two-clock gate: the clocks answer WHEN and a resume is past that decision, classification answers WHAT and every remaining DELETE is still ahead. Fail-closed - an audit that THROWS holds identically. PROVEN TO BLOCK, not merely asserted: a real unclassified table created in the live fixture schema holds an ARMED run with zero rows deleted and the job still 'confirmed'; five synthetic migration corpora (apps/api/src/__fixtures__/adr0140/) show the script rejecting an unclassified table, an ALTER-added tenant key, a missing directive and a directive that disagrees with the code. PROVEN NOT TO OVER-BLOCK: a platform table with no tenant key and an already-classified table both pass, and the pre-existing worker suite is unchanged. A test drafted with `audit_events` as the 'already classified' table was itself caught by the new gate - audit_events is the ADR's ASPIRATIONAL name and no such table exists - which is the same prose-vs-schema drift this change is about. VERIFICATION (ADR-0127): test:gates 10 files / 77 tests green (was 69; the completeness test is rewritten as the anti-drift test for the script and also runs the script's own checks); tenant-erasure-worker.integration 13/13 against real Postgres on 127.0.0.1:5433; apps/api typecheck clean; apps/api lint 63 problems = the stated baseline, 0 new. HONEST LIMIT, stated in the ADR amendment and in the narrowed remaining bullet: layers 1-2 make an unclassified table hard to LAND but are bypassable (--no-verify; a clone that never installed the hook); only layer 3 makes one impossible to ACT ON. A pre-merge check returns with CI. Files: scripts/check-erasure-classification.mjs, scripts/install-hooks.mjs, scripts/install-hooks.sh, package.json, apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts, apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.ts, apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.completeness.test.ts, apps/api/src/tenant-erasure-worker.integration.test.ts, apps/api/src/__fixtures__/adr0140/, docs/architecture/adrs/0140-right-to-erasure-scope.md.

The self-serve PASSWORD path stops stranding its founding admin. POST /onboarding/:id/reserve-tenant provisions the tenant EARLY with the __deferred__ sentinel, creating the admin status:‘invited’ with no credential — correct for the SOCIAL path, where the Google callback’s promoteInvitedAdmin finishes the job. On the password path there was no second act: $complete conflicted on the Tenant create, OnboardingFullProvisioner recovered the tenant through resolveExisting, ran its idempotent post-steps and returned 200 while the password on the request body was dropped on the floor. Active tenant, admin that cannot authenticate, and no invitations row either, because onboarding writes none. Measured live on five tenants 2026-07-31; apps/api/scripts/acceptance-clinician-role.mjs documents the shape as a reason to avoid the route, and apps/api/src/orphan-tenant-cleanup.ts describes the wreckage. FIX: FhirStorageTenantProvisioner.upgradeDeferredAdmin (apps/api/src/fhir-storage-tenant-provisioner.ts), called from the conflict-recovery branch of apps/api/src/onboarding-full-provisioner.ts. Chose "upgrade" over the alternative "stop calling reserve-tenant on the password path" because the latter is a client-side fix for a server-side hole: the route is not gated on isSocial (it branches to a password-path 409 for a missing email, so it plainly expects password callers), and today’s installer calling it only from the Google handler is a property of one client, not of the API. FAIL-SAFE: it refuses the sentinel and the empty string, so it can never activate a social-path admin; and it only ever touches a user who is BOTH status:‘invited’ AND credential-less, so a genuine retry-after-partial-failure whose admin already has a password is untouched — that is the property that makes it safe to call on every conflict recovery rather than only the first. It writes the CANONICAL User.passwordHash, the only field the built-in provider reads, which is the field the last defect in this area got wrong. Seam widened optionally (IFhirProvisioner.upgradeDeferredAdmin?) so the in-memory doubles across the suites are unchanged. 6 new unit cases, 22/22 in fhir-storage-tenant-provisioner.test.ts. ALSO in this change: the ADR-0140 classification gate joined a CI job for the first time, and the five-family cascade audit landed with per-table rationale — see the two narrowed remaining[] bullets.

current.summary: Cross-tenant aggregation runs and reconciles (fixed 2026-08-03, 2,570 cents across all three platform routes). The one open item is not a defect: whether the fleet-read /by-tenant should hash its tenant ids like its eight peers do. The factual errors around it are fixed — the "opaque UUIDs" claim is corrected everywhere it survived, and the duplicated hash helper now imports the canonical one.

remaining: OPERATOR-CONTRACT DECISION (the only thing left; the factual half is fixed). apps/api/src/cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts is internally inconsistent about tenant ids crossing the platform boundary: /metric-trend and /scribe-note-cost hash them citing CLAUDE.md invariant 5, /by-tenant and /tenant/:tenantId emit them raw. FIXED 2026-08-03: the false "tenant IDs are opaque UUIDs" justification is now corrected in all FOUR places it survived (apps/cernia-ops/src/app/cernia-ops/finops/page.tsx x2 — one of them rendered to the operator's screen — and apps/cernia-ops/src/components/finops/cost-by-tenant-table.tsx x2), and the file's privately re-implemented hashTenantId now imports the canonical one from cernia-ops-auth.ts that seven other cross-tenant stores use. DECISIVE EVIDENCE for whoever picks: (a) the premise that "hashing breaks the /tenant/:tenantId drill-down" is FALSE of the shipped product — fetchTenant in apps/cernia-ops/src/lib/finops-api.ts has zero production callers (only its own definition and one test), and cost-by-tenant-table.tsx renders the id as plain monospace text with no Link, href, onClick or router push; it is a React key and a sort key. (b) The house convention splits on route PURPOSE, not on file: eight fleet/telemetry read surfaces hash (activation, CSM, expansion, health, renewal, TTFV, ai-observability, and this file's own two), nine operator ACTION surfaces emit raw (quota, retention, entitlements, pricing writes, escalations, publisher). /by-tenant is a pure read-only aggregate with no action affordance, which puts it with the eight; /tenant/:tenantId is a targeted lookup and matches the nine. (c) If hashing is chosen the hash must ALSO be upgraded: it is unsalted sha256 over a small, human-guessable namespace of practice slugs, so a rainbow table inverts it in seconds — obfuscation, not de-identification. (d) NOT TRACKED ANYWHERE and larger than this bullet: cernia-ops-entitlements-routes.ts and cernia-ops-routes.ts emit raw tenantId AND displayName on cross-tenant READ surfaces.

history.note: PROD-P11: @cernia/finops PostgresCostTracker + migration 067_finops_cost_ledger. PK (tenant_id, occurred_at, ledger_id BIGSERIAL); CHECK on provider + category + non-neg quantity/cost. PHI tripwire blocks MRN/DOB-shaped values + forbidden keys (patientId, mrn, dob). 16/16 tests green against real Postgres including cross-tenant rollup isolation. Commit 99fdddd2.

CORRECTION to the 2026-05-26 "complete". /cernia-ops/finops/{rollup,by-tenant,margin-per-tier} returned EMPTY WITH NO ERROR. PostgresCostTracker never implemented the cross-tenant capabilities the routes assumed — and, contrary to the reading in both the route comment and the bug report, it did NOT reject the wildcard: "*" is a non-empty string, so it satisfied the `tenantId is required` guard and was bound as a literal WHERE tenant_id = '*', matching no row and returning a well-formed ZERO rollup. Because nothing threw, the route's own cost-tracker-wildcard-not-supported fallback never fired — the failure was quieter than documented. /by-tenant and /margin-per-tier separately probed for listTenantIdsInWindow, did not find it, and substituted an empty tenant list. Measured live on a 2,570-cent / 2-tenant ledger: all three answered HTTP 200 with zeros and no warning field at all. FIX: packages/finops/src/cost-tracker.ts gains platformRollup() and listTenantIdsInWindow(), both sharing ONE private aggregate() with rollup() so the platform figure cannot drift from the per-tenant rows it is supposed to be the sum of; rollup() now REJECTS PLATFORM_WIDE_TENANT_SENTINEL by name, so a wildcard can never again be silently read as a tenant. apps/api/src/cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts returns 501 cost-aggregation-unsupported naming the missing capability instead of degrading to zeros / items:[] / all-tier-zero. An empty 200 from these routes now means the ledger really was empty. LIVE AFTER: rollup totalCents 2570; by-tenant t-cedar 1030 + t-lakeshore 1540 = 2570; margin-per-tier tenantCount 2 / totalCostCents 2570. WHY IT WAS GREEN THE WHOLE TIME: cernia-ops-finops-routes.test.ts injected a hand-written TestCostTracker that implemented BOTH capabilities production lacked — it honoured the "*" wildcard and had listTenantIdsInWindow — so every case passed against a double strictly more capable than the shipping class. Same failure as the bare-Fastify harness on /api/o6/audit, in the dependency direction instead of the middleware one. That double is deleted; the suite now injects the REAL PostgresCostTracker, with one deliberately-incapable double retained solely to prove the 501. Tests: @cernia/finops 136/136, cernia-ops-finops-routes 11/11 (R08-R11 new, pinning refused-vs-empty in both directions).

The "opaque UUIDs" claim corrected everywhere it survived, and the duplicated hash helper removed. The earlier 2026-08-03 defect fix corrected the justification in cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts’s header but left it standing in four other places, one of them RENDERED TO THE OPERATOR ("Tenant IDs are opaque UUIDs", apps/cernia-ops/src/app/cernia-ops/finops/page.tsx). Live tenant ids are practice-naming slugs. All four corrected; no patient identifier is involved on this surface either way, so the accurate statement is that a CUSTOMER-identifying value crosses the platform boundary — a different claim from the one being made. Separately, cernia-ops-finops-routes.ts carried its own byte-identical copy of hashTenantId while cernia-ops-auth.ts exported the canonical one seven other cross-tenant stores import; it now imports it, with the unsalted-sha256 weakness recorded at the function rather than only in a status file. The BEHAVIOUR is deliberately unchanged — see the narrowed remaining[] bullet, which now carries the evidence that makes the decision cheap: the drill-down the bullet was protecting has no production caller.

stages.name: Search parameters return the rows they name
stages.rationale: A declared search parameter that builds a predicate no row can satisfy is a conformance defect that looks like a clean answer: HTTP 200, well-formed Bundle, total=0. Nothing downstream can tell it apart from 'this patient has no records', which is why it survived in production across $everything, bulk export, the EOB assembler and the pre-visit brief. This stage tracks the parameters whose SQL translation is known to be unable to match, by type.

current.summary: The guaranteed-empty class is CLOSED on both halves. References were fixed 2026-07-31/2026-08-03; the remaining 72 non-reference parameters (68 token, 3 string, 1 uri) are fixed 2026-08-03 — applyJsonbFallback now ORs its original containment probe with a SQL/JSONPath predicate for DOTTED expressions only, which is a strict superset and so provably cannot lose a row that matched before, and the token system|code branch no longer hard-codes a coding[] shape that a conformant Identifier never has. Single-segment expressions (~190 parameters, already correct) compile byte-identically. Proven red-then-green against real PostgreSQL: 16 of 19 cases in packages/storage/src/search-sql-containment.integration.test.ts fail against github/main and all 19 pass after — and the 3 that passed on the broken code are all EXCLUSION assertions, which is the point. The appointment-reminder job no longer depends on participant slot order. Open: compartment pagination (and a next link that loops), write-time reference validation, and the 225 unregistered columns now re-scoped as a perf question.

remaining: The five array-indexed reference COLUMNS (`appointment_patient`, `appointment_practitioner`, `provenance_target`, `encounter_practitioner`, `procedure_performer`) still exist and are still materialised on every write, now with NO reader: `packages/notifications/src/scheduled-jobs/postgres-appointment-reminder-store.ts` was the last one and was rewritten 2026-08-03 to LATERAL lookups that scan `participant[]` for the type being asked for (red-then-green on real Postgres: 2 new cases fail against `github/main`, 13/13 pass after). What remains is dead weight rather than a defect — five STORED generated columns plus their partial B-tree indexes, computed on every Appointment/Provenance/Encounter/Procedure write for nobody. Dropping them is a migration; the build-time drift gate already prevents anything registering them again, so leaving them costs write time and index space, not correctness.

`walkPatientCompendium` / `walkEncounterCompendium` page at 1000 and report `truncated` when a page comes back exactly full, but 1000 is the storage adapter's hard ceiling — a patient with more than 1000 of a single resource type is still truncated, now honestly rather than silently. Real pagination through the compartment (a `next` link that continues per-type rather than restarting) is not implemented. Worse than "not implemented": `assembleBundle` (apps/api/src/everything-routes.ts:535) DOES emit `Bundle.link[rel=next]` pointing at `_page=2`, and nothing anywhere reads `_page` — the query type declares it (everything-routes.ts:163) and no handler consumes it. A conforming client that follows the next link gets page 1 again, forever. Either implement a resumable per-type cursor or stop emitting a link that loops.

227 declared search parameters name a `column` that is not in KNOWN_GENERATED_COLUMNS. Two named a column no migration creates and are fixed; the other 225 name columns that DO exist, so they fall through to the same clause they would have used with no column declared. RE-SCOPED 2026-08-03: this was worth reclaiming because falling through meant a guaranteed-empty containment probe. It no longer does — `applyJsonbFallback` now answers dotted expressions correctly via jsonpath — so registering these columns is a PERFORMANCE change (indexed equality instead of a GIN probe), not a correctness one. Measure before doing it: the perf comparison already recorded in KNOWN_GENERATED_COLUMNS found the jsonpath plan FASTER than the column plan on a live table (4.0ms vs 26.5ms for the same 191 rows), so the assumption that a registered column is the fast path is not safe to carry into this batch unmeasured.

The generic FHIR write surface (`POST /Composition`, `POST /Appointment`, …) still accepts a bare `subject.reference` and any `participant[]` ordering. The scribe path is closed at its source and the corpus is repaired, but nothing REJECTS a non-conformant reference on the way in. Validating `Reference.reference` against the three FHIR R4 forms at write time would close the class rather than the instance; not done here because it changes generic write semantics for every caller and needs its own measurement of what currently posts non-conformant references.

history.note: Reference search parameters fixed at the translation layer. applyReferenceParam (packages/storage/src/search-sql.ts) no longer falls back to JSONB containment — it emits `body @? '$.<path> ? (@ == "<value>")'`, which matches the stored {reference: ...} shape and, in lax mode, any element of an array-valued path (AuditEvent.entity, DocumentReference.author) with no cardinality table to drift. @? rather than jsonb_path_exists() so the existing idx_resources_body_gin can serve it; the value is JSON.stringify-escaped into a BOUND parameter and never reaches SQL text. 63 single-valued reference columns that already existed and were already indexed were registered; 8 array-indexed ones deliberately were not, because a column reading `-> 0` answers only for the first element. DocumentReference added to PATIENT_LINK_PARAM_BY_TYPE (packages/core/src/compartment-link.ts) and PATIENT_COMPENDIUM_RESOURCE_TYPES (packages/fhir-graph/src/edge-catalog.ts) — it was in neither, so every patient's signed-note documents were unreachable through $everything by any route. New real-Postgres regression test packages/storage/src/search-sql-reference.integration.test.ts executes the clause and counts rows (5 of 7 cases fail on github/main); the pre-existing suites could not catch this because one asserts on compiled SQL and the other drives an in-memory storage double. Live evidence docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/finding32-red-github-main.json and finding32-green-fix.json, probe apps/api/scripts/everything-fix-probe.mjs. Closes journeys.json finding 32.

The half of finding 32 that PR #744 dismissed, plus the three follow-ups it deliberately left. (1) BARE PATIENT REFERENCES. The 2026-07-31 note said a scan of run2_b found zero bare subject references and concluded the hazard was latent; it scanned the two databases on the host that happen to have none. A census of all 299 databases (296 with a `resources` table, 64,310 resources) finds 108 bare rows in 13 databases — run2_c 3, run3_c 4, api_errors 19, scribe_f1 14, scribe_fix 14, scribe_e2e 13, and seven more — every one a `subject.reference` on Composition / DocumentReference / ServiceRequest, with `patient.reference`, participant and target clean everywhere. FIXED ON THE WRITE SIDE: `ScribeSessionStore.start` (apps/api/src/scribe-session-store.ts) canonicalises via the new `canonicalPatientReference` (packages/core/src/patient-reference.ts) before the INSERT. The store rather than the route, because `session.patientId` is read by FIVE writers that each drop it straight into a `.reference` — Composition.subject (scribe-draft-routes.ts), DocumentReference.subject twice (scribe-sign-routes.ts), and ServiceRequest.subject / Appointment.participant[0].actor / Task.for (index.ts ~4258-4420). D19 is NOT narrowed: the API still accepts both spellings and still answers 201 for "pt-123"; D19's own comment defers "normalising the STORED value" as a separate, migration-shaped change, and this is that change. Migration 344 repairs rows already written — tenant-scoped and fail-closed, rewriting a bare id only when exactly one non-deleted Patient with that id exists in the SAME tenant. Read-side acceptance deliberately NOT added: the reference is wrong in the record and not only in the index ($push-to-ehr transmits it to an EHR that cannot resolve it), and a bare value names no type, so accepting it on read would make `?subject=Practitioner/x` match the same row. LIVE RED→GREEN on database `barefix`, a template clone of run3_c, with port↔database pairing proven in both directions by a write before either probe (present in barefix, absent from run3_c): `$everything` for the J07 patient went total=4 / 3-of-7 own records to total=8 / 7-of-7. Isolation: patient B (same tenant) and tenant t-meridian were each SEEDED NON-EMPTY first — 2 records each, one canonical and one deliberately bare — and B's own bare record was invisible to B in RED (1/2) and visible in GREEN (2/2) while never appearing in A's compendium in either. Zero leaked in either direction; cross-tenant read still 404 not 403; undeclared parameter still 422; the token parameter still answers. Evidence: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/barefix-{red,green}.json. (2) ARRAY-INDEXED REFERENCE COLUMNS — five, not four. `appointment_practitioner` also pins a slot (`participant -> 1`) and the 2026-07-31 census missed it by grepping for `-> 0`. It and `appointment_patient` are generated from the SAME declared expression, `participant.actor.reference`, so the schema was encoding a writer convention. All five removed from KNOWN_GENERATED_COLUMNS so `referencePathMatch` serves them, matching any element. The perf objection recorded on 2026-07-31 ("trades an indexed lookup for a GIN scan on a live path") does not survive measurement: on cernia_main the jsonpath plan runs 4.0 ms against the column's 26.5 ms for an identical 191-row answer, and neither is a scan, because `AdapterSearch` pins tenant_id + resource_type + deleted before any parameter clause. The claim that this breaks the voice reschedule flow TODAY is also not true: 295 Appointments across the host, 0 with a Patient participant at an index other than 0, 0 with a Practitioner at any index other than 1, 0 NULL `appointment_patient`. It is LATENT, and fixed because it costs nothing and is invisible when it fires, not because it is currently biting. Real-Postgres red→green in packages/storage/src/search-sql-array-reference.integration.test.ts — 3 red on github/main, and the 4 isolation controls green on both sides, which is the property a control should have. (3) COMPENDIUM TRUNCATION. `walkPatientCompendium` passed no `count` on all THREE passes (the tracked bullet named only pass 1) and `walkEncounterCompendium` on one more, so each took the adapter default of 20 while `summary.truncated` reported only the maxResources cap. Now `COMPARTMENT_PAGE_SIZE = 1000` on every compartment search, and a page returning exactly full sets `truncated`. packages/fhir-graph/src/walker-paging.test.ts is red 4-of-5 against github/main's walker; its double reproduces the adapter's real `Math.min(count ?? 20, 1000)`, which the existing walker.test.ts double does not — that is why 19 green tests missed this. (4) TWO PHANTOM COLUMNS. `practitioner_identifier` and `consent_date` confirmed absent from all 296 databases AND from every GENERATED ALWAYS clause in the migrations; the `column:` claims are dropped from apps/api/src/resources.ts. No behaviour change — an unregistered column was already ignored — but the registry stops asserting an index it does not have. (5) THE DRIFT GATE the 2026-07-31 note asked for. packages/storage/src/known-generated-columns.test.ts parses migrations/*.sql and fails on any registered column a migration does not create, or that pins an array slot, with an explicit allowlist for the 31 token/string columns where indexing coding[0] is deliberate. It goes red 3-of-5 the moment `appointment_patient` or `practitioner_identifier` is re-added. Deliberately parses the migration TEXT rather than booting a fixture: applying 303 migrations blows the 10s hook timeout and would make a correctness gate skippable whenever Postgres is down. The parser was validated against `information_schema` on the dev host first — identical answer, two independent derivations. (6) apps/api/scripts/search-param-census.mts replaces the prose census: 526 declared, 243 column-backed, 21 jsonpath, 190 correct containment, 72 guaranteed-empty — not 74, because `applyDateParam` uses `#>` extraction rather than containment and the 2 date parameters counted on 2026-07-31 were never broken. HARNESS TRAP WORTH KEEPING: `$everything` caches its Bundle for 30s keyed on (tenant, anchor, window, types, count, includeAuditTrail). The first GREEN run — 24s after RED, with identical parameters by design — was served the RED answer and reported the fix as having done nothing. barefix-probe.mjs now waits out the TTL. A harness that does not know about that cache produces a false negative indistinguishable from a failed fix.

The 72 non-reference guaranteed-empty parameters, and the reminder job’s participant-order assumption. (1) CONTAINMENT. applyJsonbFallback (packages/storage/src/search-sql.ts) built `body @> {"<first-segment>": value}` from a DOTTED expression, so `identifier.value` asked whether an ARRAY of Identifier objects equals a string — false by construction, exactly as for references, on 68 token + 3 string + 1 uri parameters. Fixed by OR-ing the original probe with `body @? '$.<segments> ? (...)'`: dotted only, so the ~190 correct single-segment parameters compile byte-identically, and a disjunction rather than a replacement so it is a strict SUPERSET — no per-parameter before/after measurement is needed to establish that nothing was lost, which is what made the earlier "blanket flip is not safe" objection blocking. String modifiers are carried through (like_regex with flag "i", metacharacters escaped) so a dotted string parameter still answers starts-with/contains rather than silently becoming equality. (2) system|code. The token branch built {key:[{coding:[{system,code}]}]} — right for a CodeableConcept, impossible for an Identifier, which spells its fields system/value and has no coding at all; that is the 17-type `identifier` family the bullet called "probably one fix". Now also OR-ed with a filter applied at the PARENT of the final segment, which derives the right shape from the expression instead of assuming the datatype. (3) EVIDENCE. packages/storage/src/search-sql-containment.integration.test.ts, 19 cases against real PostgreSQL on :5433, every exclusion paired with the inclusion proving the excluded row exists and is matchable. Red-then-green measured by checking out github/main’s search-sql.ts under the same tests: 16 failed, 3 passed — and all 3 that passed are exclusion-only assertions, the failure mode the file header warns about. 32/32 pre-existing compiled-SQL tests unchanged. (4) REMINDER JOB. postgres-appointment-reminder-store.ts read the patient from appointment_patient (participant[0]) and the provider display from participant->1; an HL7v2 SIU appointment (AIL before AIP, no patient participant) produced NO reminder — null patient ref, failed join, no phone, no email, silently. Both are now LATERAL scans of participant[] keyed on the referenced type. 3 new cases; 2 of them red against github/main, 13/13 green after. (5) PRE-VISIT BRIEF. GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief?patientId=Patient/<id> 404’d because the route required a bare local id while every other surface — and scribe_sessions.patient_id since the canonicalisation fix — uses the canonical spelling; now normalised in via the existing patientLocalId export, leaving a non-Patient reference untouched rather than reinterpreting it.

tracks.name: Microservices Wave-2 — Interop-service extraction
tracks.description: First Wave-2 satellite: a new independently-deployable apps/interop-service (@cernia/interop-service, port 8093, own Postgres DB) — the protocol-speaking integration edge (HL7v2/MLLP, X12/EDI, CDA, NCPDP, connectors, mapping) extracted reuse-first from the monolith per the Wave-1 R4 assignment. Built 2026-07-21 per docs/plans/2026-07-21-001-refactor-microservices-wave2-interop-plan.md; closeout in docs/architecture/microservices-wave2-retrospective.md; governance in docs/architecture/adrs/0146-interop-service-extraction.md. PRs #572-577 + integration commits 8c0a443b, 4086bad5.

stages.name: Scaffold + own DB/RLS + outbox + service-identity (IU1-IU5)
stages.rationale: Governance ADR-0146 + a Wave-1-pattern scaffold: @cernia/server.createServer boot, net-new RLS-native operational tables, the stock event-backbone outbox, and the service-identity substrate. Reuse-first — IU2 is ~90% a copy of audit-service; the outbox and identity substrate lift as-is.

baseline.summary: No apps/interop-service. Interop rode generic FHIR RBAC in the monolith with no owned tables, no dedicated boot, no outbox, no service identity. Connection/ConnectionRun were FHIR resources indexed via STORED generated columns in packages/storage migration 005.

current.summary: IU1 ADR-0146 landed (canonicalization decided: x12-engine + catalog-hl7-v2-messages canonical; retire catalog-x12-edi-transactions + hl7v2). IU2 scaffold on @cernia/server, port 8093, DB interop_service, compose opt-in 'interop' profile — live boot proven (/healthz 200, /readyz 503 fail-closed), 7 tests. IU3 migration 001 = 7 RLS-native operational tables (composite (tenant_id,id) PK + FORCE RLS + per-tenant policy), 37 real-PG tests, cross-tenant read denied on all 7. IU4 stock PostgresOutboxStore bound to interop_outbox (bespoke store eliminated), 43 tests + PG crash-soak zero-lost/zero-double. IU5 service-identity verify + outbound KMS-signed client + per-tenant rate-limit, 25 tests.

history.note: IU1-IU5 merged (PRs #572-577). ADR-0146 + service-map cross-ref; scaffold apps/interop-service (port 8093, DB interop_service) with live boot; migration 001 (7 RLS-native operational tables, 37 real-PG tests); stock event-backbone outbox on interop_outbox (crash-soak zero-lost/double); service-identity verify+client+rate-limit (25 tests).

stages.name: Lift engines + connectors + eRx libs (IU6-IU9)
stages.rationale: The reuse-heavy core: the ~37k-LOC transform layer (parsers/mappers/adapters) lifts as pure DI libraries. Net-new is only the runtime host the monolith never built (createDefaultRegistry with real HTTP deps) and the format-engine registry executing the canonicalization decision.

baseline.summary: createDefaultRegistry() was never called anywhere in apps/api; the FastifyRouteRegistrar was constructed then eslint-disabled as reserved. 8 of 10 engine packages had zero production consumer. Two X12 and two HL7v2 implementations overlapped with no canonicalization. Surescripts client is a stub throwing NotImplementedError.

current.summary: IU6 format-engine registry executes ADR-0146 canonicalization (HL7v2->catalog-hl7-v2-messages, X12->x12-engine, CDA->catalog-hl7-cda-r2, NCPDP->catalog-ncpdp-telecom-d0) with construction-time drift guards rejecting retired packages; 14 tests incl. X12 270/271 round-trip via injected fetchImpl. IU7 mapping-runtime hosts @cernia/mapping (5 rungs), 10 tests + paramsToSlotSearch parity. IU8 connector runtime host bootstraps all 15 adapters with real HttpClient/FastifyRouteRegistrar (TCP/SFTP deferred to IU15/16), dropped the dead @cernia/storage dep from packages/connectors, 9 tests + Epic slotSearch round-trip. IU9 hosts eRx builders + surescripts-adapter behind an explicit NotImplementedError stub-transport boundary, 19 tests.

remaining: eRx production transport (NCPDP-SCRIPT SOAP/REST, mTLS, EPCS controls) is external-gated (Surescripts certification + directory registration) — IU9 lands the stub boundary only; this is the Wave-3 eRx build seam.

history.note: IU6-IU9 merged. Format-engine registry (canonicalization executed, drift guards), mapping-runtime, connector runtime host (15 adapters real deps, dead-dep dropped), eRx libs hosted behind a stub-transport boundary. apps/interop-service/src/{engines,connectors,erx}/*.

stages.name: Monolith endpoints + service-side seam clients (IU10-IU14 + P3 reconcile)
stages.rationale: The seam inversion vs voice: interop WRITES mapped FHIR back to the monolith RecordGatewayRouter and READS config/secrets/patient-identity over service-identity-gated endpoints. RecordGateway stays monolith-side; SecretsResolverClient is a broker (no plaintext creds/PHI in the interop DB).

baseline.summary: No interop-platform seam surface. The monolith RecordGatewayRouter, TenantSecretResolver, and MPI were reachable only in-process; no service-identity-gated read/write endpoints for an extracted service.

current.summary: IU10 apps/api/src/interop-platform-routes.ts exposes five service-identity-gated /interop-platform endpoints (config-read, secret-broker $resolve, record-write->RecordGatewayRouter, patient-match/MPI, mapping-resources read) with ONE additive index.ts registration; interop-service added to SERVICE_ROUTE_FAMILY_REGISTRY; 18 real-PG tests (record-mode honored, secret never persisted, cross-tenant 403). Service-side clients: IU11 ConnectionConfigClient (short-TTL cache+invalidate, 13 tests), IU12 SecretsResolverClient broker (no-persist structural, mTLS->KMS-grant handle, 9 tests), IU13 RecordWriteClient (inverse of voice reads) + PatientMatchClient (quarantine-on-unmatched, 13 tests), IU14 MappingExecutorClient (agent/workflow rung reads over the seam) + AuditEmitClient (hash-chained PHI-free events over the IU4 outbox, 27 tests). P3-reconcile fixed outbound route-family prefixes + added endpoint (e) mapping-resources (AIAgent/Workflow allow-list only).

history.note: IU10-IU14 + P3 reconcile merged. Five monolith /interop-platform seam endpoints (one additive index.ts registration) + four service-side seam clients; broker non-persistence asserted; RecordGateway stays monolith-side. apps/api/src/interop-platform-routes.ts, apps/interop-service/src/platform-client/*.

SECURITY (task #157): the /interop-platform/secrets/$resolve broker keyed its never-plaintext rule on the caller-supplied req.body.kind, so OMITTING the field fell past the mtls-client-cert boundary into the plaintext arm. Fixed in apps/api/src/interop-platform-routes.ts via the new apps/api/src/platform-secret-broker-policy.ts: kind is REQUIRED and matched against INTEROP_SECRET_KINDS; the platform vendor providers (stripe/twilio/openai/anthropic) are hard-denied; only TENANT-provisioned secrets are brokered (no process.env fallback, which was a platform-environment read primitive for any interop-scoped token); and records/$write is constrained to INTEROP_WRITABLE_RESOURCE_TYPES. Red/green regression suite: apps/api/src/platform-secret-broker-policy.test.ts.

stages.name: Inbound ingress physics + message pipeline (IU15-IU17)

Acceptance proven end-to-end on real PG by apps/interop-service/src/boot-e2e.integration.test.ts: a real MLLP frame over loopback -> persist + AA -> pump -> parse/match/map -> RecordWrite over the seam -> exactly 1 audit event, idempotent on replay. Not urgent: human operators use the monolith POST /Connection/:id/$run (apps/api/src/connection-routes.ts:203), which is RBAC-gated on connection.run today.

SECURITY (task #157): the /erx-platform/secrets/$resolve broker keyed its never-plaintext rule on the caller-supplied req.body.kind — OMITTING the field fell past the epcs-signing-key branch and returned the EPCS controlled-substance signing key (a DEA 21 CFR 1311 sole-control credential) as PLAINTEXT. Fixed in apps/api/src/erx-platform-routes.ts via the new apps/api/src/platform-secret-broker-policy.ts: (1) kind is REQUIRED and matched against ERX_SECRET_KINDS, which is the sole source of custody; (2) each kind is bound to the provider namespaces it may resolve and the platform vendor providers are hard-denied (previously {provider:"stripe"} resolved the PLATFORM Stripe key through TenantSecretResolver s process.env fallback); (3) the plaintext arm re-checks custody from the RESOLVED secret metadata, so a KMS/HSM secret can never be emitted regardless of caller input; (4) records/$write is constrained to ERX_WRITABLE_RESOURCE_TYPES. Client side: apps/erx-service/src/platform-client/secrets-resolver.ts now requires an explicit ErxPlaintextSecretKind. Red/green regression suite: apps/api/src/platform-secret-broker-policy.test.ts.

Cutover is per-TENANT with a DUAL in-flight pin: a per-session pin (an in-flight video visit drains across a flip) AND a per-device pin (an in-flight reading window drains) — two lifecycle-pin registries because two planes have two in-flight unit types.

SECURITY FIX (KU6 seam) — the marketplace platform seam had an UNGATED PHI read. apps/api/src/marketplace-platform-routes.ts carries a hosted entitlement gate whose 402 branch fires only when an `entitlementChecker` is injected, and the boot (apps/api/src/index.ts, the marketplacePlatformRoutes registration) injected only `entitlementReader` — which feeds endpoint (c) alone. The 402 branch was therefore DEAD in production, and GET /marketplace-platform/fhir/{resourceType} + /{resourceType}/{id} — an ANY-resourceType tenant-scoped read — served PHI to a tenant whose `marketplace` entitlement had lapsed. The theory that KU9 covered it does not hold: KU9 gates the marketplace-service's OWN publish/checkout/execute routes, not this seam. FIX: the boot now injects `entitlementChecker: productEntitlementChecker` (matching interop AW-3 / erx EU11), and the plugin exempts ONLY the entitlement read-back (c) — gating an entitlement QUERY on that entitlement is circular and would turn its documented SoR-404 → service-fallback into a 402 for exactly the tenants the fallback exists for; that route carries no PHI (tenant id + product slug). The exemption compares a $-normalized path so a percent-encoded %24read caller cannot land on the wrong branch. RED/GREEN in apps/api/src/marketplace-platform-routes.test.ts: a lapsed tenant now gets 402 on both the single-resource and the searchset back-read and on the secret broker, an entitled tenant still gets 200, and (c) still answers 404 (not 402) for a lapsed tenant in both the literal and percent-encoded forms. A source assertion pins the boot wiring so the dead-branch regression cannot return silently.

KU11 absorbed the duplicate copy carried in microservices-billing/ops-activation-closeout and now names the exact route to mount and the exact runtime to adapt, re-verified absent on main.

baseline.summary: BrandStyle built, tested, contrast-guarded, XSS-safe, and exported from @cernia/branding — but rendered in NO app layout, so the white-label promise (Wave-H completion / F2 / AE2) was unmet despite the code existing. No brand-color confirm marker existed anywhere.

current.summary: Code complete: the brand_color_confirmed_at marker is wired end-to-end and BrandStyle is mounted in admin/patient/web (NOT cernia-ops, R19), fail-closed so pre-existing/unconfirmed colors emit nothing. The two gates before a LIVE per-tenant recolor are both external to the theming work: the SSR resolver cannot be wired to the tenant-brand API as it stands (that route is authenticated; anonymous SSR has no credential — see remaining[0] for the unblocker), and browser acceptance needs a seeded stack.

remaining: BLOCKED, and the blocker is not in the apps. Wiring each app's configureDefaultResolver to the tenant-brand API is what this bullet asks for, and GET /tenants/:id/brand CANNOT SERVE IT: apps/api/src/tenant-brand-routes.ts:210-246 requires an authenticated principal bound to that tenant (401 unauthenticated, 403 cross-tenant, per ADR 0126's anti-enumeration posture). SSR brand resolution runs on the ANONYMOUS request — the login page is the surface a per-tenant recolor most needs to reach — so there is no credential to present. Confirmed unwired: configureDefaultResolver has zero non-test callers repo-wide, resolveBrand soft-falls-back to DEFAULT_CERNIA_BRAND on every request (packages/branding/src/ssr/resolve-brand.ts:355-360), and BrandStyle therefore renders nothing in admin/patient/web even though it is correctly mounted in all three. UNBLOCKER: a deliberate decision to expose an UNAUTHENTICATED brand-only read — resolvable by host/subdomain rather than by tenant id, returning colour + logo + brandColorConfirmedAt and nothing else. That discloses which tenant slugs exist and what they look like, which is exactly what the 403-not-404 posture on this route was chosen to prevent, so it is a security tradeoff to be made explicitly and not a wiring task.

Live-acceptance (ADR-0127 by original intent): browser-verified tenant recolor of a seeded confirmed-brand tenant on patient/admin/web + default-brand visual-regression-unchanged screenshot — needs a running seeded stack.

Fail-closed: unconfirmed/pre-existing colors emit no style tag (no deploy-day surprise recolor, KTD5). Admin branding page shows the AE2 'adjusted for contrast (WCAG AA)' + 'save to confirm' activation notices. Fixed admin tailwind hsl(var()) -> var() so the mounted vars recolor admin; deleted the superseded cernia-theme.css placeholder. Tests: core 821, branding 106 (brand-style 10), storage tenant-brand-store 25, api tenant-brand-routes 30 (incl. forgery-dropped). Status stays 'partial' because a LIVE recolor also needs the pre-existing SSR resolver lookup wired + a seeded-stack browser proof.

Investigated the SSR-resolver bullet rather than half-wiring it, and found it is not implementable as written. GET /tenants/:id/brand is authenticated (apps/api/src/tenant-brand-routes.ts, authorize() — 401 unauthenticated, 403 cross-tenant under ADR 0126 anti-enumeration). SSR brand resolution happens on the anonymous request, which is the whole point of a per-tenant recolor: the login page. So "wire configureDefaultResolver to the tenant-brand API" cannot be done without first deciding to expose an unauthenticated brand-only read keyed on host, which discloses tenant existence — the exact thing the 403-not-404 choice on that route protects. Bullet narrowed to name the unblocker instead of leaving it looking like unstarted wiring. Confirmed while there: zero non-test callers of configureDefaultResolver, resolveBrand soft-falling back everywhere, BrandStyle correctly mounted in admin/patient/web and correctly absent from cernia-ops.

Admin's card compat shim collapsed to a pure re-export 2026-08-03; badge and button cannot, for reasons now measured rather than assumed (a default-value recolor across 272 files, and a variant/size rename plus class drift). The two "known e2e selector carry-forwards" this bullet carried are STALE as of 2026-08-03 and removed: the installer stepper testids are fixed (packages/ui/src/wizard-shell.tsx:72,82 emit wizard-stepper and wizard-step-<id>, and tests/e2e/specs/onboarding-installer.spec.ts:125-127 expects exactly those), and the patient badge div->span change has no in-tree selector depending on the tag — a sweep of tests/e2e/specs and apps/patient/src for locator('div, div:has-text, div.rounded, tagName, toBe('DIV') and querySelector('div returns zero hits, every badge assertion being getByTestId or text-based. tracks.name: Specialty Taxonomy Unification
tracks.description: One specialty vocabulary across the platform, three orthogonal axes, NUCC-anchored (docs/prds/specialty-taxonomy-unification.md). Five disjoint lists had drifted apart because they described different kinds of thing: onboarding (9 values conflating specialty + org type + care setting), scribe (11 template tags), k5-specialty-role-templates (25 RBAC keys), voice-agent (75 patient-speech phrases) and catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos (83 orphaned NUCC codes). packages/specialty-taxonomy is now the canonical source; consumers migrate one at a time, each keeping its current behaviour.

stages.name: Stage 1 — Canonical taxonomy package (consumed by nobody)
stages.rationale: PRD Rollout step 1: ship the vocabulary as a pure addition — 42 clinical specialties + 3 escape hatches, 8 org types, 8 CMS-POS-anchored care settings, one merged alias table (clinical free text + patient speech + NUCC codes, longest-alias-first), a conservative resolver that returns undefined rather than guessing, and the legacy mapping tables. A leaf package with zero @cernia dependencies so every consumer can import it without a cycle.

baseline.summary: Five disjoint specialty vocabularies, no shared definition, no shared alias table. A tenant onboarded as `dental` still got the SOAP note default because nothing joined onboarding's value to scribe's tags.

current.summary: packages/specialty-taxonomy ships the full surface (specialties, org types, care settings, aliases, NUCC codes, resolver, ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP / SCRIBE_TAG_MAP / K5_MAP, version stamps). Retroactively tracked — Stage 1 landed without a status entry.

history.note: Stage 1 shipped as commit fefa5c67 (PR #648) but left NO production-readiness entry — this track is the retroactive record, added by Stage 2B. packages/specialty-taxonomy/src/{specialties,org-types,care-settings,aliases,nucc-codes,resolver,legacy-maps,version,types,index}.ts. Data corrections carried in the package (upstream untouched): 367500000X is the CRNA; 363LP2300X is NP Primary Care; 207N00000X is dermatology; scribe's alias table had pointed rheumatology's 207RR0500X at cardiology.

stages.name: Stage 2 — Consumers migrate one at a time, behaviour unchanged
stages.rationale: PRD Rollout step 2: each consumer imports the shared vocabulary and deletes its local one, KEEPING its current behaviour. What unifies is the vocabulary definition and the alias table; each consumer's legacy output strings survive at its own edge via the mapping tables, because those strings are matched against persisted data and live tenant records. No user-visible change in this stage.

baseline.summary: packages/specialty-taxonomy was imported by NOBODY. All five local vocabularies still live, still free to drift. Also: apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts carried a hand-copied duplicate of scribe's 11 tags with the comment "Kept in sync here (admin does not depend on @cernia/scribe)" — the drift risk named in its own source.

current.summary: All four package consumers migrated (2A: scribe + apps/admin; 2B: voice-agent, k5-specialty-role-templates, onboarding), and as of Stage 1b every consumer union is DERIVED at the type level too — ScribeLegacyTag, apps/admin SpecialtyTag, k5 Specialty and onboarding Specialty are each `keyof typeof <MAP>`, so a specialty list outside packages/specialty-taxonomy is now unrepresentable rather than test-caught. Every local specialty vocabulary in the monorepo is now gone, catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos included: as of 2026-07-29 its src/nucc-taxonomy.ts is DELETED (65 of its 82 codes were already in the taxonomy; the other 17 are suppliers, facility subtypes and provider roles that no SPECIALTY or ORG_TYPE references, so the taxonomy's own R3 test forbade folding them), and packages/catalog-abms-credentialing was cleared as NOT a specialty vocabulary at all — it is credentialing data with no NUCC code, slug, alias or resolver — so it is kept as-is rather than folded or deleted. packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.ts is a thin adapter over matchSpecialty() + SCRIBE_TAG_MAP (37-entry local ALIASES table DELETED); apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts depends on the leaf package directly, retiring the hand-copied 11-tag duplicate that carried the comment "Kept in sync here". apps/api/src/scribe-clinician-specialty.ts needed NO change — both consumed exports kept their signatures. Persisted tag strings are unchanged platform-wide. Stage stays `partial` for the three follow-ups below (the voice-agent legacy back-map, the accepted narrowing's live re-verification, and the two mapping bug fixes owed a real-tenant spot-check) — no longer because a rival vocabulary remains.

evidence.label: scribe adapter over the shared vocabulary

remaining: Voice-agent back-map is a bridge, not an end state: packages/specialty-taxonomy folds obstetrics/gynecology, hematology/oncology, orthopedics and surgery, so LEGACY_CODE_BY_SLUG in packages/voice-agent/src/practitioner-directory.ts maps canonical slugs back to the PractitionerRole.code labels live tenant directories actually contain. It deletes itself once tenant PractitionerRole data is migrated onto canonical slugs.

Two mapping bug fixes and two NARROWED specialty families still owe ONE live check, and it is the same check for all four. The fixes: "Pediatric Dentistry" / NUCC 1223P0221X used to resolve to the pediatrics MEDICAL template and now resolves to dentistry; NUCC 207RR0500X (Rheumatology) was mapped to cardiology in the deleted scribe table and now returns undefined. The narrowings: counselor titles now land on system-psychotherapy and pediatric-emergency/hospital titles on system-emergency-medicine / system-hospital-medicine rather than on the psychiatry or general-pediatrics templates they used to be stamped with. ALL of it is proven twice already — in-process against the REAL built dist of packages/specialty-taxonomy + packages/scribe (all four display names resolve to a real template, none to SOAP), and over the REAL HTTP API (:8090, tenant scribe-harness, real bearer): GET /scribe/templates 200 with 26 templates including all three system-* ids. WHAT IS STILL OWED, and it is one thing: no live $draft has been run by a clinician actually CARRYING one of these specialties, so the specialty->template tier was exercised directly rather than through a real note. The residual risk is confined to the resolution CHAIN ORDER (personal / visit-type / facility / practice tiers overriding the specialty tier), never to whether the templates exist or the aliases map.

history.note: Stage 2C — the two orphaned specialty-adjacent vocabularies are resolved, and they got DIFFERENT answers because they are different things. (1) packages/catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos: DELETED src/nucc-taxonomy.ts + src/nucc-taxonomy.test.ts, buildPractitionerWithTaxonomy and the NUCC_SYSTEM/NPI_SYSTEM/FhirPractitioner/FhirHumanName/FhirIdentifier scaffolding in src/fhir-builders.ts, the NuccTaxonomyCode and PractitionerInput types in src/types.ts, their barrel exports in src/index.ts, and the NUCC sections of README.md. The package survives as what its NAME says — CPT modifiers + Place of Service + pricing engine + Claim/Encounter builders. The decision rested on a measured diff, not an assumption: of the catalog's 82 unique codes (the tracked bullet said 83), 65 were ALREADY in the taxonomy, and the 17 that were not are suppliers, facility subtypes and provider roles rather than practice specialties. Because the taxonomy's R3 test fails on any code no SPECIALTY or ORG_TYPE references, folding those 17 would have BROKEN the package that is supposed to be frozen — the invariant made folding illegal, not just pointless. And the file was not inert: 7 of the 65 shared codes were mislabelled upstream (PRD R4's three, plus 1223P0700X, which is Prosthodontics and not Pediatric Dentistry), while getTaxonomyBySpecialty/searchTaxonomy formed a second specialty-resolution API that resolved 'Dermatology' to the dermatopathology code — a live trap for the next developer who imported it. (2) packages/catalog-abms-credentialing: KEPT, neither folded nor deleted. It carries no NUCC code, slug, alias or resolution function, so it never was a sixth specialty vocabulary and does not violate R1; board -> certification -> subspecialty is credentialing (what an individual is certified for), a different shape from the taxonomy's practice axis, and folding it in would have corrupted that model to avoid a deletion. Deletion was rejected on measurement rather than sentiment: 60 of the repo's 70 catalog-* packages have zero workspace consumers, so 'no consumer' singles this one out only by accident of which package the PRD happened to name, and the data behind it is real — 24 boards, 114 subspecialty relationships, 52 state/territory licences, working DEA check-digit and NPI Luhn validators with algorithmic tests. It did, however, FAIL tsc --build on baseline (credentialing-workflow.ts(304,5) TS2322, a stateResults literal widening status to string); preserving a package for a future consumer is only honest if it compiles, so that one-line cast is fixed. NO migration, no slug/tier/alias/legacy-map change, and the only edit inside packages/specialty-taxonomy is a comment: nucc-codes.ts's R4 note used to say fixing the upstream labels was 'a later stage's job' and pointed at a file that no longer exists. Verification, same-tree baseline vs after: @cernia/specialty-taxonomy 78 tests pass (unchanged), @cernia/catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos 146 -> 106 tests pass across 4 -> 3 files (40 removed with the deleted nucc-taxonomy suite and the 5 buildPractitionerWithTaxonomy cases, zero failures, no surviving assertion edited), @cernia/catalog-abms-credentialing typecheck+build now clean where the baseline FAILED, @cernia/api typecheck clean at 0 errors (it never imported either package, so there is no path for this change to reach it), and pnpm -r --no-bail --filter './packages/**' build goes from 4 failures to 2 (302 packages build clean). Baseline failures were r-mobile-ios-foundation, catalog-abms-credentialing, connectors and p1c-ml-model-registry; catalog-abms-credentialing is fixed here and connectors was a first-run ordering artifact that clears once the workspace has been built once. The 2 survivors are pre-existing, unrelated and carried forward. ZERO new failures — specialty-taxonomy, catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos, catalog-abms-credentialing and connectors all report 'build: Done'.

Stage 1b — the last hand-written specialty list is gone, at the TYPE level. Four consumers still spelled their literal union out by hand (packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.ts ScribeLegacyTag, apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts SpecialtyTag, packages/k5-specialty-role-templates/src/types.ts Specialty, packages/onboarding/src/types.ts Specialty) because the three tables in packages/specialty-taxonomy/src/legacy-maps.ts were ANNOTATED Readonly<Record<string, ...>>, which erases the keys — Object.freeze was never the culprit, the annotation was. The maps are now declared with `satisfies` instead (ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP additionally goes through a mapped type over keyof typeof ONBOARDING_LEGACY_ENTRIES so its VALUES stay pinned to OnboardingLegacyMapping and an entry with specialties: [] does not infer never[] for Stage 3). Each union is now `keyof typeof <MAP>`, so a specialty list declared outside the taxonomy package is unrepresentable rather than merely test-caught — the PRD constraint is enforced by tsc. PROOF, and the failure mode that matters: each of the four consumer sources carries a @ts-expect-error negative type test asserting that `not-a-specialty` is rejected; if the keys ever erase back to `string` the union collapses to `string`, every other check still passes, and the now-unused directive fails the build. Falsified deliberately by re-annotating the maps: scribe src/specialty-match.ts(103,1), k5 src/types.ts(89,1), onboarding src/types.ts(407,1) and admin src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts(58,1) all reported TS2578 Unused @ts-expect-error directive. dental-restorative (PRD R13, the only key mapped to undefined) is a REQUIRED property of type `undefined`, so it survives keyof and Object.keys — asserted by a positive type test in scribe + admin and re-verified at runtime through matchSpecialtyTag. ZERO RUNTIME CHANGE, proven by diffing the emitted dist JS before/after: the only non-comment delta in any of the four files is ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP becoming an alias binding to the identical frozen object (Object.freeze moved onto a private ONBOARDING_LEGACY_ENTRIES const). Key ORDER untouched, so SPECIALTY_TAGS / ALL_SPECIALTIES / LEGACY_SPECIALTIES and the admin Specialty <select> render identically. One drift-guard test DELETED as tautological: onboarding types.test.ts "every legacy value is assignable to the Specialty union" — its body was `const all: readonly Specialty[] = LEGACY_SPECIALTIES`, an assignment that could never fail because LEGACY_SPECIALTIES is DECLARED readonly Specialty[], and vitest does not typecheck, so the "compile-time half of the lock" it advertised was never executed by anything; its only real assertion, toHaveLength(9), is subsumed by the byte-identical-to-pre-migration test beside it. Every other drift-guard test is KEPT and its stale comment corrected: they assert runtime VALUES and ORDER, which Object.keys erases to string[] and which the type system therefore still cannot see. Verification: @cernia/specialty-taxonomy build + 78 tests, @cernia/scribe typecheck/build + 302 tests, @cernia/k5-specialty-role-templates typecheck + 256 tests (incl. real-Postgres store), @cernia/onboarding typecheck + 182 tests, @cernia/api typecheck clean, @cernia/admin typecheck clean + 1761 tests. No assertion edited anywhere.

Stage 2B — three consumers migrated, zero output strings changed. (1) packages/voice-agent/src/practitioner-directory.ts: the 75-phrase SPECIALTY_TAXONOMY literal is DELETED; matchSpecialty now delegates to matchSpecialtyText and maps the canonical slug back to today's FHIR PractitionerRole.code via LEGACY_CODE_BY_SLUG (+ LEGACY_CODE_BY_ALIAS for the two folded slugs, since obstetrics-gynecology must answer 'obstetrics' for "obstetrician" and 'gynecology' for "gynecologist"); a slug with no legacy code returns null, so the emitted vocabulary cannot grow. SPECIALTY_TAXONOMY survives as a DERIVED view over TEXT_ALIASES. Regression found and fixed by the equivalence proof: the shared package marks "ent"/"gp"/"gyno"/"er doctor" exact-only (they are substrings of "dentist"/"urgent care"/"other doctor"), which silently broke "the ENT" and "the gyno" — the most natural phone phrasings; matchShortTokenAlias restores them with WORD-BOUNDARY matching, run only after the resolver declines, so longest-alias-first still wins. New proof: packages/voice-agent/src/practitioner-directory.legacy-equivalence.test.ts pins all 75 pre-migration phrases bare AND padded into an utterance. (2) packages/k5-specialty-role-templates/src/types.ts: ALL_SPECIALTIES derived from K5_MAP keys — 25 RBAC keys unchanged and in the same order, so no role template can be orphaned. (3) packages/onboarding/src/types.ts: LEGACY_SPECIALTIES derived from ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP keys and wired into validateUseCase in wizard-orchestrator.ts; the `Specialty` type name is deliberately NOT renamed because apps/installer's use-case wizard page imports it by name. Persisted shapes, step schemas and UseCaseStepData.specialty are byte-identical.

Stage 2A — scribe + admin migrated, completing the package-consumer set. packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.ts: the private 37-entry ALIASES table is DELETED; SPECIALTY_TAGS derives from Object.keys(SCRIBE_TAG_MAP); matchSpecialtyTag is now exact-tag self-match -> matchSpecialty() -> inverted SCRIBE_TAG_MAP, with the exact-tag check FIRST because SCRIBE_TAG_MAP deliberately maps dental-restorative to undefined (PRD R13: a procedure type, not a specialty) yet the tag must still round-trip. apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts drops its hand-copied duplicate and depends on the dependency-free leaf package directly — no transpilePackages entry needed, it resolves from dist. apps/api/src/scribe-clinician-specialty.ts unchanged (verified, not cosmetically touched). Behaviour measured two ways: an 820-string corpus sweep plus a reverse sweep of all 34 keys of the deleted table. 33 inputs NEWLY resolve that previously returned undefined (patient-speech phrases such as "heart doctor" and "skin doctor" plus 14 NUCC subspecialty codes) — pure broadening, and safe in one direction only: the shared resolver can turn undefined into a correct specialty, never into a wrong one. Four families changed rather than broadened; see the two PRODUCT DECISION / BUG FIX bullets in `remaining`. Regression locks packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.test.ts and apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.test.ts both pass with no assertion edited.

CLOSURE PASS — 5 remaining bullets to 2, and three of the five were closed by work that had ALREADY LANDED. (1) The catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos bullet described its own completion: verified on main that packages/catalog-cpt-modifiers-pos/src/ no longer contains nucc-taxonomy.ts or its test (the directory holds only cpt-modifiers, pos-codes, pricing-engine, fhir-builders, types, index), so the rival 82-code specialty vocabulary and its second resolution API (getTaxonomyBySpecialty / searchTaxonomy) are gone — commit f4fddc01 / PR #663. Moved to history rather than left on a punch list it had stopped describing. (2) Same for the catalog-abms-credentialing bullet: verified the package is present and intact (24 boards, state-licence and DEA/NPI validators, src/credentialing-workflow.ts carrying the TS2322 fix), and that it holds no NUCC code, slug, alias table or resolver — it is credentialing data, not a specialty vocabulary, so KEPT-AS-IS was the decision and there is nothing outstanding. Same commit. (3) The accepted-narrowing bullet and the mapping-bug-fix bullet were asking for the SAME evidence — a live check against real tenant data — so they are MERGED into one, keeping the sharper statement of what is actually owed (a live $draft by a clinician who carries one of the affected specialties, i.e. the chain-order tier) and dropping ~4.5 KB of narrative that recorded already-paid debts. The voice-agent LEGACY_CODE_BY_SLUG bridge stays open and was re-verified present at packages/voice-agent/src/practitioner-directory.ts.

stages.name: Stages 3-5 — Tenant projection, resolution tier, specialty templates
stages.rationale: PRD Rollout steps 3-5. Stage 3 splits onboarding's conflated 9-value field onto the three axes and migrates existing tenants with a DISMISSIBLE confirm prompt (R15/R16 — no tenant is blocked, and a tenant with no specialty behaves exactly as today). Stage 4 adds the resolution tier + relevance filter behind a per-tenant flag, with 'show all' shipping WITH the filter, never after it. Stage 5 ships specialty note templates in tier order.

baseline.summary: No tenant carries specialty/org-type/care-setting on the new axes; no confirm prompt; no relevance filter; templates limited to scribe's original tags.

current.summary: STAGE 4 IS COMPLETE — the headline defect R10 is closed. A dental tenant whose clinician carries no Practitioner.qualification and whose practice set no default now drafts on the DENTISTRY template instead of SOAP, because apps/api/src/note-template-store.ts resolveForClinician gained two rungs below the clinician-specialty match: `tenant-specialty` (the practice's own declared specialty, R10) and `care-setting` (R11's (*, care_setting) rung — the SNF round note without a fictional snf-internal-medicine specialty). Both read tenant_specialty_profiles (migration 328) through an INJECTED store, so a caller that injects none cannot change behaviour at all, which is R15's regression guard by construction rather than by inspection. GET /scribe/templates now orders by tenant relevance with the full library shipped in the SAME response under `hidden` (R8/R9 — one action, no second round trip) plus ?all=true for the flat pre-Stage-4 list; tenant-authored templates and SOAP are never filtered. The per-tenant gate is now a REAL COLUMN (migration 329, 2026-07-29): scribe_tenant_config.specialty_relevance_enabled, tri-state so NULL keeps the pre-329 derived answer (a settled profile: needs_confirm = FALSE), TRUE forces it on and FALSE turns it off even for a confirmed profile — the state the derived gate could not express. The same migration widened the template_source CHECK so `tenant-specialty` and `care-setting` PERSIST as themselves instead of being flattened onto `specialty`, and the recorder chip names them apart. The admin Specialty picker gap Stage 5 opened is closed: it now offers every template-bearing specialty and persists the CANONICAL SLUG, with existing legacy-tag values deliberately NOT migrated. The stage stays `partial` only because the Stage-5 template tail and the four Stage-3/GA follow-ups below remain open. LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30: test family F2 (docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md section 5) executed all EIGHT rungs of resolveForClinician over real HTTP — 15/15 — asserting the PERSISTED scribe_sessions.template_source by direct Postgres query, with a decoy default on the tier above wherever one is possible so no rung passed by elimination. Its first run found 172 unmapped tenant-facing routes; 101 were mapped in the same change. WHAT IS STILL OWED, and neither piece is a mapping: (a) 71 routes stay unmapped ON PURPOSE and are enumerated with a per-family reason in ACCEPTED_UNMAPPED -- the largest group is an OPERATOR-ONLY family served under a TENANT prefix (/admin/tenants* CRUD + transitions + invitations + lifecycle + metrics + exports, plus /policies, /grace/*, /trials/*, /scale/*, /api/o4/*, /api/o6/*), which is unreachable by ANYONE today because the operator pass is scoped to /cernia-ops/* and a tenant grant would be the WRONG fix; the rest are external signature/JWT-gated callers needing an allow-list decision (CDS Hooks, the RPM device webhook, GET /metrics), the authed MFA phone-verify pair needing the self-service pass, and seven patient-vs-staff self-service operations whose correct principal is undecided. (b) 13 routes are mapped but onto a CUSTOM verb no default role grants (ACCEPTED_UNBOUND_VERB) -- admin:tenants:erase / admin:tenants:read on the five erasure routes, admin:patient-portal-links:* on the six portal-credential routes, and connection.replay + connection.run -- so they 403 a tenant-admin today despite looking registered. Both lists are asserted EXACTLY in both directions, so a new gap fails the build and a closed one cannot rot in the list -- PROVEN 2026-07-29 when the reverse assertion independently went red on POST /dev/checkout-grant after that route was allow-listed, forcing the stale entry out. CORRECTION 2026-07-29 to the (a) rationale above: "each of these files states in its header that it is gated to cernia-super-admin" is NOT true of every member, and the exception is the dangerous one. apps/api/src/llm-observability-routes.ts (/api/o4/cost, /api/o4/budgets/:id) carries NO in-route gate at all -- no requireSuperAdmin, no requirePermission, no preHandler, no rbacClaims check -- and its tenantOf(req, fallback) at :52-58 returns the CALLER-SUPPLIED ?tenantId= BEFORE consulting the header. Today that is harmless ONLY because unmapped means the deny-all catch-all denies it, so the route is unreachable. It is therefore a trap primed to fire on the obvious fix: the natural response to "this route 403s" is to map it, and the moment anyone does, any authenticated caller reads another tenant cross-tenant LLM spend with no second line of defence. So for /api/o4/* specifically, unmapped is LOAD-BEARING rather than merely accepted; before it is ever mapped the route needs its own operator gate AND tenantOf must stop trusting the query string. The corrected rationale is recorded in the ACCEPTED_UNMAPPED header block.

(b) THE SIGN IS NOT ATOMIC, and idempotent replay newly makes that LOOK successful. The path is Composition update, then DocumentReference create, then Provenance create, then the session row; a crash between the first two leaves the replay branch answering 200 forever on a note that has no DocumentReference and was never pushed to the EHR. Pre-existing non-atomicity, newly reachable in a shape that reads as success. The narrow fix is for the replay branch to verify the downstream artifacts exist rather than trusting Composition.status alone (or for the sign to become one transaction); $push-to-ehr already covers the write-back leg.

SCRIBE CONSENT WITHDRAWAL — THE AUDIO QUESTION IS RULED (2026-07-31, ADR 0153, PR #744): a withdrawal DESTROYS the captured audio. A destruction whose object-store delete fails is retryable work, found by deriving the due set from scribe_recording_consents.decision=revoked — but the only automatic driver is the retention sweep, which is OFF unless CERNIA_SCRIBE_RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS is set. On a deployment that never arms it, a failed destruction is retried only by a repeat POST /$revoke-consent. Either arm the sweep in the production runbook or give destruction its own timer. (c) NO OPERATOR SURFACE lists pending destructions; scribeAudioDestructionsDue() exists and nothing in apps/cernia-ops calls it, so "which patients asked us to delete audio that we have not deleted" is a SQL question today. (d) PER-PATIENT ERASURE ADR still not written — ADR 0140 remains tenant-aggregate only, and this per-session destruction deliberately does not go through the erasure executor or its retention floor (ADR 0153 explains why).
