history.note: J04 CONSENT-DECLINE SEAM — A PATIENT'S REFUSAL TO BE RECORDED IS NOW A RECORDABLE FACT. Consent was the PRESENCE OF A ROW (migration 305), so a patient who refused and a visit nobody ever asked about were the same database state: the product could honour a refusal but never PROVE it had. Measured live on github/main 47d679f5 it was worse than unmodelled — POST /scribe/sessions/:id/consent {decision:'declined'} answered 201 and recorded an AFFIRMATIVE, after which audio was accepted (202), the audio object assembled (200), the audio downloadable (200) and the transcript readable (200) on the refused session; a second clinician's bodyless POST also returned 200 and the note then drafted. Migration 338 adds decision (granted|declined|revoked) + decided_by/decided_at + revoked_at/revoked_by to scribe_recording_consents (attested_by/attested_at nullable: a decline never had an attestation; a revocation KEEPS them beside revoked_at because those two together are the only evidence the audio already captured was captured lawfully) plus an append-only scribe_recording_consent_events table so a change of mind cannot erase the refusal. hasConsent() is now true ONLY for decision='granted', so all 17 consent-gated route guards close on declined AND revoked with no route change — the sweep was RE-PROVED on both states after the change (17/17 → 403 consent-required, zero artifacts) alongside the never-asked control and the consented control. POST /consent now takes {decision} and 400s anything unrecognised (a bodyless post still means granted — the shipped recorder contract); POST /$revoke-consent is the withdrawal; GET /consent is the audit read. Consent decisions are OWNER-gated like $cancel. A declined session is the new terminal status 'declined' instead of sitting in the clinician's list as 'recording' with a live Record button, and getDraft propagates the API's own 403 reason instead of flattening every 403 to 'forbidden' — the clause J04 actually failed on, re-measured first (PR #723 had not reached it). Live BROKEN→FIXED evidence with the same runner, DB and fixtures: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/j04-consent-broken.json (3/12) vs j04-consent-fixed.json (13/13), summary + 4 browser screenshots in j04-consent-summary.md.

SCRIBE TEST FAMILIES F3 (consent/AE1, 8/8) + F8 (HIL sign gate, 7/9) EXECUTED ON THE ⚙️ REAL-HTTP + 🗄️ DIRECT-POSTGRES CHANNELS — and the two P0 fixes from 2026-07-29 are now proven on the channel the plan actually accepts. WHY IT MATTERED: §0.1 already recorded D1 and D5 as fixed, but BOTH proofs used Fastify inject with a stubbed rbacClaims, which docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md §1 explicitly rejects as ⚙️ evidence — the same shape of test that let ten routes ship 403-ing every real caller. D5 HOLDS (F3-05): with a scribe_transcripts row seeded directly (the seam that made the exploit possible) and NO consent row, all five write-path steps refuse 403 {error:'consent-required'} — $draft, PUT /draft, $after-visit-summary, $sign, $push-to-ehr — and a direct query confirms nothing was minted (composition_ref NULL, 0 DocumentReferences, 0 scribe-sign Provenances, ehr_writeback_status NULL, session never 'signed', 0 consent rows). F3-07 is the FALSIFYING CONTROL: with consent the same chain completes 201/200/200/201/200/200 and reaches 'final', so this is a gate that discriminates rather than one that refuses everybody. F3-08 confirms the deliberate $amend carve-out survives deleting the consent row (200). D1 HOLDS (F8-06): the second $sign answers 200 alreadySigned:true with ZERO artifact drift — Composition version_id 2→2, DocumentReferences 1→1, scribe-sign Provenances 1→1, total Provenances 3→3, ehr_writeback_at byte-identical. F8-06b: after $amend a re-sign is 409 already-signed and the note is STILL 'amended' in the database, never reverted to 'final'. Artifacts were COUNTED, not statuses — a status-only assertion passes on the unfixed code too, which is exactly how D1 shipped. NEW P0 DEFECT D14 (open, from case F8-04b which was NOT in the plan): the KTD5 storage guard covers 'final' but NOT 'amended'. packages/storage/src/scribe-sign-guard.ts:58 returns early unless status === 'final', while the route gate treats final AND amended as post-signature states (isSignedStatus, packages/scribe/src/sign-gate.ts:33). So POST /Composition with {status:'amended', meta.tag=[scribe-note]} is 201 CREATED AND PERSISTED — a signed legal record minted outside the clinician sign action, bypassing the owner check, the clinician-role check, AE1 consent, the Provenance and the DocumentReference. The lesson is sharper than the bug: D1's OWN FIX on 2026-07-29 widened this predicate at the route layer and did not mirror it onto the storage layer, and packages/storage/src/scribe-sign-guard.test.ts has never contained the word 'amended', so nothing failed. When a predicate is duplicated across two enforcement layers, widening one is a defect in the other. NOT FIXED HERE — this change is the harness and the red. D4 HALF-REPRODUCED, HALF WITHDRAWN (F8-04): a 'final' scribe-tagged Composition over HTTP → 500 with a FHIR OperationOutcome severity=fatal code=exception where a 403 belongs, so the status-mapping half is real and now has a baseline. The INVARIANT HELD (0 rows persisted, confirmed independently by a manual probe) and the guard is correctly SCOPED — the untagged-'final' control is accepted 201, which is what makes the 500 attributable to the scribe guard rather than to a generally broken POST /Composition. BUT D4's 'leaking the exception message' claim is NOT reproducible on current code: diagnostics is a generic 'An unexpected error occurred.'. That half of the defect row is withdrawn, which narrows the fix to error-code mapping and removes the information-disclosure argument for prioritising it. FIVE PLAN CORRECTIONS, all recorded in place: F3/F8 are 8 and 9 cases (an earlier brief said 5 and 7); the chunk body is {index,dataBase64} not {chunkIndex}; $amend takes addendumText not text; PUT /draft takes {title,text} validated against the note's EXISTING section titles; and a correctly-signed note carries THREE Provenances (draft + edit + scribe-sign), so a count===1 assertion FAILS ON CORRECT CODE — the discriminating filter is activity.text='scribe-sign'. The first three all 400 BEFORE the gate under test, so each would have made a case fail (or pass) for a reason unrelated to what it asserts. STACK, and it is load-bearing: commit cc7944c1 (boot stamp gitSha matched HEAD), API :8153, Postgres :5433/scribe_f1, STT stub, LLM ollama/qwen→qwen3-vl:8b-instruct, CERNIA_LLM_ROUTING=primary-fallback, CERNIA_ENFORCE_ORG_SCOPE=1. The port/DB pairing was PROVED not assumed — a throwaway tenant's /dev/login on :8153 wrote 18 rows to scribe_f1 and 0 to scribe_e2e. That check is not ceremonial here: apps/api/.env names DB_NAME=scribe_e2e, so a failed env override would have run every consent assertion against the wrong database and still looked green. The env now lives in ONE file that both the boot script and the runner source, and the runner writes the stack into the artifact from its own process.env, so §0.3 cannot claim a stack the API did not boot with. THREE TEST-SIDE BUGS ARE RECORDED IN §7 because each impersonated a product finding, and all three are the same failure mode — an assertion wrong in a direction that looks like a defect: (1) a sentinel string containing a literal NUL byte used as a SQL LIKE parameter, which Postgres rejects with SQLSTATE 22021 and which surfaced mid-F3-05 as a stack trace that read like a product crash; (2) `count === 1` on Provenances, which FAILS ON CORRECT CODE since a signed note carries three — reported as F8-01/F8-02/F8-06 failures on the first run; (3) a falsifying CONTROL sharing a title prefix with its SUBJECT, so F8-04 counted the control it was supposed to exclude and the artifact said persistedFinalRows=1, reading like a KTD5 breach that had not happened. The lesson kept in the plan: a control and its subject must never share a matching prefix, and an invariant should be reported as its own field rather than folded into a pass/fail boolean.

D1 (P0 clinical-record defect) CLOSED — `POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$sign` could sign an ALREADY-SIGNED session. apps/api/src/scribe-sign-routes.ts passed a hard-coded `currentStatus:'preliminary'` into assertSignAllowed, which made packages/scribe/src/sign-gate.ts's `post-sign-immutable` branch unreachable from the ONLY route that can mint a `final` note; the sole other guard (`409 no-draft`) fires on a null composition_ref, which a signed session does not have. A second call therefore re-wrote the Composition, minted a SECOND DocumentReference, wrote a SECOND Provenance and RE-FIRED the EHR write-back — a duplicate signed legal note in the patient's chart AND a duplicate document pushed into the practice's EHR. FIX: the route now READS the Composition before the gate and passes its real status. The Composition was judged the authoritative signature record over scribe_sessions.status, because the session row is a mirror the route updates LAST and can therefore lag a note that is already `final` — exactly the partial-failure shape in which the duplicate is minted. BEHAVIOUR: an already-`final` note whose session is `signed` REPLAYS the existing result (200 + `alreadySigned:true`, nothing written), because at the HTTP layer a retry of a lost 200 is indistinguishable from a deliberate re-sign and rejecting would strand a note the clinician believes is unsigned; a note that has moved PAST its signature is refused `409 already-signed` — 409 not 403 because the caller is fully authorised and it is the RESOURCE STATE that forbids the transition, consistent with $amend / $push-to-ehr (`409 not-signed`) and PUT /draft (`409 post-sign-immutable`). A SECOND, UNREPORTED defect surfaced while fixing: sign-gate's immutability branch tested only `final`, so re-signing an `amended` note — the state $amend leaves composition_ref pointing at — passed the gate and would have REVERTED a legally amended note to `final` plus minted another document. Generalized to isSignedStatus() (`final`|`amended`), which also stops a signed note being reverted to a draft. PROOF: apps/api/src/scribe-sign-routes.integration.test.ts describe `D1 — repeat $sign never duplicates the signed record` counts ARTIFACTS rather than status codes (Composition writes, DocumentReferences, Provenances, EHR pushes) and was watched RED on main — "expected [ { …(5) }, { …(5) } ] to have a length of 1 but got 2" — alongside a red `409` assertion for the amended case; plus 5 new sign-gate unit tests (red first) and a real sign→$amend chain test proving the legitimate post-sign path still works. That suite also now bootstraps migration 316 so the EHR write-back count is real, narrowing D8 for this file. VERIFIED: @cernia/scribe 371/371, all 44 apps/api scribe suites 495/495, @cernia/api typecheck + build clean; the one lint error on scribe-sign-routes.ts (`require-await` on scribeSignRoutes) is carry-forward, proven present on baseline via `git stash push` of that single file.

Surfaces an unanswered product question (manual clinical findings like fundal height have no write path under strict device-only) and an enforcement gap (the sign guard only covers Composition). Migration 329's tri-state flag became SELF-SERVE: apps/admin/src/app/admin/settings/practice-profile/page.tsx now renders the control a tenant admin was missing, so flipping specialty-relevance no longer requires an operator with direct API access. Shipped as a THREE-option select (testid `relevance-enabled`), deliberately NOT a checkbox: `scribe_tenant_config.specialty_relevance_enabled` is tri-state and the third state is not a polite 'off' — it is 'never chose', which TRACKS the practice profile (on once needs_confirm clears, off while it has not) and is the state every tenant is in today. A checkbox would have to render it as one of the two explicit answers, misreporting what the tenant is actually getting and deleting the only route back to it once touched. The page also states which way the default currently resolves for THIS tenant (testid `relevance-default-explainer`), read off the saved profile rather than guessed, so an admin does not have to experiment on live notes to find out. WIRE CONTRACT, and the subtle part: the unset state is carried by ABSENCE, not by a null — the server omits `relevanceEnabled` entirely for a tenant that never chose (R15: an unset tenant's response is byte-identical to pre-329). So the client types it `relevanceEnabled?: boolean` and NOT `boolean | null`, and the save OMITS the key when the admin did not move the control (server reads absent as 'leave it alone') while sending an explicit `null` when they return it to the default (server reads null as 'clear the choice'). Those are three distinct instructions and apps/admin/.../practice-profile-api.ts builds the PUT body key-by-key rather than letting JSON.stringify erase an undefined, so the distinction does not rest on implicit behaviour. ANTI-SILENT-FAILURE: the control renders from the SERVER's echo after a save, never the optimistic local pick, and an 'unsaved' marker (testid `relevance-unsaved`) stays lit whenever the draft diverges from stored — so a failed write cannot leave the switch standing there showing a value that never landed. No new API route and no new deriveOperation mapping: GET/PUT /admin/practice-profile were already mapped to read|write TenantSpecialtyProfile in apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts. Tests: apps/admin/src/app/admin/settings/practice-profile/page.test.tsx +10 (25 total) pinning all three states in both directions, the omit-vs-null distinction, the failed-save marker, and server-echo-wins. RBAC completeness gate generalised from /scribe/* to the WHOLE API, and the blast radius it exposed measured and partly closed. NEW: apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.repo-coverage.test.ts. It walks every `<instance>.<method>(` call in all 623 non-test modules under apps/api/src -- skipping a generic argument list, resolving a `${CONST}` template prefix against the file's own string constants -- and finds 972 route declarations across 253 files. It then subtracts the FIVE places registerRbacHook authorises OUTSIDE the RBAC model (the unauth allow-list INCLUDING buildApp's boot-time extension of it, TEST_MODE_DISABLE_RBAC, the service-identity branch, the self-introspection pass, the platform-operator pass) and fails on any remaining route that lands on the deny-all catch-all, OR that is mapped onto a verb no default role grants. THE SCRAPER IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, so it is guarded rather than trusted: a >900 route floor, a >200 file floor, eight named routes from unrelated families each exercising a different registration style, and an EXACT list of the one declaration it cannot resolve statically (observability-middleware.ts's config-driven Prometheus scrape path -- its default GET /metrics is scraped from index.ts anyway). Reading only the module-level permitAllForUnauthenticatedRoutes would have reported four boot-exempt families as broken, so the boot extension is scraped from index.ts too, with an assertion that the block was found. THE FINDING: 172 tenant-facing routes across ~49 modules had NO mapping and were 403ing before their handler -- the same defect as billing-write, the developer portal and the ten scribe routes, at 17x the scale. 101 were mapped here in 27 families whose route-file headers name apps/admin or the clinic UI as the consumer (email templates, schedule import, telehealth visits, RPM clinic reads, voice budget, ML pipeline + drift, LLM gateway, billing alert queue, usage thresholds, marketplace entitlements, revenue recognition, surveys, setup tasks, MEDD, tenant secrets/brand assets/custom-domain/SMTP, the remaining /admin/billing surface, workflow+bot $run, cross-org report, referral fax log, voice ingress). Verb rule applied per route and stated in the code: collection GET -> search, item GET -> read, mutating POST/PUT/PATCH -> write, DELETE -> delete, and a POST that is PURE COMPUTE over caller-supplied input -> read, because mapping a read as a write would lock tenant-member (which holds only *:read / *:search) out of something it should see. The block is APPENDED AT THE END of the if-chain deliberately: every path in it previously resolved to the catch-all, so it cannot swallow an earlier branch -- and the neighbours it sits beside are asserted to still resolve unchanged. /cernia-ops/* is EXCLUDED, with the inversion documented in the test: there an unmapped path is the CORRECT deny for a non-operator, and mapping one would make the hook log an ALLOW and demote the real decision to the handler's requireSuperAdmin (the allow-then-deny bug this repo already shipped and fixed on isolation-posture-summary). A dedicated test locks that exclusion in both directions so it cannot be tidied away. FALSIFIED BEFORE SHIPPING, twice: deleting the /admin/setup-tasks mapping turns the gate red naming `GET /admin/setup-tasks`, and re-pointing that same mapping at a custom verb turns the unbound-verb check red naming the same route. (The first version of the scribe gate asserted deriveOperation(...) === undefined, which nothing ever returns, so it passed while reporting nothing -- not repeated.) WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED is in the two exactly-asserted lists and in `remaining`: 71 routes stay unmapped with a per-family reason, and 13 stay mapped-but-unbound because closing them means widening default-roles.ts, which was out of scope. VERIFICATION (same-tree baselines via git stash -u): @cernia/api typecheck CLEAN (baseline clean); lint 66 problems (baseline 66, none in the changed files); test 6417 passed / 28 failed / 6 skipped across 563 files (baseline 6401 / 36 / 6 across 562) -- fewer failures than baseline, the remainder being the pre-existing non-deterministic Postgres fixture timeouts and migration drift on the shared dev DB; the two coverage suites pass in isolation, 14/14.

Stage 4 — the resolution tier + the relevance filter. THE HEADLINE (PRD R10): a dental tenant with no clinician qualification and no defaults anywhere now resolves system-dentistry, not SOAP. That is the defect the whole programme exists for, and apps/api/src/scribe-specialty-relevance.integration.test.ts "R10 — THE HEADLINE" is the assertion that says so, against real Postgres. (1) apps/api/src/note-template-store.ts — resolveForClinician gains two rungs BELOW the clinician-specialty match and above SOAP: `tenant-specialty` (R10) and `care-setting` (R11). TemplateResolutionSource is widened with both; every pre-existing value is untouched. The profile store is an INJECTED, OPTIONAL dependency (NoteTemplateStoreOptions.specialtyProfiles) — a store constructed without it cannot execute either rung, so R15's regression guard holds by construction, and the test proves it by running the same inputs through a Stage-4 store and a pre-Stage-4 store and comparing tier for tier. The profile read happens at the BOTTOM of the chain, so the common paths (a saved default, a recognised credential) cost no extra query, and it is fail-soft: a missing table degrades to the old chain rather than aborting a capture. (2) apps/api/src/scribe-template-relevance.ts — ONE module owns "what does this tenant practice, and what follows from that", so the tier and the picker can never disagree about a tenant. THE MULTI-SPECIALTY DECISION lives here: the tenant rung fires only when the tenant declared EXACTLY ONE specialty. A tenant with two or more has told us its clinicians are not all one thing (R2 made that representable on purpose), and picking one for a clinician we cannot identify is a coin flip whose losing side is a cardiology note on a nephrology visit — strictly worse than SOAP, which is generic and reads as generic. Cardinality is measured on the DECLARED set, not on the subset that happens to carry a template, so [cardiology, nephrology] abstains too: ambiguity is a property of what the practice said, not of our library's coverage. Abstaining does not strand the tenant — the care-setting rung still runs. (3) packages/scribe/src/care-setting-templates.ts — the (*, care_setting) map, TOTAL over CareSettingSlug by `satisfies` so a care setting added upstream is a compile error until somebody decides what it drafts with. skilled-nursing -> system-geriatrics (the 4Ms note IS the SNF round document: functional status, cognition, mobility/falls, deprescribing, what-matters); hospice, ED, inpatient and urgent-care map to their obvious documents; office / telehealth / home are DELIBERATELY undefined — office shapes nothing, telehealth is a modality not a document shape, and home has no shipped template, so guessing would be the wrong-specialty defect the PRD forbids. ORDERING CALL, recorded as an assertion rather than left implicit: an INTERNIST in a SNF still gets the internal-medicine note, because (specialty, *) outranks (*, care_setting) in the PRD's own chain and Stage 4 places both new rungs below the clinician-specialty match. The PRD's prose ("an internist working in a SNF gets the SNF-shaped note") reads the other way and the two cannot both hold; flipping the order is a one-line change if the setting should dominate. (4) GET /scribe/templates (apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts) — relevance ordering with the reveal SHIPPING IN THE SAME RESPONSE: `items` leads with the tenant's specialties, then the care-setting template, then tenant-authored rows, then SOAP; `hidden` carries the rest of the system library so "Show all specialties" is a client-side concat, not a second query; `?all=true` returns the flat pre-Stage-4 list. Tenant-authored templates and SOAP are never hidden. A tenant with no profile, or with the gate off, gets the original list in the original order with NEITHER new field present — byte-identical over the wire, which is what makes R15 checkable by a client. (5) THE PER-TENANT GATE is derived, not a column: ON iff a profile row exists AND needs_confirm is FALSE. A migrated guess the tenant has not seen is not consent, and no row at all is off. This is PRD rollout step 4 ("enable for new tenants first, then existing ones once the prompt has run") expressed against data that already exists, because a flag column is a migration and Stage 4's scope excluded one — see `remaining` for the DDL still owed and why the persisted template_source is narrowed to `specialty` for now. The gate is injectable at both call sites so a column-backed reader drops in without touching the logic. (6) apps/admin/src/lib/clinician-specialty.ts — the picker gap Stage 5 opened is closed. Options derive from SPECIALTIES[].templateId, so all 24 template-bearing specialties are selectable (the fourteen Stage-5 templates were previously unreachable from the admin UI entirely), plus dental-restorative, which is derived from SCRIBE_TAG_MAP as the one legacy tag with a template and no canonical slug (R13). It PERSISTS THE CANONICAL SLUG; existing legacy values are NOT migrated and specialtySelectOptions(current) keeps a stored legacy tag selected so an edit form cannot blank it. (7) Carry-forward fixed in passing: apps/api typecheck was RED on baseline with 2 pre-existing errors in Stage 3's backfill (indexing ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP's nine literal keys with a runtime string). Fixed with a local widening that can MISS, typed to say so — the map's literal keys are load-bearing upstream and must not be widened there. R16 PLATFORM HALF — the operator-facing fleet view of the specialty-migration audit. Stage 3 shipped the tenant-facing half only; per CLAUDE.md a feature that surfaces in apps/admin but not apps/cernia-ops is half-shipped, and 'which tenants did we auto-map, from what, and how many are still unconfirmed' was unanswerable without SQL. (1) apps/api/src/specialty-migration-fleet-store.ts — a SEPARATE platform-scoped module, deliberately NOT a cross-tenant method on tenant-specialty-profile-store.ts: that store's tenant scoping is a safety property, and a getAllTenants() sitting beside get(tenantId) is how it gets lost. One FULL OUTER JOIN of tenant_specialty_profiles (328) to tenant_summary (062) — full outer because neither side is authoritative: a freshly provisioned tenant can have a profile before the nightly roster refresh, and an un-backfilled tenant has a roster row and no profile. Either LEFT JOIN silently drops exactly the population the view exists to surface. Totals, worklist and rollup are all derived from that one row set so they cannot disagree. (2) The from->to ROLLUP is the point, not the flat list: per legacy value it shows what ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP decided, how many tenants are still on that guess, and every target a human CORRECTED to with a count. mapLikelyWrong fires when >= CORRECTION_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD (2) tenants converge on the SAME target that DISAGREES with the map — agreement, not volume, because two tenants correcting one value to two different answers means the legacy value was ambiguous (which the map may already record via needsConfirm), not that the decision was wrong. A 'correction' that lands on the map's own answer is marked agreesWithMap and confirms the decision instead of counting against it. (3) THE WORKLIST INCLUDES TENANTS WITH NO PROFILE ROW, with reason 'no-profile'. Unmapped is not confirmed; dropping them would make the worklist look finished. totals.unresolved = needsConfirm + withoutProfile. (4) apps/api/src/specialty-migration-fleet-routes.ts — GET /cernia-ops/platform/specialty-migration, requireSuperAdmin + sendPhiSafe, READ-ONLY (an operator changes a tenant profile via the audited $impersonate flow, never a fleet view; CLAUDE.md invariant 6). (5) deriveOperation: the route is DELIBERATELY LEFT UNMAPPED and iam-route-guards.ts now documents why, because 'always register the route' is the correct reflex for a TENANT-scoped path and the wrong one here. /cernia-ops/* is authorised for its intended caller by the platform-operator pass, which runs BEFORE rbacEvaluate; mapping the path onto any synthetic type a tenant-admin's {'*','admin'} covers would make the hook log an allow and demote the real decision to a handler check — the audit-misleading allow-then-deny already found and fixed on /cernia-ops/isolation-posture-summary. specialty-migration-fleet-routes.deriveoperation.test.ts pins the catch-all, proves against real buildDefaultRoles output that no default tenant role covers it, carries /admin/practice-profile as the control that keeps the negative assertions honest, and then proves the thing that actually matters end to end through the REAL registerRbacHook: a tenant-admin with a real signed JWT and a real {'*','admin'} RoleBinding gets 403 AT THE HOOK ('RBAC denied' diagnostics, handler never runs), while a cernia-super-admin token with no RoleBinding at all passes and gets 200. (6) apps/cernia-ops/src/app/cernia-ops/platform/specialty-migration — @cernia/ui primitives, semantic tokens, lucide icons, cookie-session fetchOpsJson like every sibling fleet view; the map-likely-wrong signal is a banner naming the legacy value rather than a flag to spot in a table. Axes render as SLUGS, not prose labels: this is an audit of a mapping, so the stored value is the thing to show, and the map's own rationale arrives as mapNote. (7) PHI: the payload is tenant id + tenant display name + taxonomy slugs + counts + full ISO instants. Those slugs describe the PRACTICE, never a patient — which is why migration 328 records the table as carrying no PHI and Stage 3 classified it erase-on-tenant with no independent retention obligation. confirmed_by is NOT selected: a named individual inside the tenant that a mapping audit does not need. Timestamps are full ISO instants because assertNoPhi reads a bare YYYY-MM-DD as DOB-shaped and would 500 the route. PROOF: 9 route/store tests against real Postgres :5433 (from->to, correction rollup, the map-is-wrong signal AND its negative control, the no-profile worklist member, totals reconciliation, 401/403, zero-PHI payload), 7 deriveOperation/RBAC-gate tests, 9 cernia-ops page tests. FINDING: the dev database has no human-corrected tenant, so the mapLikelyWrong signal is proven by seeded fixtures only and says nothing yet about ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP's nine real decisions -- the backfill has still not been run against any live database (separate bullet above).

Stage 5 — 14 specialty note templates shipped in evidence-led tier order (packages/scribe/src/specialty-templates.ts, library 11 -> 25). Each carries the standard it is grounded in as a code comment directly above it, so R12 is checkable without guessing. TIER 1, the two gaps that close the Stage-2 narrowing: system-emergency-medicine (AMA CPT 2023 E/M revision + ACEP 2023 guidance — the ED visit level is MDM-only, so the MDM section is `required` and must carry differential, data reviewed and risk; deliberately NOT the urgent-care shape, it adds a chronological ED course, reassessment and a justified disposition, asserted by test) and system-psychotherapy (CPT 90832/90834/90837 + 45 CFR 164.501, which EXCLUDES modality, frequency, session times, diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan and progress from the privileged 'psychotherapy notes' definition — the template documents ONLY that excluded set, i.e. a progress note for the designated record set and never a privileged note; no access-control mechanism implied or implemented, out of scope). TIER 2: system-hospital-medicine (CPT 99231-99233 as revised 2023 + SHM Core Competencies; inpatient progress-note shape, interval events first, A/P by problem, running discharge planning), system-obstetrics-gynecology (ACOG well-woman visit + chaperone documentation + cervical screening intervals; the AMBULATORY GYNECOLOGIC shape chosen deliberately and documented in-file — the ACOG antepartum record is a serial flowsheet and is NOT merged in), system-physical-therapy (CPT 97161-97163, whose four graded evaluation elements are the section list, + CMS timed-code minutes), system-hospice-palliative-medicine (NCP Clinical Practice Guidelines for Quality Palliative Care 4th ed. domains + Medicare hospice CoP 42 CFR 418.54/418.56). TIER 3 ambulatory coverage: system-gastroenterology (ACG/AGA alarm features + ACG CRC surveillance interval), system-endocrinology (ADA Standards of Care incl. CGM time-in-range + the annual complication-screening set), system-neurology (AAN exam domains + localization-first reasoning), system-ophthalmology (AAO Preferred Practice Pattern element order), system-otolaryngology (AAO-HNS CPGs keyed to otoscopy/laryngoscopy/audiometry), system-oncology (AJCC stage + NCI CTCAE grading + ECOG performance status), system-podiatry (ADA comprehensive diabetic foot exam + Wagner/UT wound classification), system-geriatrics (IHI Age-Friendly 4Ms + AGS Beers + CMS Annual Wellness Visit elements). Radiology, pathology and anesthesiology deliberately skipped (the taxonomy records they have no ambient encounter) as are the three escape hatches — asserted by test so none can acquire a template by accident. R14: every new section sets omitIfEmpty explicitly, so no conditional section can render an empty header; R13: no procedure type entered the specialty enum. TAXONOMY: templateId set on those 14 slugs in packages/specialty-taxonomy/src/specialties.ts (24 pointers now) — the only field edited in the otherwise frozen package. REACHABILITY, the load-bearing part: the new templates are tagged with their CANONICAL slug (inventing a 12th legacy tag would re-create the package-local vocabulary Stage 2 deleted), and the legacy matchSpecialtyTag can never return a slug, so packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.ts gained matchTemplateSpecialty() = legacy tag if one exists, else the canonical slug when SPECIALTIES[].templateId is set (DERIVED from the taxonomy, never hand-listed, so a future template becomes reachable the moment the pointer lands). matchSpecialtyFromCandidates — the one function apps/api/src/scribe-clinician-specialty.ts calls, whose result is handed straight to resolveDefaultTemplate and never persisted — now resolves template keys, while matchSpecialtyTag keeps its 11-value persisted wire vocabulary byte-identical for the callers that WRITE it. Proven by packages/scribe/src/specialty-templates.test.ts 'Stage 5 — end-to-end reachability': 27 realistic clinician specialty strings ('Licensed Professional Counselor', 'Pediatric Emergency Medicine', 'OB/GYN', 'ENT', NUCC 207P00000X, …) run through the exact production chain to a template id, plus a coverage guard that fails if a future template ships with no reachability row, plus the negative case (nephrology/urology/rheumatology/radiology still fall through to SOAP — nothing is guessed). packages/scribe/src/specialty-match.test.ts passes UNCHANGED (81 tests). Verification: @cernia/specialty-taxonomy build + 78 tests green, @cernia/scribe typecheck/build clean and 302 tests green.

Stage 3 — tenant specialty projection + migration + confirm prompt. (1) packages/storage/src/migrations/328_tenant_specialty_profile.sql: one row per tenant, tenant_id PK (mirrors 055_tenant_customizations), org_type single / specialties TEXT[] SET-valued / care_setting single, needs_confirm + confirmed_at + confirmed_by, source ('migration'|'onboarding'|'admin') + legacy_value for R16, a GIN index on specialties, partial indexes for the R16 audit query and the confirm worklist, and a CHECK forbidding needs_confirm = TRUE alongside a non-null confirmed_at. Note what that CHECK deliberately does NOT require: needs_confirm = FALSE does not imply a stamp, because the three values the mapping was confident about (dental / physical-therapy / hospice) land settled WITHOUT anyone being asked. Requiring a timestamp there would have the database assert that a human confirmed something no human ever saw, and would leave R16 unable to separate "we were sure" from "they told us" — which is exactly what `source` exists to record. Slugs are validated in the APPLICATION layer, not by a CHECK, because the taxonomy tracks NUCC's twice-yearly releases and a CHECK would turn every vocabulary addition into a migration. (2) apps/api/src/tenant-specialty-profile-store.ts — InMemory + Postgres implementations. get() returns null for 'never derived', which is load-bearing: Stage 4 must be able to tell that from a real answer, so the store never fabricates a default. seed() is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, which buys idempotence and confirmation-preservation in one SQL clause instead of a read-then-write race. confirm() PRESERVES legacy_value so R16 survives a tenant correcting our guess. validateProfile() is the only slug gate (PRD R5) and collapses duplicates because the axis is a SET. (3) apps/api/src/tenant-specialty-profile-routes.ts — GET/PUT /admin/practice-profile. The tenant comes from rbacClaims only; the path carries no tenant id, so there is no cross-tenant addressing surface at all, and a smuggled body tenantId is ignored rather than validated (proven by test). confirmedBy is server-derived and cannot be forged. (4) apps/api/src/iam-route-guards.ts — BOTH verbs added to deriveOperation as read/write on the synthetic TenantSpecialtyProfile type. Without this the global hook falls through to the catch-all {verb:'*', resourceType:'*'}, which no binding covers, and 403s a legitimate tenant-admin BEFORE the handler runs — invisible to route tests that stub rbacClaims. tenant-specialty-profile-routes.integration.test.ts therefore asserts deriveOperation directly AND that a real buildDefaultRoles('tenant-admin') covers the result, with an unmapped-sibling control proving the assertion has teeth. FINDING: office-admin is NOT covered — {'*','admin'} belongs to tenant-admin alone, while office-admin is a scoped front-desk allow-list (Appointment/Patient/Task/Invoice/Communication) — so this route's isAdmin deliberately OMITS office-admin instead of copying the scribe predicate, which advertises an access path the hook denies. tenant-member CAN read (so a clinician sees the banner) but cannot write. (5) apps/api/src/backfill-tenant-specialty-profiles.ts — a SCRIPT, not a migration, for two reasons: the decision table is TypeScript (ONBOARDING_LEGACY_MAP; re-expressing those nine decisions as a SQL CASE would create exactly the second source of truth this PRD exists to kill), and it must stay re-runnable after the migration ledger has moved on, since tenants keep arriving. LEFT JOIN from tenants so a tenant with no persisted session (provisioned before migration 281 made the wizard durable) is still backfilled rather than dropped; DISTINCT ON takes the newest session per tenant for retried provisions; needsConfirm comes from the MAP and is never re-decided; care_setting is seeded from the org type's defaultCareSetting so R11's (*, care_setting) rung has something to match for a migrated tenant. (6) apps/api/src/onboarding-full-provisioner.ts — an optional specialtyProfileStore seam writes the SAME derivation at wizard completion with source 'onboarding', so a new tenant does not wait for a backfill run. Best-effort: it never blocks a tenant going live. The wizard UI, its step schemas and UseCaseStepData are UNCHANGED. (7) apps/admin/src/app/admin/settings/practice-profile/{page.tsx,practice-profile-api.ts} — single-select org type, MULTI-select specialties (R2 in the UI: 'multi-specialty' appears nowhere as an option; ticking two boxes IS a multi-specialty group), optional care setting, escape hatches included under 'Other' so the picker cannot dead-end, and a DISMISSIBLE confirm banner that explains what was guessed and from what using the map's own note. Grouping labels come from SPECIALTY_GROUPINGS rather than a local table, so no vocabulary is re-declared. Visible success AND visible error on save; a save attempted with no org type says why rather than silently doing nothing. (8) apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts — tenant_specialty_profiles classified into ADR_0140_CASCADE as delete-all on tenant_id. The ADR-0140 completeness test is a forcing function that goes red on any unclassified tenant-scoped table, and it caught this one. Classified as ERASE rather than retained: the row describes what a PRACTICE does and where, never who it treats, so it carries no independent retention obligation — the same class as tenant_customizations and tenant_facility_profile. RETRACTION + controlled model A/B. The 2026-07-29 'F4 follow-up extraction accuracy' finding reported earlier today (invented '3 months' interval, 'two weeks' migrating from the rinse duration into an appointment) was an ARTEFACT OF THE HARNESS, not a product defect, and is withdrawn. The harness recorded 75s of a 162s consultation, so the entire back half of the visit — the periodontics referral, the six-week follow-up, the chlorhexidine instruction — was never captured. Both models were being graded on content they had never been given; the 'invented' intervals were invented from an empty prompt, which is a different and much less alarming thing than misreading a stated one. Root cause: a hardcoded 75_000ms record window. Fixed by deriving the duration from the WAV header (WAV_SECONDS + 12s tail), because a fixed number cannot know how long a fixture is, and the parts of a consultation clinicians care about — what happens next — live at the END, exactly where a truncation lands. WITH THE FULL 2272-char transcript, on identical input: ollama/qwen and anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 BOTH extract the six-week follow-up, the periodontics referral and the two-week chlorhexidine course correctly. Sonnet is marginally richer clinically (specifies 0.12% concentration); qwen is fully adequate for this task, which matters for the self-hosted no-BAA posture — there is no accuracy argument here for sending PHI to a third party. Both duplicate every action identically, which is what identified the duplication as OURS. METHOD NOTE: two earlier attempts at this A/B were invalid and were caught before being reported — a re-draft returned the stale rows from the previous model unchanged, and clearing the rows first produced zero. Byte-identical output from two different models was the tell.

$DRAFT IN-FLIGHT CLAIM (migration 330) + orphan cleanup. The F4 residual is closed. `$draft` had no concurrency claim, so two overlapping calls both ran transcript -> per-section LLM drafting -> coding -> follow-up -> order -> write a Composition -> set composition_ref; last writer won on the ref and the loser’s note survived in `resources` at status `preliminary`, referenced by nothing. Measured in scribe_harness: 10 Compositions, 7 sessions, 4 with a composition_ref, 6 orphans. The partial guard that existed was shaped right and scoped wrong — migration 291’s route set status `transcribing` before STT so a concurrent GET saw the in-flight state, but ONLY when no transcript existed yet; once one was persisted the second call skipped that branch and raced into the expensive phase. Migration 330 extends the same idea over the whole operation: packages/storage/src/migrations/330_scribe_draft_claim.sql adds scribe_sessions.drafting_claimed_at (the claim AND its fencing token) + drafting_prior_status, and widens the status CHECK with `drafting`. apps/api/src/scribe-session-store.ts claimDraft() is a single conditional UPDATE (WHERE drafting_claimed_at IS NULL OR < staleBefore ... RETURNING *) — a read-then-write would be the same race one level up. The claim rides the TIMESTAMP, not `status`, because the draft path legitimately moves `status` to `transcribing` while holding it. apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts takes the claim before template resolution, answers 409 `draft-in-progress` (retryable, nothing written) to the loser, releases explicitly before EVERY reply so an immediate retry is not 409’d, and releases again in a `finally` so a THROWN draft frees it rather than waiting out the timeout. Release RESTORES the status captured at claim time (an `uploaded` session that fails to draft lands back on `uploaded`), mirroring the contract the `transcribing` branch already had. Stale window: 10 minutes (DEFAULT_DRAFT_CLAIM_TTL_MS, overridable via deps.draftClaimTtlMs) — crash recovery only, sized an order of magnitude above the ~15-30s harness pipeline and several times the worst realistic draft (one LLM call per template section plus the coding/ follow-up/order passes), so it never fires on a draft that is merely slow. apps/api/src/scribe-draft-inflight-claim.integration.test.ts proves it against real Postgres: two concurrent $draft calls give one 201 + one 409 and EXACTLY ONE Composition (red before the fix at 201/201), a sequential redraft still succeeds, a thrown draft restores `uploaded` and is immediately re-draftable, a stale claim is reclaimable while a live one blocks, release is fenced on the claim token, and the claim is tenant-scoped. Cleanup for the orphans already written: apps/api/src/purge-orphan-scribe-compositions.ts (runnable script, not a migration — the decision logic is TypeScript). It matches only SCRIBE-TAGGED, `preliminary`, unreferenced Compositions, is tenant-scoped, idempotent, DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT and REFUSES to execute without an explicit single --tenant (there is no cross-tenant delete). It removes the resources row + its resource_versions history and KEEPS the audit Provenance — the PHI goes, the record of the write stays. A "has no Provenance" safety predicate was written and then removed: the storage adapter mints a CREATE Provenance for every write, so it matched all 10 harness Compositions and would have made the purge a permanent no-op. TENANT ERASURE ALREADY REACHES ORPHANS — apps/api/src/erasure-cascade.ts entries 0/1 delete `resources` + `resource_versions` delete-all BY tenant_id, not by walking from the session, so an unreferenced Composition is erased with the tenant; locked in by a new assertion in erasure-cascade.test.ts. Migration 330 was added to the BOOTSTRAP_SQL of all 26 integration fixtures that touch scribe_sessions, and `drafting` was threaded into the analytics in-progress set (apps/api/src/scribe-analytics-store.ts) and the admin status union + actionsFor (apps/admin/src/lib/scribe-api.ts) so a mid-draft session is not counted nowhere and not offered a Draft button that would only earn a 409.

SCRIBE P1 TRIO CLOSED (D2 + D3 + D9 of docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md §0.1), one red-then-green each. (1) D2 — POST /scribe/sessions/:id/$cancel had NO ownership check at all while iam-route-guards.ts maps it to a bare write:ScribeSession that any *:admin satisfies, so any tenant-admin or second clinician could end a colleague's in-flight recording mid-consultation. apps/api/src/scribe-session-routes.ts now gates on the session owner and answers 403 {error:'forbidden',code:'not-session-owner'}, the same signature its PATCH sibling already used. DELIBERATELY NO ADMIN CARVE-OUT: the plausible 'admin tidies a stuck recording row' need loses to the asymmetry — a wrong cancel is unrecoverable through the API (no route writes status back off 'cancelled'; PATCH only moves template_id) and $coverage evicts its cache on a terminal status, while a stuck row blocks nothing (start() is a plain INSERT with no open-session predicate, the $draft claim self-heals on draftClaimTtlMs, usageByTemplate already excludes a null composition_ref). A real ops need must arrive as its own audited $force-cancel. Chunks + assembled audio survive a cancel untouched (scribe-chunk-routes.ts gates on neither status nor owner) — the capture is interrupted, not erased. (2) D3 — CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT=deepgram (a VALID id in the streaming SttBackendId union, and the obvious thing a human types) crashed the whole API at boot with 'unknown batch backend "deepgram"'; resolveScribeProviders validates that var for emptiness only. Rejecting the value is right and failing FAST is right (a lazy throw would fail after a clinician had already recorded a visit), so the fix is the message: packages/speech/src/batch-transcriber.ts now names the variable, the rejected value, the full valid batch set, and the streaming/batch mix-up itself via STREAMING_ONLY_BACKEND_HINTS (deepgram -> deepgram-prerecorded; whisper -> no batch equivalent, the scribe's option is the self-hosted whisper-selfhost) plus the reminder that CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT and CERNIA_SPEECH_STT are separate variables. (3) D9 — $coverage re-resolved the template with `undefined` for the facility (apps/api/src/scribe-draft-routes.ts) while $draft threads activeOrgOf(req) on BOTH of its re-resolution paths, so a tenant with a facility default coached the clinician against the PRACTICE template while the note drafted from the FACILITY one — prompted for sections the note would not contain, silent about sections it would. One-argument fix. Tests: apps/api/src/scribe-session-routes.integration.test.ts (D2, red 'expected 200 to be 403'; green also asserts a tenant-admin is refused, cross-tenant is 404, owner still cancels), packages/speech/src/batch-transcriber.test.ts (D3, 4 message-content cases, red on the old bare message), apps/api/src/scribe-coverage-routes.integration.test.ts (D9, red "expected [ 'practice-only' ] to deeply equal [ 'facility-only' ]"; green compares $coverage's returned section keys against the templateId $draft stamps, runs with CERNIA_ENFORCE_ORG_SCOPE=1 and gates its activeOrgId stamp on isOrgScopeEnforced() exactly as iam-route-guards.ts does — the facility tier is dead without the flag and the test would otherwise pass vacuously, so it asserts the flag is armed). GET /scribe/analytics had no requireEntitlement at all, so a tenant holding no scribe product was answered 200 WITH THE FULL PAID AGGREGATE while its sibling GET /scribe/sessions 402d in the same breath; its only gate was an in-route tenant-admin check, and role is not payment — every tenant has an admin. GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief was gated on ambient-scribe-pro ONLY, so a tenant that had bought nothing got 403 tier-denied: told its TIER was too low for a product it did not own. FIX: an optional requireEntitlement dep plus a plugin-scoped preHandler hook in apps/api/src/scribe-analytics-routes.ts and apps/api/src/scribe-pre-visit-brief-routes.ts (the scribeVocabularyRoutes pattern — the hook is scoped to each plugin encapsulation context so it gates only its own family), with requireAmbientScribe passed at both registrations in apps/api/src/index.ts. ORDERING WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: createRequireProduct orders itself 401 then 404 unknown-product then 402, and the brief pro check is IN-ROUTE, so a preHandler necessarily lands first — which is what lets the two signatures coexist (402 product-not-entitled for owns-nothing, 403 tier-denied for base-but-not-pro). They are deliberately NOT collapsed: F1-02 asserts the first and F1-05 the second, and they are different facts about the customer. Consequence worth knowing: on analytics, payment now precedes the in-route admin check, so an un-entitled non-admin gets 402 rather than 403 — the actionable answer. (2) D13 — OBSERVABILITY, NOT BEHAVIOUR. A pro tenant whose coding pass failed 100% of the time was byte-identical over HTTP to a base tenant that never bought coding ($draft 201 with no coding key, then GET /coding 404 coding-not-found), so a paying practice could get no diagnostic coding for months with nothing to look at, and F1-06 could not tell a correct tier skip from a silent failure. The fail-soft swallow is CORRECT and is unchanged — a note must still arrive — and the status codes are unchanged, so no client breaks and the review UI still hides the card. FIX: a ScribeCodingPassStatus discriminator (ready, failed, skipped-not-entitled, not-drafted, unavailable) on the $draft 201 and on GET /coding (the 404, plus the 200 for symmetry). DESIGN CHOICE — DERIVED FROM ALREADY-PERSISTED STATE, NO MIGRATION: 'attempted' is exactly 'pro-entitled AND a draft exists', because the coding pass runs unconditionally when entitled and always persists a row on completion (even when the model legitimately returns zero diagnoses) — so entitled + a Composition + no row can only mean the pass failed. That needs no column and no backfill AND it retro-classifies the sessions that had ALREADY failed, which a new column could not. 'unavailable' is kept distinct from 'skipped-not-entitled' on purpose: labelling an unwired deployment 'not entitled' would be a lie about what the customer bought — the same conflation D13 is about. Visible to BOTH parties: the practice on its own API responses (it is their paid feature failing), the operator via the pre-existing non-PHI scribeCoding log marker. No PHI either way — product/config facts only. (3) WHY THE OLD TESTS COULD NOT CATCH D13: apps/api/src/scribe-coding-routes.integration.test.ts already had a base-tier case AND a fail-soft case — in two separate describe blocks with two separate Fastify apps, so nothing ever compared them. The new suite puts a failing-pro, a working-pro and a base tenant in ONE app via a per-tenant codingClientFor and asserts the discrimination directly: first that the status codes, the error body and the absent coding key are all IDENTICAL, then that codingStatus differs. On main that test cannot be written to pass — both sides read undefined, so even the not.toBe comparison fails. (4) RED WAS OBSERVED, not inferred: the source files were stashed and the new suites re-run against main's handlers. D12 red = expected 200 to be 402 (analytics), expected 403 to be 402 (brief), expected 403 not to be 403 (the two-denials case). D13 red = expected undefined to be failed, four times. Green: scribe-entitlement-gates.integration.test.ts 8/8, scribe-coding-pass-status.integration.test.ts 5/5, full scribe surface 533/533 across 47 files, tsc --noEmit clean, lint unchanged against a git stash -u baseline (13 pre-existing errors in the touched files, same rules, only line numbers shifted). Both suites carry falsifying controls — an ENTITLED admin must still get 200 from analytics, and a WORKING pro pass must report ready — without which a gate that denied everybody, or a status that said failed to everybody, would also look green. (5) TWO PROCESS CORRECTIONS FOUND WHILE DOING THIS. The obvious re-run command (--out f1-results.json) would have OVERWRITTEN the only record of D12 red, i.e. the 200-with-paid-aggregate; the green run is written to f1-results-2026-07-30-post-d12-d13.json and the 2026-07-29 artifact is preserved. And the runner discriminate() reduces every response to a whitelist of keys, so codingStatus was absent from the evidence artifact even though the API was returning it — the ⚙️ evidence would have understated the fix as unchanged. codingStatus is now in that list; any future discriminator must be added there too. (6) A LIMIT OF THE ⚙️ CHANNEL, recorded: on 2026-07-29 Tenant B pro coding pass failed twice on the local 8B model (which is how D13 was found); on this re-run it succeeded first try. The live channel CANNOT summon the failed state on demand, so D13 proof is necessarily a forced-throw in-process case and F1-06 live assertion covers only the skipped-not-entitled side. Separately, Tenant B $draft intermittently exceeds the undici 300s header timeout (TypeError: fetch failed at the F1-08 $draft call) — a pre-existing local-model latency characteristic unrelated to these fixes, but it makes the runner flaky at F1-08 and cost multiple full runs; a per-request timeout/retry on the runner api() helper is owed.

SCRIBE TEST FAMILY F4 (CAPTURE) EXECUTED ON THE REAL CAPTURE CHANNEL — 5/6, and the biggest hole in the scribe's coverage is closed. F4-06 is the case that did not exist in any form CI could run: a real Chromium fed a 162 s synthetic dental consultation into getUserMedia, MediaRecorder chunked it at 30 s, SIX chunks uploaded (measured median inter-chunk gap 30,036 ms — cadence, not just count, so a single end-of-visit burst cannot pass), $finalize-upload assembled the audio, REAL batch STT (deepgram-prerecorded) transcribed it, $draft wrote the note on the DENTISTRY template and the review screen signed it. Verified in POSTGRES, not from the API echo: Composition status='final', 1 DocumentReference, 1 scribe-sign Provenance (3 total = draft + edit + sign), session 'signed', template_id='system-dentistry' via template_source='specialty', 8/8 dentistry headings and ZERO SOAP headings, all 8 sections non-empty. STT was proven to have RUN rather than merely been configured: the persisted transcript is not the stub string, is 2272 chars, is speaker-diarized, and contains 8/8 clinical terms from the fixture's verbatim script. This matters because with CERNIA_SCRIBE_STT=stub a canned string is returned for ANY audio, so a completely broken capture path would still yield a signed dentistry note and a green test — the runner therefore reports F4-06 BLOCKED, never passed, if run behind the stub. The audio fixture did not exist and was generated from tests/e2e/fixtures/make-consult-audio.ps1 (5,185,646 bytes ~ 162.1 s, 24 turns, two SAPI voices); because the script is embedded in the generator it doubles as exact ground truth. TWO OF THE SIX PLANNED EXPECTATIONS WERE WRONG, in opposite directions, and both are corrected in the plan with the originals quoted. (a) F4-01's 'every scribe call under 400' is UNACHIEVABLE on correct code for the base-tier capture tenant: the recorder and review screens poll $coverage (pro-gated, 403), transcript (404 until the first chunk is transcribed), coding (404, pro-only) and after-visit-summary (404, empty state), all fail-soft by design (R16). 14 of 73 calls were >=400 and every one was correct. The PRE-EXISTING harness asserted this literal condition, so it would exit 1 on a perfectly healthy run. Replaced with: zero >=400 on the capture WRITE path (consent/chunks/$finalize-upload/$draft/$sign) plus a justified allowlist, so a genuinely new 403 still fails — deleting the assertion was the tempting wrong answer, since 403s on real routes are the class of defect the capture channel exists to catch. (b) F4-04's 'duplicate chunk index -> 400' DEMANDED A REGRESSION: re-POSTing the same index at the same size is a documented idempotent no-op (202) because a lost ack means the client re-sends (packages/scribe/src/chunk-session.ts:47); only a duplicate index at a DIFFERENT size is chunk-conflict. Corrected to assert both, with the idempotent replay as the control. NEW DEFECT D17 (P2) from F4-03 — the 10 MiB per-chunk cap cannot fire through its own route (413 + FHIR OperationOutcome, not 400 chunk-rejected); see its own remaining bullet. NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING: the first capture attempt rendered 'SOAP / Practice default' on the recorder for the dentist — indistinguishable from the flagship defect this family exists to detect — while the resolver was behaving correctly. The cause was a stale t-cedar/__tenant__ -> system-soap row that a REUSED scribe_f1 still carried (test-plan §6). Preflight now deletes it and the runner ASSERTS the capture session is stamped system-dentistry before recording, aborting rather than reporting a product defect. The template verdict was then FALSIFIED deliberately (--falsify reinstates that row): same dentist, same predicate, note returns [Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan], predicate false — so F4-06 discriminates rather than describing whatever the stack happens to do. STACK (recorded into the artifact from the runner's own process.env, via the same apps/api/scripts/f4-env.sh the API booted with): API c4219ac3 on :8163, admin :3210, Postgres :5433/scribe_f1 with the port-to-DB pairing asserted inside the runner before any case (18 rows for a throwaway tenant, 0 elsewhere; a zero count aborts). Note the LLM substitution: 192.168.1.164:11434 was DOWN and BOTH qwen3-vl blobs in the local Ollama cache are CORRUPT ('unable to load model'), and OPENAI_API_KEY is live but billing_not_active, so the draft ran on local qwen2.5:7b-instruct — F4's note quality is therefore NOT comparable with F1/F2's.

SCRIBE TEST FAMILIES F13 (CROSS-TENANT ISOLATION) + F16 (RBAC PER ROUTE) EXECUTED ON THE REAL-HTTP CHANNEL — F16 43/43, F13 42/43, two new defects. These are the two WHOLE-SURFACE sweeps, and F16 is the family that would have caught the incident that motivated the whole plan: ten /scribe/* routes once shipped 403ing every real caller while all their unit tests were green, because a route test stubs rbacClaims and never traverses the hook that denies them. New runner apps/api/scripts/run-scribe-f13-f16.mts; stack apps/api/scripts/f13-f16-env.sh (sourced by boot-f13-f16.sh AND by the runner, so the artifact records the environment the API actually booted with); evidence docs/status/evidence/scribe-e2e/f13-f16-results.json + f13-f16-summary.md (generated from the JSON by apps/api/scripts/scribe-f13-f16-summary.mts, not transcribed — 172 request/response rows is exactly where a hand transcription quietly writes 404 next to a route that answered 201). THE ROUTE LIST STOPPED BEING A HAND-WRITTEN CLAIM. New apps/api/scripts/derive-scribe-routes.mts derives the inventory from the scribe-*-routes.ts files; the runner cross-checks it against SCRIBE_ROUTES in run-scribe-f1.mts with a route-SHAPED comparison (a :param matches any one segment, because the hand list carries concrete values like Ozempic and pa-1 where the source carries params, and a naive string compare reports four false disagreements). Both say 43 and they agree pair-for-pair, so F1s correction of the plans 41 is now independently confirmed rather than re-asserted. Building the deriver REPRODUCED the original miscount: with a six-line lookahead it found 40, dropping PUT .../coding, PUT .../after-visit-summary and PUT /scribe/templates/:id — each behind a fastify.put<{...}>( generic spanning ten-plus lines. The fix is to bound the lookahead by the NEXT registration, not by a line count. F16 — 43/43 REACHABLE, and the falsifying control is what makes that mean anything: a classifier that could never return denied would report every route reachable, which is the exact shape of the original incident. admin.reachable comes from the SAME isRbacForbidden call that denies tenant-member on 26 of 26 mutating pairs and office-admin on 40 of 43, so it demonstrably fires. TWO REFINEMENTS THE RUN FORCED. (1) The prediction is now a CHECK, not a restatement: iam-route-guards.scribe-coverage.test.ts proves MAPPING (no declared /scribe/* path left unmapped) but its STANDARD_VERBS set is a hand-written CLAIM about default-roles.ts and would stay green if the tenant-admin wildcard grant vanished tomorrow. The runner computes the expected outcome from the real deriveOperation + buildDefaultRoles + permissionCoversOperation (the same matcher the hook uses) and compares it to the live result: 0 mismatches / 43. (2) deriveOperation returns NO null — an unmatched url falls through to {verb:'*',resourceType:'*'}, the catch-all no binding covers, which IS the fail-closed deny that made those ten routes 403 everybody. Unmapped therefore has to be detected as the catch-all; a null check would report zero unmapped routes no matter what. Measured: none of the 43 sits on it. A BRIEF EXPECTATION THAT WAS WRONG, checked rather than assumed: office-admin is NOT denied on all 43. OFFICE_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS holds (Appointment, read) and (Patient, read), and GET /scribe/schedule / GET /scribe/patient-search map to exactly those, so both answer a front-desk token 200 — correct by design and not an escalation, since the same reads are already theirs on the generic FHIR surface. The third, GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief, also passes the HOOK on (Patient, read) and is refused IN-ROUTE with 403 clinician-role-required. Worth recording as its own fact: the RBAC mapping alone does not defend the paid clinical brief; a route-level gate does. F13 — 42/43, and the one failure is a WRITE. Tenant B (t-lakeshore, its OWN token and its OWN base+pro entitlement, so nothing it gets back can be an entitlement refusal masquerading as isolation) was refused on 25 session-scoped pairs, 4 template-by-id pairs and the patient-scoped brief using tenant A's ids; the sharpest probe — GET /scribe/patient-search?q=Avery, the shared-by-NAME patient section 2 deliberately plants in both tenants — returned only Bs own; and a direct Postgres read shows tenant As row state BYTE-IDENTICAL after the whole sweep (session status, template version + archived, vocabulary row, consent row, E/M config, total session count), so no 404 was hiding a mutation. D19 (P2, NEW): POST /scribe/sessions never resolves patientId. apps/api/src/scribe-session-routes.ts:157 checks typeof patientId === 'string' and nothing else, so tenant B opens a scribe session on tenant A's patient id (201, row persisted in t-lakeshore, verified against the resources row still owned by t-northside), on an id that exists in no tenant (201), and on "not-a-reference-at-all" (201). session.patientId then becomes Composition.subject AND DocumentReference.subject at $sign (scribe-sign-routes.ts:307 + :411), so a tenant can mint a signed legal record subjected to another tenant's patient identifier, and $push-to-ehr would transmit it. BLAST RADIUS STATED HONESTLY: REFERENTIAL, not a PHI read — the Patient resource is never fetched on any scribe path and GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief for the same id correctly 404s — with the escalation condition written down (the moment any consumer resolves session.patientId without the tenant filter, this is a disclosure). The sharpest framing is internal: the SAME handler validates visitType against a closed set specifically so a typo cannot mint a phantom key, and says so in a comment. The PHI subject of the note gets none of that. THE ATTRIBUTION D19 FORCED, which matters more than the defect: GET /scribe/sessions in tenant B does return pt-t-northside-local — but as the patientId of a row BELONGING TO B, planted by D19s own earlier POST. Flagging that as a second isolation breach would have double-counted one defect and misdescribed it as a tenant-filter failure. The runner instead looks up every returned session ids tenant_id in Postgres (all t-lakeshore, so the filter held) and records the finding against D19, while still stating the real consequence: another tenant's patient identifier is persistently displayed in B's session list. The artifact separates tenantFilterFailures (none) from aIdentifiersVisibleToB (one, attributed). D18 (P2, NEW), found by F16 rather than F13: POST /scribe/templates validates only that name is a string and sections is a non-empty array (scribe-draft-routes.ts:1192) and never checks a sections SHAPE, so a section without promptFragment reaches sanitizeFragment(undefined) (packages/scribe/src/note-template.ts:122 via note-template-store.ts:417) and throws, surfacing as an unhandled Fastify 500 where 400 invalid-input field=sections belongs. PUT /scribe/templates/:id shares the miss. Reproduced WITH a falsifying control (a well-formed section still 201s) because without it this reads as "template creation is broken", which it is not. Found because F16 sent the body SCRIBE_ROUTES declares ({heading:S}); F1 never noticed, since F1-02 only asserts the 402 that fires first. Same CLASS as D4 (an unmapped exception surfacing as 5xx), different cause — D4 is a deliberate guard with no status mapping, this is absent input validation — so they should not be folded into one fix. D7'S EVIDENCE DEBT IS PAID, and the plan undercounted it. Section 4 says two bodies; the sweep measures FOUR, one of which is a different SHAPE: {error:'not-found'} (4 routes, all scribe-session-routes.ts), {error:'session-not-found'} (21 routes), {error:'template-not-found'} (4 NoteTemplate routes), and a FHIR OperationOutcome issue[0].code=not-found from GET /scribe/pre-visit-brief (1). A normalisation written against the two NAMED STRINGS would leave the other two untouched — precisely the vacuity D7 is about. The full per-route map is f13.d7BodyMap and the proposed normalisation is in the plans section 7 (collapse the two session-family strings onto session-not-found, the 21-route majority, changing 4 callers all in one file; KEEP template-not-found, which names a different resource; leave the pre-visit-brief OperationOutcome alone unless the generic-FHIR-shape decision is revisited). NOT DONE HERE — changing a response body is a separate reviewable change. TWO HARNESS DEFECTS FIXED IN PASSING. (1) run-scribe-f1.mts EXPORTED SCRIBE_ROUTES while also calling main() at module scope, so importing the inventory re-ran the entire F1 suite against the booted API AND OVERWROTE the importer's own --out evidence file with F1's artifact — the first F13/F16 run produced F1's artifact under the F13/F16 filename. Fixed with an entrypoint guard. (2) TWO >>>>>>> github/main conflict markers were committed into docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md (section 0 and section 0.3); removed. AND THIS FILE WAS BROKEN A THIRD TIME: docs/status/production-readiness.json carried SIX conflict markers on github/main and did not JSON.parse. Repaired SEMANTICALLY, not line-wise: the first region had THREE successive restatements of the SCRIBE DEFECT REGISTER bullet (after F2, after D12/D13, after F3/F8) plus three byte-identical SCRIBE SIGN SURFACE copies — keeping them all would leave two stale open-counts in the punch list, which is the exact lie the status rule exists to prevent — so they are collapsed to one bullet restated after F13/F16, and the KTD5-does-not-cover-amended bullet is REMOVED because that is D14, fixed on main by c4219ac3. VERIFICATION: @cernia/api typecheck clean; eslint src byte-identical to baseline (this change touches no src/ file — only apps/api/scripts/* and docs/*, and the lint script's scope is src only). STACK: commit c4219ac3 matching the API's own boot stamp (gitSha), API :8167 (8080 and 8090 were AGAIN held by other sessions, third run in a row), DB :5433/scribe_f1 reused (290 migrations; a fresh migrate is ~90 min here), STT stub, LLM ollama logical qwen to qwen3-vl:8b-instruct, CERNIA_LLM_ROUTING=primary-fallback, CERNIA_ENFORCE_ORG_SCOPE=1. Port-to-DB pairing is asserted INSIDE the runner before any case, in BOTH directions: a /dev/login for a brand-new throwaway tenant must land Role/RoleBinding rows in the database the runner queries (9 rows) AND must land ZERO of them in scribe_e2e, which is the DB_NAME apps/api/.env actually names — either half aborts the run. All HTTP goes through node:http with no timeout rather than global fetch, whose 300 s undici cap surfaces as a bare TypeError: fetch failed that is indistinguishable from a dead API. Only the LABELS moved; every status, body and count in the artifact is the value the live run recorded, and the summary markdown was REGENERATED from the relabelled JSON rather than hand-edited. CTRL-0 SETTLED by RUN 3 of J06 — the /dev/checkout-grant provisioning fan-out is EXONERATED. J06 is tested on TWO corpora that disagree by construction: four timelines drafted by genuinely pre-335 code AFTER migration 340 stamped its epoch (the log watched them — answered exactly on all four, findings 46 and 47 included) and run 2’s own four notes carried in by a CREATE DATABASE … TEMPLATE clone and drafted hours BEFORE it (the log never watched them — answered `indeterminate`, never `failed` and never quiet). J05 gained a sixth step for PR #744’s 84-parameter reference-search change, driven from both practices against ground truth read out of Postgres, with the INCLUSION arm asserted first because an empty compendium excludes the other tenant trivially and that was the defect. NOT MEASURED: the 🖥️ channel. apps/admin is unrunnable in the cernia-w2 worktree (half-materialized pnpm store — the next package directory is empty), so #741’s review-screen reason and #747’s indeterminate banner are proved on the wire and in the client source only. Recorded as J04-F1 in docs/testing/scribe-live-journeys.md §6 rather than left implicit. Evidence: docs/status/evidence/scribe-journeys/run3-j04-j06-report.md.

CLOSURE PASS — 20 remaining bullets to 12. Six were closed by work that had already landed and two were closed by this change; nothing was deleted without checking the code. ALREADY DONE, verified on main: (1) "one migration is owed" — migration 329 shipped BOTH halves (packages/storage/src/migrations/329_scribe_specialty_relevance.sql widens the scribe_sessions.template_source CHECK to admit tenant-specialty and care-setting, and adds the tri-state scribe_tenant_config.specialty_relevance_enabled). Proof the narrowing is really gone: toPersistedTemplateSource now has ZERO production call sites — grep finds it only in its own definition and in two test files — so the two Stage-4 tiers persist verbatim and the recorder chip can tell a clinician credential from a practice declaration from a care setting. (2) The admin picker-gap bullet contained no open work at all: it recorded that specialtySelectOptions() derives from SPECIALTIES[].templateId and that legacy tag values are deliberately NOT migrated. A record, not a gap. (3) D17 (the 10 MiB chunk cap unreachable through its own route) is FIXED — apps/api/src/scribe-chunk-routes.ts now DERIVES the route bodyLimit from maxChunkBytes (scribeChunkBodyLimitFor), and a plugin-scoped error handler re-answers the transport backstop in the route's own 400 chunk-rejected/chunk-too-large shape, so the admin client's existing 400 mapping is correct and the "add a 413 branch" half is moot. PR #711. (4) The "9 of 17 open" defect-register bullet: EVERY defect it named as open is now fixed — D18 (template-section 400) and D19 (patientId resolution) and D7 (404-body normalisation) by PR #703, D4 and D6 by PR #708, D15/D8 by PR #705, D16 by PR #709, D17 by PR #711. Confirmed against the live register at docs/testing/scribe-e2e-test-plan.md section 0.1, where all nine now read fixed. The register remains the tracker for the defects filed AFTER that bullet was written (D20-D49), which is where D43 and the rest live. (5) The scribe P1 trio bullet: (a) D2/D9 live debts recorded as paid, (b) D7 is fixed by PR #703 — the four measured 404 bodies are normalised from the frozen constants in apps/api/src/scribe-error-bodies.ts — and (c) "no $force-cancel exists" was explicitly an intended trade recorded so it would not be re-filed as a bug. Nothing left. CLOSED BY THIS CHANGE: (6) Stage 4's two follow-ups. (a) An explicit OFF now leaves a trace on the confirm prompt: the practice-profile confirm banner promises "so we pick the right note templates", which is FALSE for a tenant that turned specialty-aware templates off — the Stage-4 rungs do not run and the picker is not reordered — so the banner now says so (apps/admin/.../practice-profile/page.tsx, testid practice-profile-confirm-relevance-off, keyed off the STORED value not the draft, with tests in both directions). (b) The flag now surfaces CROSS-TENANT as an aggregate: SpecialtyFleetTotals.relevanceOptOut counts tenants with an explicit FALSE (apps/api/src/specialty-migration-fleet-store.ts) and apps/cernia-ops/.../specialty-migration renders it as a "Turned it off" tile. A COUNT and never a list, per CLAUDE.md invariants 2 and 5 — the integration test asserts no row in the payload carries the flag. NULL is not counted as off (migration 329's tri-state exists to keep unset and off distinct); the seed carries FALSE, TRUE and NULL so a fold would fail. An absent field renders as an em dash, never as 0 — "nobody opted out" and "this server cannot tell you" must not look the same on a fleet dashboard. While there, the suite stopped hand-listing migration 328 and now bootstraps from the derived SCRIBE_BOOTSTRAP_SQL (D8's rule). (7) The AE1 consent gate is no longer opt-in at the composition root. Every scribe consent gate reads `if (deps.consent && ...)`, so an unwired dep means NO ENFORCEMENT — which is exactly how D5 shipped. apps/api/src/scribe-consent-composition-root.test.ts now DERIVES the population (every apps/api/src/scribe-*.ts module declaring a consent dependency on its options — five today: session, chunk, draft, sign, audio) and asserts index.ts registers each with `consent:`, brace-matching the option literal, with a falsifying control that a registration lacking it is rejected. A source scan rather than a required constructor dep: ~40 route suites build their own Fastify app with a hand-written option literal, so the compile-time version is a 40-file edit whose only effect on those suites is a stub, and a stub is not evidence about production wiring. scribe-amend-routes.ts is out of scope BY CONSTRUCTION, not by omission — it declares no consent dep, and its header argues why ($amend requires a signed session, and a signed session is itself evidence consent existed). NARROWED: the sign-surface bullet drops the two clauses that were closed or were never open (the D5 correction, the deliberate 404-before-403 ordering note) and keeps the two that are — the mute client on replay, and the non-atomic sign.
